summary: Part 1 of the blueprint of Endoscopic transfer and unitary trace comparison: the local and global theory of stable conjugacy and endoscopy (ET.0), transfer factors and the harmonic analysis of orbital integrals (ET.1), the geometry of the Hitchin fibration behind Ngô's proof (ET.2b), and the fundamental lemma with the existence of transfer (ET.3). ET.0 plans crossed-module and abelianized Galois cohomology, Kneser and Hasse principles, Tate–Nakayama for tori and complexes, Kottwitz's map and sign, rational classes in stable classes, the global obstruction, endoscopic and twisted endoscopic data with z-pairs and norms, the elliptic endoscopic data of the unitary similitude groups of Shin and Caraiani–Scholze, and Leslie's unitary Hermitian computations. ET.1 plans the conventions, Lie-algebra version and descent of orbital integrals (the group orbital integral and the real pseudo-coefficients are imported from AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.6), κ- and stable orbital integrals, a-data and χ-data, the Langlands–Shelstad factors with the corrected Kottwitz–Shelstad conventions, twisted and Lie-algebra factors, matching functions, Shalika germs and Fourier transforms, the unitary factor, real characters, real transfer, Euler–Poincaré packet averages and their transfer. ET.2b plans the Chevalley quotient, Kostant section and regular centralizer, the Hitchin stack (importing Bun_G from GlobalShtukas GS.0), Schiffmann's boundedness, cameral covers, the Picard action, the anisotropic locus, affine Springer fibres (in the affine Grassmannian of GS.1), the product formula, δ-stratification, weak abelian fibrations, the κ-decomposition, Ngô's support theorem, the geometric stabilization and the point count. ET.3 plans Ngô's Lie-algebra fundamental lemma, Laumon–Ngô's unitary case, the non-standard fundamental lemma, Waldspurger's change of characteristic, the group fundamental lemma, local transfer, inner-form transfer for GL_n, stable base change, the twisted fundamental lemma and transfer, and the global almost-all-places statement. ET.2, ET.2a and its two sub-layers are dropped by the accepted restructuring RS-19 and recorded as closed with their suppliers.

nodes.title: Galois cohomology with coefficients in a crossed module
nodes.statement: Let Γ be a profinite group and ∂ : H̃ → H a crossed module of discrete groups (H acting on H̃ by automorphisms, ∂(h·x) = h ∂(x) h⁻¹ and ∂(x)·y = x y x⁻¹) on which Γ acts continuously and compatibly (σ(h·x) = σ(h)·σ(x), ∂∘σ = σ∘∂). Define pointed sets H^{-1}(Γ, H̃→H) = ker(∂)^Γ, H^0(Γ, H̃→H) and H^1(Γ, H̃→H) as the cohomology of the crossed module in the sense of Borovoi (equivalently of the two-term complex with H̃ in degree −1 and H in degree 0): a 0-cocycle is a pair (h, u) with h ∈ H and u : Γ → H̃ continuous with ∂(u_σ) = h⁻¹σ(h) and u_{στ} = u_σ·σ(u_τ) twisted by h; a 1-cocycle is a pair (u, h) with u : Γ×Γ → H̃ and h : Γ → H continuous satisfying the crossed-module cocycle identities; coboundaries are given by the actions of H and of maps Γ → H̃. For a crossed module 𝓗̃ → 𝓗 of smooth affine group schemes over a field F of characteristic 0, H^i(F, 𝓗̃→𝓗) := H^i(Γ_F, 𝓗̃(F̄) → 𝓗(F̄)) for i = −1, 0, 1. The case H̃ = 1 is nonabelian Galois cohomology, planned here: H^0(Γ, H) = H^Γ and H^1(Γ, H) the pointed set of continuous 1-cocycles a (a_{στ} = a_σ σ(a_τ)) modulo a ~ b iff b_σ = c⁻¹ a_σ σ(c), functorial in Γ (inflation, restriction) and in H, with twisting (for a cocycle a, the twisted group _aH and the bijection H^1(Γ, _aH) → H^1(Γ, H), b ↦ ba) and, for a normal subgroup H′ ⊆ H, the exact sequence of pointed sets up to H^1(H/H′) whose fibres over H^1(H/H′) are orbits of (H/H′)^Γ. They satisfy: (1) H^i(Γ, 1→H) = H^i(Γ, H) for i = 0, 1; (2) a morphism of crossed modules inducing isomorphisms on ker ∂ and on coker ∂ induces bijections on H^{-1}, H^0, H^1 (quasi-isomorphism invariance); (3) for H̃ ⊆ H a normal subgroup with ∂ the inclusion, H^i(Γ, H̃→H) = H^i(Γ, H/H̃) for i = 0, 1; (4) there is an exact sequence of pointed sets H^{-1}(H̃→H) → H^0(H̃) → H^0(H) → H^0(H̃→H) → H^1(H̃) → H^1(H) → H^1(H̃→H), with the usual meaning of exactness at the nonabelian terms; (5) if the crossed module is braided, for instance quasi-isomorphic compatibly with Γ to a two-term complex of commutative groups (as [G_sc → G] and [Z(G_sc) → Z(G)] are for G connected reductive, by Borovoi), the pointed sets H^0 and H^1 carry a canonical abelian group structure, functorial for morphisms of such crossed modules. The kernel of a crossed module is always central in H̃, and an abelian cokernel does not suffice: for ∂ = 1 : ℤ/3 → ℤ/2 with ℤ/2 acting by inversion and Γ = ℤ/3 acting trivially, H^0 ≅ ℤ/3 ⋊ ℤ/2 is nonabelian.
hypotheses: Γ profinite acting continuously on discrete groups
the action is compatible with the crossed-module structure
proofSteps: Define the cocycle and coboundary relations as in Labesse §1.2 (crossed sets) or Borovoi §3 (summarised in Kisin (3.2.7)); the relations are equivalence relations by direct computation (Labesse Lemme 1.2.1).

Item (1) and nonabelian H^1: with H̃ = 1 the definitions collapse to Γ-invariants and to nonabelian H^1 (Labesse §1.3; Serre's twisting argument). AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty:NC.3/nonabelian-h1 plans the same object for topological groups, but NC.3 is in a higher upstream tier and lies downstream of this stage in the atlas, so the notion moves down: it is planned here and the restructure proposal has NC.3 import it.

Item (2): a quasi-isomorphism of crossed modules induces a bijection on cohomology (Labesse Proposition 1.2.2), by comparing cocycles through the long exact sequence and the five lemma for pointed sets with group actions.
Item (4): the connecting maps are constructed exactly as for a short exact sequence of groups; exactness is checked on cocycles (Kisin (3.2.7)(3), Borovoi Corollary 3.4.3).

Item (5): the braiding gives a symmetric product on cocycles; for [G_sc → G], Borovoi's group law is transported through the quasi-isomorphism to the two-term complex of tori (ET.0/abelianized-cohomology). Kisin's (3.2.7)(4) asserts an abelian structure whenever the cokernel is abelian; the confirmed erratum PAPER-KISIN-17/E41 corrects it to braided crossed modules, and every crossed module this roadmap uses is braided.
acceptance: With H̃ = 1 the construction reproduces the nonabelian H^0 and H^1 of AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty:NC.3.
For [SL_2 → GL_2] over a characteristic-0 field, H^0 ≅ F^× via the determinant and H^1 = 0.
The seven-term sequence is exact for [G_sc → G] with G = PGL_2 over ℝ.

sources.match: Labesse defines crossed sets and crossed modules with a Γ-action, their 0- and 1-cohomology, and proves that a quasi-isomorphism of crossed sets induces an isomorphism in cohomology (Proposition 1.2.2).
Kisin recalls Borovoi's pointed sets H^i(Δ, H̃→H) for i = −1, 0, 1 with the four listed properties, which this node states.

nodes.title: Abelianized Galois cohomology of a connected reductive group
nodes.statement: Let F be a field of characteristic 0 and G a connected reductive group over F, ρ : G_sc → G_der ⊆ G the simply connected cover of its derived group, T ⊆ G a maximal torus, T_sc = ρ⁻¹(T), Z = Z(G) and Z_sc = Z(G_sc). The crossed module [G_sc → G] (G acting on G_sc by conjugation through the isogeny) is quasi-isomorphic to the complexes of tori and groups of multiplicative type [T_sc → T] and [Z_sc → Z] (in degrees −1 and 0). Define H^i_ab(F, G) := H^i(F, G_sc → G) for i = 0, 1, an abelian group by ET.0/crossed-module-galois-cohomology (5), canonically isomorphic to the hypercohomology H^i(F, T_sc → T) and to H^i(F, Z_sc → Z); these identifications are independent of T and functorial in G for normal homomorphisms. The abelianization maps are ab^0 : G(F) = H^0(F, G) → H^0_ab(F, G) and ab^1 : H^1(F, G) → H^1_ab(F, G), induced by [1 → G] → [G_sc → G]; they fit into the exact sequence G_sc(F) → G(F) → H^0_ab(F, G) → H^1(F, G_sc) → H^1(F, G) → H^1_ab(F, G). For an inner form G′ of G, H^i_ab(F, G′) = H^i_ab(F, G) canonically (the centre complex does not change). For a global field F, the adelic groups H^i_ab(𝔸_F, G) are the restricted products of the local ones, and H^1_ab(𝔸_F/F, G) is the global-mod-local abelianized cohomology of Labesse §1.6, defined through the quasi-toric crossed set attached to [G_sc → G] with adelic-modulo-rational coefficients (for a torus T it is Kottwitz's H^1(𝔸_F/F, T) of ET.0/tate-nakayama-tori (b)); the sequence ker^1(F, G) → H^1(F, G) → H^1(𝔸_F, G) → H^1_ab(𝔸_F/F, G) is exact (Labesse Proposition 1.6.12). It receives the cokernel of the localization H^1_ab(F, G) → H^1_ab(𝔸_F, G) but differs from it in general (for a torus T by ker^2(F, T)).
hypotheses: F of characteristic 0
G connected reductive (Labesse also allows quasi-connected groups: kernels of a surjection from a connected reductive group onto a torus)
proofSteps: Quasi-isomorphism: T_sc → T and Z_sc → Z map to G_sc → G with the same kernel (the finite group Z_sc ∩ ker ρ) and the same cokernel G/ρ(G_sc) = G_ab; apply ET.0/crossed-module-galois-cohomology (2) (Labesse Lemme 1.6.1, which proves that [Z_sc → Z] → [T_sc → T] → [G_sc → G] are quasi-isomorphisms, and Lemmes 1.6.2–1.6.3; Borovoi's comparison, extraction item PAPER-KISIN-17/H05).
Independence of T: two maximal tori are conjugate over F̄ and the induced isomorphisms of hypercohomology are canonical (inner automorphisms act trivially on the centre complex).
Exact sequence: specialise the seven-term sequence of the crossed module (ET.0/crossed-module-galois-cohomology (4)) to [G_sc → G].
Inner forms: an inner twist does not change [Z_sc → Z] with its Galois action (Labesse Lemme 1.6.2).

Adelic and global-mod-local groups: restricted products of the local hypercohomology groups, using that for almost all places the torus complexes are unramified and the local groups are trivial on integral classes (Labesse §1.4, §1.6, Proposition 1.6.8; the global-mod-local group after Corollaire 1.6.11, p. 34, and its exact sequence, Proposition 1.6.12, p. 35).
acceptance: For a torus T, H^i_ab(F, T) = H^i(F, T); for simply connected semisimple G, H^i_ab(F, G) = 0.
For GL_n, ab^0 = det : GL_n(F) → F^× and H^1_ab = 0.
For PGL_2 over ℝ, H^1_ab = ℤ/2, matching the two real forms.

sources.locator: §1.6, Lemmes 1.6.1–1.6.3 and Proposition 1.6.8, pp. 28–33; the definition of H^i_ab(𝔸_F/F, G) after Corollaire 1.6.11 (p. 34) and Proposition 1.6.12 (p. 35)
sources.match: Labesse defines the abelianized cohomology of a (quasi-)connected reductive group through the crossed module G_sc → G, proves its invariance under inner forms and the quasi-isomorphism with torus complexes, including the adelic version, and the exact sequence ker^1(F, G) → H^1(F, G) → H^1(𝔸_F, G) → H^1_ab(𝔸_F/F, G) (Proposition 1.6.12).

Borovoi's cohomology of crossed modules, which Kisin applies to [G̃ → G] for reductive G (extraction item PAPER-KISIN-17/H05); the quasi-isomorphisms with [T_sc → T] and [Z_sc → Z] are Borovoi's and Labesse's, not restated in Kisin §3.2.7.
Uses H^0_ab(ℚ, G) = H^0(ℚ, Z(G_sc) → Z(G)) and the map ab^0, with the crossed-module comparison (extraction item PAPER-VANHOFTEN-24/E01).

H^1_ab(F, G) is identified with π_0(Z(Ĝ)^Γ)^D
C(T_δ/F) = ker(H^1(F, T_δ) → H^1_ab(F, U(V)))

nodes.title: Kneser, Hasse principle and the abelianization comparisons
nodes.statement: Let G be connected reductive over a field F of characteristic 0. (a) (Kneser; imported from AdelicAlgebraicGroups:AA.4/kneser-local-torsor) If F is nonarchimedean local and G is semisimple simply connected, H^1(F, G) = 1. (b) If F is nonarchimedean local, ab^1 : H^1(F, G) → H^1_ab(F, G) is bijective and ab^0 : G(F) → H^0_ab(F, G) is surjective; if F is archimedean or global, ab^1 is surjective. (c) (Kneser–Harder–Chernousov) If F is a number field and G is semisimple simply connected, H^1(F, G) → ∏_{v real} H^1(F_v, G) is bijective. (d) For F a number field, the square formed by H^1(F, G) → H^1_ab(F, G) and the localization to the archimedean places, H^1(F, G) → H^1(F_∞, G) → H^1_ab(F_∞, G), is cartesian and all four arrows are surjective; consequently ker^1(F, G) := ker(H^1(F, G) → ∏_v H^1(F_v, G)) maps bijectively to its abelianized analogue ker^1_ab(F, G), and for an inner form G′ of G the natural map ker^1_ab(F, G′) → ker^1_ab(F, G) is an isomorphism, so that ker^1(F, G′) and ker^1(F, G) are in canonical bijection. (e) For F a number field and a finite subset of H^1(F, G), there is a maximal F-torus T ⊆ G such that the subset lies in the image of H^1(F, T) → H^1(F, G). (f) For F a number field and G adjoint, H^1(F, G) → ∏_v H^1(F_v, G) is injective; hence an inner form of a connected reductive group over F is determined up to isomorphism by its localizations. (g) (Serre) If F = ℝ and G(ℝ) is compact, H^1(ℝ, G) is in bijection with the G(ℝ)-conjugacy classes of elements of order dividing 2 in G(ℝ), functorially in G; and for a connected reductive subgroup H′ ⊆ H over ℝ with H_ad(ℝ) compact and H′ containing the maximal ℝ-split central torus of H, ker(H^1(ℝ, H′) → H^1(ℝ, H)) is trivial.
hypotheses: F of characteristic 0
G connected reductive
for (a): F nonarchimedean local and G simply connected; for (c): G simply connected; for (f): G adjoint
proofSteps: (a) Kneser's theorem is imported from AdelicAlgebraicGroups:AA.4/kneser-local-torsor, which states it for torsors (every torsor under a semisimple simply connected group over a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic 0 is trivial); for smooth affine groups over a field of characteristic 0, torsors are classified by Galois H^1. Labesse Théorème 1.6.6 states the same, citing Kneser. ReductiveGroupsPartII supplies the vanishing over the completed maximal unramified extension (RG2.1/steinberg-quasi-split), the starting point of the Bruhat–Tits proof.

(b) Use the exact sequence of ET.0/abelianized-cohomology: by (a) the term H^1(F, G_sc) vanishes, giving injectivity of ab^1 and surjectivity of ab^0; surjectivity of ab^1 uses a fundamental (elliptic) maximal torus T, for which H^1(F, T) → H^1_ab(F, G) is onto (Labesse Lemme 1.6.5, Proposition 1.6.7; Borovoi Proposition 5.1, Theorems 5.4 and 5.7). Over a number field the surjectivity is Borovoi's Theorem 5.7.

(c) The Hasse principle for simply connected groups is imported (AdelicAlgebraicGroups:AA.4/hasse-principle-simply-connected) in the form: an F-torsor under G is trivial iff it is trivial at every place; with (a) at the finite places this gives the bijectivity onto the real places (Labesse Théorème 1.6.9).

(d) Combine (b) and (c) with the density of the image of H^0_ab(F, G) in H^0_ab(F_∞, G), proved by dévissage to a complex of tori [T_2 → T_1] with T_1 induced (Labesse Théorème 1.6.10, which states the cartesian square with H^1(𝔸_F, G) and reduces to F_∞ by (b) at the finite places, and Corollaire 1.6.11; Borovoi's theorem, recalled by Kisin as Theorem (3.4.6), who cites it as [Bo, Thm. 5.12]).
(e) Borovoi Theorem 5.11 as used in Kisin §4.4.7 (item PAPER-KISIN-17/H10): choose a maximal torus meeting each class at every place of a finite set and use (d).

(f) The Hasse principle for adjoint groups is used by Kisin (§4.3.1, proof of Corollary 4.6.5) as a known result; by Kottwitz's duality (ET.0/kottwitz-duality (b), whose proof does not use (f)) it amounts to ker^1(F, Z(Ĝ)) = 0 for the finite Galois module Z(Ĝ) when Ĝ is simply connected. Its proof (Platonov–Rapinchuk, Chapter 6) was not read for this plan and is recorded as a gap; inner forms of a reductive group are classified by H^1(F, G_ad) (ET.0/inner-twist), which gives the consequence.
(g) Serre, Galois Cohomology III §4.5, Theorem 6 (recalled by Kisin, proof of Lemma 4.4.5) for compact G(ℝ); the injectivity statement is Kisin Lemma 4.4.5 (item PAPER-KISIN-17/H09).
acceptance: For G = SL_2 over a p-adic field, H^1(F, SL_2) = 1, while H^1(F, PGL_2) = H^1_ab(F, PGL_2) = ℤ/2 classifies the split and the quaternion forms.
For G = SL_1(D) with D a quaternion division algebra over ℚ ramified at ∞ and one prime, (c) identifies H^1(ℚ, G) with H^1(ℝ, G), which has two elements.
For G = SO(3) over ℝ (compact), (g) gives H^1(ℝ, G) of cardinality 2: the identity and the class of rotations by π.

sources.locator: Théorème 1.6.6 (p. 31), Proposition 1.6.7 (pp. 31–32), Théorème 1.6.9 and Théorème 1.6.10 (p. 33), Corollaire 1.6.11 (p. 34)

sources.locator: Theorem (3.4.6), p. 46; the remark after (4.3.1)(iv), p. 75; §§4.4.1–4.4.9 with Lemma (4.4.5) and its proof, p. 81; proof of Proposition (3.4.11), pp. 47–48
sources.match: The global–real abelianization square (item H06), Borovoi's lifting through a torus (H10), the adjoint Hasse principle (§4.3.1), Serre's description of real H¹ of compact groups and the injectivity lemma (H09), and Kneser's vanishing as used in Kisin's proofs.

nodes.title: Degree-zero abelianization and positive rational images
nodes.statement: Let G be a connected reductive group over ℚ with ρ : G_sc → G. (a) H^0_ab(ℚ, G) = H^0(ℚ, Z(G_sc) → Z(G)) and the sequence G_sc(ℚ) → G(ℚ) → H^0_ab(ℚ, G) → H^1(ℚ, G_sc) is exact, so the kernel of ab^0 on G(ℚ) is ρ(G_sc(ℚ)); the same holds over ℝ and over every ℚ_ℓ. (b) Assume the Hasse principle for G_sc, i.e. ker(H^1(ℚ, G_sc) → H^1(ℝ, G_sc)) = 1 (true by ET.0/abelianization-theorems (c)). Let G(ℝ)_+ be the inverse image in G(ℝ) of the identity component (for the real topology) of G_ad(ℝ), so that G(ℝ)_+ = Z(G)(ℝ)·ρ(G_sc(ℝ)), and G(ℚ)_+ = G(ℚ) ∩ G(ℝ)_+ (van Hoften's convention, §3.4; it is not the identity component of G(ℝ), which Kisin (3.4.7) uses: for G = G_m it is ℝ^×, not ℝ_{>0}). Then G(ℚ)_+/ρ(G_sc(ℚ)) is identified by ab^0 with the inverse image of ab^0(Z(G)(ℝ)) under H^0_ab(ℚ, G) → H^0_ab(ℝ, G). (c) If G and H are inner forms over ℚ, with identifications away from p, G(𝔸_f^p) ≅ H(𝔸_f^p), compatible with a fixed global inner twisting on the centre complex [Z(G_sc) → Z(G)], then their positive rational images agree in G(𝔸_f^p)/ρ(G_sc(𝔸_f^p)) × (π_1(G)_I)^σ, the second factor being the Frobenius-invariant part of the inertia coinvariants of the algebraic fundamental group at p.
hypotheses: G connected reductive over ℚ
for (b): the Hasse principle for G_sc (a theorem by ET.0/abelianization-theorems (c))
for (c): G and H inner forms with compatible identifications away from p
proofSteps: (a) Exactness is the degree-zero part of the exact sequence of ET.0/abelianized-cohomology; the centre complex computes H^0_ab by the quasi-isomorphism there (van Hoften §§4.3.12–4.3.13, after Borovoi).

(b) An element g ∈ G(ℚ) with ab^0(g) in ab^0(Z(G)(ℝ)) satisfies g = z·ρ(h) with z ∈ Z(G)(ℝ), h ∈ G_sc(ℝ) in G(ℝ), so g ∈ G(ℝ)_+ (G_sc(ℝ) is connected); conversely, an element of H^0_ab(ℚ, G) with real image in ab^0(Z(G)(ℝ)) maps to a class of H^1(ℚ, G_sc) trivial at ∞, hence trivial by the Hasse principle, so it comes from G(ℚ) (van Hoften Lemma 4.3.14, Corollary 4.3.15).

(c) The inner twisting does not change the centre complex, so H^0_ab(ℚ, G) = H^0_ab(ℚ, H) compatibly with the local maps; apply (b) to both groups and compare images through the away-from-p identifications and the Kottwitz map at p (van Hoften Proposition 4.3.13; the compatibility is made explicit in extraction item E04).
acceptance: For G = GL_2 over ℚ: H^0_ab(ℚ, GL_2) = ℚ^× via det, G(ℚ)_+ is the set of rational matrices of positive determinant, and (b) identifies G(ℚ)_+/SL_2(ℚ) with ℚ_{>0}.
For G = SL_2 (simply connected) both sides of (b) are trivial.
For G = G_m: G(ℝ)_+ = ℝ^× and G(ℚ)_+ = ℚ^×, and (b) holds since ab^0(Z(G)(ℝ)) = ℝ^×; with the identity component ℝ_{>0} of G(ℝ) in place of G(ℝ)_+ the identification in (b) would fail.

sources.locator: arXiv v4: §4.3.12 (pp. 56–57), Proposition 4.3.13 (p. 57, proof p. 58), Lemma 4.3.14 and Corollary 4.3.15 (p. 57); §3.4 (p. 40) for G(ℝ)_+ and G(ℚ)_+
sources.match: Degree-zero abelianized cohomology through the centre complex, its exact sequence with kernel ρ(G_sc(ℚ)), the real-positive criterion and the comparison of positive images of inner forms (extraction items E01–E04).

nodes.title: Tate–Nakayama isomorphisms for tori
nodes.statement: Let S be a torus over a field F of characteristic 0, split by a finite Galois extension E/F with group Γ_{E/F}, and X_*(S) its cocharacter module. (a) (Local) If F is local and u_{E/F} ∈ H^2(Γ_{E/F}, E^×) is the local fundamental class, cup product with u_{E/F} gives isomorphisms Ĥ^i(Γ_{E/F}, X_*(S)) → Ĥ^{i+2}(Γ_{E/F}, S(E)) of Tate cohomology groups for every integer i, using S(E) = X_*(S) ⊗ E^×. In particular H^1(F, S) ≅ Ĥ^{-1}(Γ_{E/F}, X_*(S)) = (X_*(S)_Γ)_tors (the inflation H^1(Γ_{E/F}, S(E)) → H^1(F, S) being an isomorphism by Hilbert 90 for split tori), and H^2(Γ_{E/F}, S(E)) ≅ X_*(S)^Γ/N X_*(S), with inflation H^2(Γ_{E/F}, S(E)) → H^2(F, S) injective; if S is anisotropic then H^2(F, S) = 0. The isomorphisms are compatible with restriction and corestriction, and with inflation in a tower E ⊆ E′ only after multiplying by the degree [E′ : E]. (b) (Global) If F is a number field and C_E the idele class group, cup product with the global fundamental class gives Ĥ^i(Γ_{E/F}, X_*(S)) ≅ Ĥ^{i+2}(Γ_{E/F}, X_*(S) ⊗ C_E); in degree −1 this identifies Kottwitz's global-mod-local group H^1(𝔸_F/F, S) := H^1(Γ_F, S(𝔸_F̄)/S(F̄)) = H^1(Γ_{E/F}, X_*(S) ⊗ C_E) with (X_*(S)_Γ)_tors (it contains the cokernel of H^1(F, S) → H^1(𝔸_F, S), with quotient ker^2(F, S)) and, dually, gives ker^1(F, S) ≅ ker^1(F, Ŝ)^D. (c) The same holds for two-term complexes of tori [S_1 → S_2] with finite kernel (hypercohomology in place of cohomology and the cone of X_*(S_1) → X_*(S_2)), compatibly with the long exact sequences, with norm and restriction maps and with central isogenies. The sign convention: some authors (e.g. Kaletha in the proof of Theorem 4.8) use λ ↦ λ ∪ c^{-1}, the negative of the isomorphism above; each consumer records which one it uses.
hypotheses: F of characteristic 0 local (finite extension of ℚ_p, or ℝ, or ℂ) for (a), a number field for (b)
S a torus split by the finite Galois extension E/F
proofSteps: Nakayama's generalization of Tate's theorem: for a finite group Γ, a class formation module C with fundamental class u and a ℤ-free (hence Tor-free) Γ-module M, cup product with u is an isomorphism Ĥ^i(Γ, M) → Ĥ^{i+2}(Γ, M ⊗ C). The case M = ℤ is the upstream ClassFieldTheory Layer 3 theorem (tateTheorem); the general case follows from it by the cup-product criterion applied to M ⊗ C with M ℤ-free (the generalization the upstream §2.4 asks for in the generic Tate-cohomology supplier). Apply it with M = X_*(S) and C = E^× (local, upstream ClassFieldTheory Layer 6) or C = C_E (global, Layer 11).

Identify S(E) = X_*(S) ⊗ E^× as Γ-modules, so Ĥ^{i+2}(Γ_{E/F}, S(E)) is Galois cohomology of the torus; Hilbert 90 for split tori (upstream ProfiniteCohomology Layer 9) gives the inflation statements in degree 1, and the injectivity in degree 2.
Anisotropic vanishing: X_*(S)^Γ = 0 gives Ĥ^0 = 0, so H^2(Γ_{E/F}, S(E)) = 0 for every splitting E, and H^2(F, S) is the colimit (Kaletha, Corollary 3.7(1)).

Compatibilities: restriction and corestriction commute with cup products by the projection formula; inflation multiplies the fundamental class by the degree (upstream ClassFieldTheory Layer 3, scaled inflation).

Global duality: Poitou–Tate for tori in the form ker^1(F, S) ≅ ker^1(F, Ŝ)^D follows from (b) by comparing with the local statements (Kottwitz 1984 §4; recalled in Labesse Proposition 1.7.3 for the centre complex).
Complexes: use the long exact sequences of hypercohomology and the five lemma (Labesse §1.7, 'Tate–Nakayama pour les complexes de tores').
acceptance: For S = G_m: (X_*(S)_Γ)_tors = 0 and H^1(F, G_m) = 0 (Hilbert 90).
For S = R^1_{E/F} G_m the norm-one torus of a quadratic E/F: X_*(S) = ℤ with the nontrivial element acting by −1, (X_*(S)_Γ)_tors = ℤ/2 and H^1(F, S) = F^×/N E^× ≅ ℤ/2 for F local nonarchimedean.
For S = R_{E/F} G_m: X_*(S) is induced, Ĥ^i vanishes and H^1(F, S) = 0 (Shapiro and Hilbert 90).

sources.locator: arXiv v5: §4 introduction; Theorem 4.8 (p. 24) and its proof (p. 25); Corollary 3.7 (p. 14); §5.3 (p. 33)
sources.match: The ordinary Tate–Nakayama isomorphism (X_*(S)_Γ)_tors → H^1(F, S) and its all-degree form, the scaled inflation, injectivity of inflation in degree 2 and the anisotropic vanishing (extraction items P12, P29).
Labesse applies the Tate–Nakayama isomorphism for complexes of tori to the centre complex, and proves H^2(F, T) = 0 for an anisotropic torus over a local field (Lemme 1.5.1).
Kottwitz's construction of α_G starts from the Tate–Nakayama isomorphism for tori, recorded as the case G = T of Theorem 1.2.

nodes.title: Kottwitz's map and the duality for reductive groups
nodes.statement: Let F be a field of characteristic 0 and G connected reductive over F, with dual group Ĝ (complex), its centre Z(Ĝ) with the Galois action of ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.5/galois-action-on-dual-group, and A(G) := π_0(Z(Ĝ)^Γ)^D (Pontryagin dual). (a) (Local) If F is local there is a unique extension of the Tate–Nakayama isomorphisms for tori to a morphism of functors α_G : H^1(F, G) → A(G) on the category of connected reductive groups and normal homomorphisms (Kottwitz 1986, Theorem 1.2). It factors through ab^1 and an injective homomorphism H^1_ab(F, G) → A(G). If F is nonarchimedean, α_G is a bijection; the group structure it induces on H^1(F, G) is Kottwitz's. If F = ℝ, the fibre of α_G over 0 is the image of H^1(ℝ, G_sc), and the image of α_G is the annihilator of the image of the norm N_{ℂ/ℝ} on Z(Ĝ); α_G is not bijective in general and H^1(ℝ, G) is not a group. For a maximal torus S ⊆ G, α_G restricted along H^1(F, S) → H^1(F, G) is α_S followed by the restriction A(S) → A(G) dual to π_0(Z(Ĝ)^Γ) → π_0(Ŝ^Γ); a class of H^1(F, S) comes from H^1(F, G_sc) exactly when α_S of it annihilates the image of π_0(Z(Ĝ)^Γ) → π_0(Ŝ^Γ). Equivalently, via ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.5/dual-centre-and-fundamental-group, for F nonarchimedean H^1(F, G) ≅ (π_1(G)_Γ)_tors. (b) (Global) If F is a number field, H^1_ab(𝔸_F/F, G) ≅ A(G) canonically; ker^1(F, G) = ker^1_ab(F, G) ≅ ker^1(F, Z(Ĝ))^D. Kottwitz's Tamagawa-number formula τ(G) = #π_0(Z(Ĝ)^Γ)/#ker^1(F, Z(Ĝ)) is not part of this node.
hypotheses: F of characteristic 0, local for (a), a number field for (b)
G connected reductive
proofSteps: (a) For a torus define α_S by Tate–Nakayama (ET.0/tate-nakayama-tori (a), degree −1). For general G use a z-extension (ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.1/z-extension-existence) to reduce to G with simply connected derived group, then use the exact sequence H^1(F, G_sc) → H^1(F, G) → H^1(F, D) with D = G/G_der a torus and Kneser's vanishing (ET.0/abelianization-theorems (a)) in the p-adic case; uniqueness follows from the existence of fundamental tori (Kottwitz 1986, Theorem 1.2 and its proof; Labesse Proposition 1.7.3).

Injectivity on H^1_ab and bijectivity for nonarchimedean F: Labesse Proposition 1.7.3 via the quasi-isomorphism [Z(Ĝ) → 1] ≃ [Ĝ → Ĝ_sc]-dual of the centre complex and the Tate–Nakayama isomorphism for complexes of tori; the limit over cofinal splitting fields gives bijectivity.
Real case: describe H^1(ℝ, G) through fundamental tori (Kaletha, extraction item P28; Kottwitz 1986 Theorem 1.2).

(b) Global: Labesse Proposition 1.7.3 (global part), from the global Tate–Nakayama isomorphism for the centre complex (ET.0/tate-nakayama-tori (b), (c)) and the cofinality of splitting fields; ker^1(F, G) = ker^1_ab(F, G) is ET.0/abelianization-theorems (d).
acceptance: For G = PGL_2 over a p-adic field: Ĝ = SL_2(ℂ), Z(Ĝ) = μ_2, A(G) = ℤ/2 and H^1(F, PGL_2) has two elements (split and quaternion forms).
For G = SL_2: Z(Ĝ) = {1} for Ĝ = PGL_2(ℂ), so A(G) = 0, matching Kneser's vanishing.
For G = U(1) over ℝ attached to ℂ/ℝ: α_G is a bijection H^1(ℝ, U(1)) = ℤ/2 ≅ A(G).

For G = SU(2) compact over ℝ: H^1(ℝ, G) has two elements (identity and −1 up to conjugacy, ET.0/abelianization-theorems (g)) while A(G) = π_0(Z(Ĝ)^Γ)^D for Ĝ = PGL_2(ℂ) is trivial, so α_G is not injective over ℝ.

sources.match: Kottwitz's theorem: a unique extension of the Tate–Nakayama map to a morphism of functors H^1(F, G) → π_0(Z(Ĝ)^Γ)^D, bijective for p-adic F; §2 gives the global cohomological results.
H^1_ab(F, G) injects into A(G), bijectively for nonarchimedean F; H^1_ab(𝔸_F/F, G) ≅ A(G) and ker^1(F, G) = ker^1_ab(F, G) = ker^1(F, Z(Ĝ))^D globally.

sources.locator: arXiv v5: Kottwitz's Theorem 1.2 as used in Corollary 3.8 (p. 15), Lemma 4.9 (p. 25), §4.7, Corollary 5.4 and Lemma 5.7 (extraction item P28)
sources.match: The real-place description of α_G (fibre over 0, image) and the criterion for a torus class to come from G_sc.

nodes.title: The Kottwitz sign of an inner form
nodes.statement: Let F be a local field of characteristic 0, G* a quasi-split connected reductive group over F and G an inner form of G*. The Kottwitz sign is e(G) = (−1)^{q(G*) − q(G)} ∈ {±1}, where q denotes the F-rank of the derived group (Kottwitz's definition); it depends only on the class h ∈ H^1(F, G*_ad) of the inner twist, and is the value at h of a map H^1(F, G*_ad) → {±1}. In dual terms (Hansen–Kaletha–Weinstein): if h corresponds under α_{G*_ad} (ET.0/kottwitz-duality) to ν ∈ X^*(Z(Ĝ_sc)^Γ), the dual group of G*_ad being Ĝ_sc, then e(G) = (−1)^{⟨2ρ, ν⟩}, with 2ρ the sum of the positive coroots of Ĝ_sc and the pairing taken modulo 2 after lifting ν to a character of a maximal torus. Properties: e(G*) = 1; e(G) depends only on the isomorphism class of the inner form; for F global and G a connected reductive group over F, ∏_v e(G_{F_v}) = 1.
hypotheses: F local of characteristic 0 (product formula: F global)
G an inner form of the quasi-split group G*
proofSteps: Well definedness: α_{G*_ad} is defined on H^1(F, G*_ad) (ET.0/kottwitz-duality), and ⟨2ρ, ν⟩ mod 2 does not depend on the choice of positive system because two choices differ by the Weyl group, which fixes Z(Ĝ_sc).

Comparison with the F-rank definition: Kottwitz, 'Sign changes in harmonic analysis on reductive groups' (cited by Kottwitz 1986 §5.1 and by Labesse Définition 1.7.1); the dual-group formula is Hansen–Kaletha–Weinstein Lemma A.2.1.

Product formula: the sum over all places of the local invariants of a global class in H^1(F, G_ad) is trivial, which follows from the global duality of ET.0/kottwitz-duality (b) (Labesse Lemme 1.7.2, from Proposition 1.6.12).
acceptance: e(G*) = 1; e(D^×) = −1 for a quaternion division algebra D; e(GL_m(D)) = (−1)^{n−m}.
For the compact unitary group U(n) over ℝ, e = (−1)^{⌊n/2⌋}.
For a quaternion algebra over ℚ, the product of local signs is 1.

sources.match: Definition of the Kottwitz sign of an inner form through H^1(F, G*_ad) → {±1}, and the product formula ∏_v e(G_v) = 1.

sources.locator: arXiv v4, Appendix A.2, Lemma A.2.1 (p. 85)
sources.match: The Kottwitz sign of an inner twist with class corresponding to ν ∈ X^*(Z(Ĝ_sc)^Γ) is (−1)^{⟨2ρ, ν⟩} (extraction item PAPER-HANSEN-KALETHA-WEINSTEIN-22/119).

Kottwitz attaches a sign e(I) = ±1 to every connected reductive group over a local field, referring to his paper on sign changes for the definition, and uses it in the local conjectures on orbital integrals.

uses.how: stable orbital integrals carry the factor e(G_γ) on each rational class
transfer from an inner form to its quasi-split form carries e(G)
the rank-two sign of quaternionic matching

tests.name: kottwitzSign_quasiSplit
tests.statement: e(G*) = 1 for every quasi-split G*.

tests.name: kottwitzSign_quaternion
tests.statement: For D^× with D a quaternion division algebra over a p-adic F, an inner form of GL_2, e(D^×) = −1; more generally e(GL_m(D)) = (−1)^{n − m} for D central division of degree d over F and n = md.

tests.name: kottwitzSign_compact_real
tests.statement: For the compact form U(n) of the quasi-split unitary group over ℝ, e(U(n)) = (−1)^{q(U*(n)) − q(U(n))} = (−1)^{⌊n/2⌋}.

tests.name: kottwitzSign_product

nodes.title: Inner twists and the quasi-split inner form
nodes.statement: Let F be a field of characteristic 0 and G, G′ connected reductive groups over F. An inner twist is an F̄-isomorphism ψ : G_F̄ → G′_F̄ such that ψ⁻¹∘σ(ψ) is an inner automorphism of G_F̄ for every σ ∈ Γ_F; σ ↦ ψ⁻¹∘σ(ψ) is a 1-cocycle with values in G_ad(F̄), and inner twists up to equivalence (ψ ~ Int(g′)∘ψ∘Int(g) with g ∈ G(F̄), g′ ∈ G′(F̄)) are in bijection with H^1(F, G_ad); every class arises. Every G has a unique quasi-split inner form G* up to isomorphism. An inner twist ψ transports: (i) semisimple and strongly regular semisimple elements, and their stable conjugacy classes, from G′(F) to G*(F̄) — a stable class of G′ that is defined over F gives an F-rational stable class of G*; (ii) maximal F-tori: every maximal F-torus T′ ⊆ G′ transfers to G*, i.e. there is an F-torus T* ⊆ G* and g ∈ G*(F̄) with Int(g)∘ψ|_{T′} defined over F (Steinberg and Kottwitz: quasi-split groups contain a transfer of every maximal torus of every inner form). (iii) Centralizers: for γ′ ∈ G′(F) strongly regular with image γ* (rational, by Kottwitz's rationality theorem when G*_der is simply connected, and after a z-extension in general), ψ induces an inner twist of the centralizers G′_{γ′} → G*_{γ*}, an F-isomorphism of tori in the strongly regular case.
hypotheses: F of characteristic 0
G, G′ connected reductive over F
proofSteps: Classification by H^1(F, G_ad): standard twisting (ET.0/crossed-module-galois-cohomology, nonabelian H^1 with twisted coefficients) applied to the automorphism group of G and its inner part G_ad (Labesse Définition 1.7.1 uses this bijection).
Quasi-split inner form: existence and uniqueness via a pinning and the splitting of Aut(G) → Out(G) (upstream ReductiveGroups Layer 7/9 pinnings).

Transfer of tori and of rational stable classes: Steinberg's theorem that a quasi-split group with simply connected derived group has a rational point in every F-rational stable (geometric) semisimple class (cited as Kottwitz 1982, Theorem 4.4 in Labesse's proof of Théorème 2.4.2), reduced to that case by a z-extension (ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.1/z-extension-existence) and Hilbert 90 for the induced central torus.
Centralizers: ψ restricted to the centralizer is defined over F up to an inner automorphism of an abelian group, hence defined over F in the strongly regular case.
acceptance: The inner forms of GL_2 over a p-adic field are GL_2 and D^×, classified by H^1(F, PGL_2) = ℤ/2.
Every maximal torus of D^× transfers to an elliptic maximal torus of GL_2.
Tori have no nontrivial inner twists.

nodes.title: Rational, geometric and stable conjugacy of semisimple elements
nodes.statement: Let F be a field of characteristic 0 and G connected reductive over F. For semisimple δ ∈ G(F) let G_δ be its centralizer and G_δ^0 the identity component; δ is regular if G_δ^0 is a torus and strongly regular if G_δ is abelian (then G_δ = T_δ is a maximal torus). Two semisimple δ, δ′ ∈ G(F) are rationally conjugate if δ′ = g⁻¹δg with g ∈ G(F), geometrically conjugate if this holds with g ∈ G(F̄). Following Labesse, let T_δ be the maximal torus of the centre of the centralizer in G of G_δ^0, and let the stable centralizer I_δ be the subgroup of G_δ generated by G_δ^0 and the δ-invariants (T_δ)^δ; I_δ = G_δ^0 when G_der is simply connected (Steinberg's connectedness theorem) and in the situations of ordinary endoscopy with G_der simply connected and of cyclic base change. Then δ′ is stably conjugate to δ if δ′ = x⁻¹δx with x ∈ G(F̄) and the cocycle a_σ = x σ(x)⁻¹ takes values in I_δ for every σ ∈ Γ_F. For strongly regular δ, stable conjugacy is geometric conjugacy by an element x with x σ(x)⁻¹ ∈ T_δ, i.e. conjugacy over F̄ such that the induced isomorphism T_δ → T_δ′ is defined over F. Stable conjugacy is an equivalence relation on semisimple elements of G(F), coarser than rational and finer than geometric conjugacy. The same definitions apply to the Lie algebra 𝔤(F) (regular semisimple X with centralizer a maximal torus, stable conjugacy by G(F̄) with defined-over-F induced isomorphism) and, with θ-conjugacy x⁻¹δθ(x), to a twisted space L = Gθ (Labesse §2.3, Waldspurger 2008 §3.1).
hypotheses: F of characteristic 0
G connected reductive (for the twisted version, a connected component L of a reductive G⁺ with identity component G having a rational point)
proofSteps: Connectedness: Steinberg's theorem that the fixed points of a semisimple automorphism of a simply connected group are connected gives I_δ = G_δ^0 when G_der is simply connected (Labesse Définition 2.3.1 and the remark following it; Lemme 2.3.3 for base change).

Equivalence relation: the cocycle of a composite is the twisted product of the cocycles, and inverses give inverse cocycles; values stay in I_δ because conjugation by x identifies I_δ with I_δ′ (Labesse Définition 2.3.4).
The Lie algebra version is identical with Ad in place of conjugation (Ngô §1.7 uses stable classes in 𝔤 parametrized by 𝔠(F)).
acceptance: In GL_n stable conjugacy, rational conjugacy and equality of characteristic polynomials agree for semisimple elements.
In SL_2 over a p-adic field a regular elliptic stable class contains two rational classes.
In PGL_2 geometric conjugacy of involutions does not imply stable conjugacy.

nodes.title: Rational classes inside a stable class
nodes.statement: Let F be a field of characteristic 0, G connected reductive over F, δ ∈ G(F) semisimple and I = I_δ its stable centralizer. (a) Sending δ′ = x⁻¹δx (stably conjugate) to the class of σ ↦ x σ(x)⁻¹ gives a bijection between the G(F)-conjugacy classes in the stable class of δ and the image of D(I, G; F) := ker[H^1(F, I) → H^1(F, G)] in ker[H^1(F, G_δ) → H^1(F, G)]; when I = G_δ (e.g. δ strongly regular, or G_der simply connected and G_δ connected) the conjugacy classes are in bijection with D(I, G; F), and the class of (δ, δ′) is denoted inv(δ, δ′). (b) If F is local, D(I, G; F) is finite, and when I = T is a torus it is a finite abelian group; then D(T, G; F) ⊆ E(T, G; F) := ker[H^1(F, T) → H^1_ab(F, G)] = ker[A(T) → A(G)] (Kottwitz's 𝔈(T/F)), with equality if F is nonarchimedean; and via ET.0/tate-nakayama-tori and ET.0/kottwitz-duality, E(T, G; F) is Pontryagin dual to Kottwitz's 𝔎(T/F), the subgroup of π_0((T̂/Z(Ĝ))^Γ) of classes whose image in H^1(F, Z(Ĝ)) is trivial (equivalently the cokernel of π_0(Z(Ĝ)^Γ) → π_0(T̂^Γ)), so that characters κ of E(T, G; F) are given by Γ-invariant elements of T̂/Z(Ĝ) that lift to T̂^Γ, up to the identity component. (c) (Steinberg's relatedness lemma) If F is a p-adic field and δ, δ′ are strongly regular and stably conjugate, they are conjugate over the completed maximal unramified extension F̆, because H^1(F̆, T) = 0. (d) (Rationality) If G is quasi-split and G_der is simply connected, every stable (= geometric) semisimple class of G(F̄) that is stable under Γ_F contains an element of G(F). (e) For a proper Levi subgroup M of G, the rational classes in a stable class of M may differ from those of G: inv is compatible with M ⊆ G through H^1(F, I^M) → H^1(F, I^G).
hypotheses: F of characteristic 0 (local for (b), p-adic for (c))
G connected reductive; for (d): G quasi-split with simply connected derived group
proofSteps: (a) Labesse §2.3 after Définition 2.3.4: the pair (x, a) gives a class in H^0(F, I\G), whose image in H^1(F, I) lies in D(I, G; F); the fibres of H^0(F, I\G) → G(F) are the kernels displayed there, giving the parametrization through the image in ker[H^1(F, G_δ) → H^1(F, G)] (also Kottwitz 1986 Introduction and §4.1).

(b) Finiteness: local H^1 of linear algebraic groups is finite (Kaletha Fact 3.4, citing Platonov–Rapinchuk Theorem 6.14; extraction item P10); E(T, G; F) is the abelianized kernel and the comparison with D uses ET.0/abelianization-theorems (b); the duality with K(T, G; F) is ET.0/tate-nakayama-tori (a) and ET.0/kottwitz-duality (a) (Kottwitz 1986 §§4.4–4.6).

(c) Steinberg: H^1(F̆, T) = 0 for every torus over F̆ (ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.1/steinberg-quasi-split, which states that H^1(L, H) = 1 for connected reductive H over the completed maximal unramified extension); conjugacy over F̄ by x with xσ(x)⁻¹ ∈ T and vanishing of the class over F̆ give conjugacy over F̆ (Hansen–Kaletha–Weinstein Lemma 3.2.1).
(d) Kottwitz 1982 Theorem 4.4 as cited by Labesse in the proof of Théorème 2.4.2; the transfer of tori in ET.0/inner-twist (ii) is the same argument.
(e) Functoriality of H^1 for M ⊆ G; example in the acceptance tests.
acceptance: G = GL_n: D(T, GL_n; F) = 0 for every maximal torus T (Hilbert 90 and Shapiro), so stable = rational conjugacy.
G = SL_2 over p-adic F, T elliptic attached to quadratic E/F: D(T, SL_2; F) = H^1(F, T) = F^×/N E^× ≅ ℤ/2, two rational classes in each regular stable class of T; for T split, D = 0.
Split torus T = G: D(T, T; F) = 0.

Nonsplit unitary group G = U(1, 1) attached to E/F with T ≅ U(1) × U(1) elliptic: H^1(F, T) = (ℤ/2)², H^1_ab(F, G) = ℤ/2 and D(T, G; F) = E(T, G; F) = ker of the sum map, of order 2 (Leslie Lemma 1.8 pattern with S_1 = {1, 2}).

Proper Levi with different rational classes in one stable class: in G = Sp_4 over p-adic F, the Levi M ≅ GL_1 × SL_2 contains elliptic elements of its SL_2 factor whose stable class splits into two M(F)-classes, as for SL_2 above.

sources.match: The stable class of δ is the image of H^0(F, I\G); the rational classes inside it are parametrized by the image of D(I, G; F) = ker[H^1(F, I) → H^1(F, G)]; rational points in rational stable classes of quasi-split groups with simply connected derived group (Kottwitz).

sources.locator: Introduction (p. 366); §4.1–4.6, definitions of 𝔇, 𝔈, 𝔎 (pp. 378–379)

nodes.title: The global obstruction for adelic stable classes
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field and G connected reductive over F with G_der simply connected (the standing assumption of Kottwitz 1986 §6), γ_0 ∈ G(F) semisimple with centralizer I_0 (connected reductive, as G_der is simply connected), and γ = (γ_v)_v ∈ G(𝔸_F) conjugate to γ_0 under G(𝔸_F ⊗_F F̄), so that each γ_v is stably conjugate to γ_0. (Kottwitz allows γ_0 in a quasi-split inner form G_0 of G, transported by an inner twisting ψ : G_0 → G; the case stated here is G_0 = G, the one the product formula (c) uses.) Let inv_v(γ_0, γ_v) ∈ D(I_0, G; F_v) be the local invariants (ET.0/rational-classes-in-stable-class) and α_v their images in A(I_0/F_v) := π_0(Z(Î_0)^{Γ_v})^D. (a) Let 𝔎(I_0/F) be the group of κ ∈ π_0((Z(Î_0)/Z(Ĝ))^Γ) whose image in H^1(F, Z(Ĝ)) is locally trivial; almost all α_v vanish, and obs(γ) ∈ 𝔎(I_0/F)^D is the character κ ↦ ∏_v α_v(κ_v) of the localizations κ_v. (b) If G_sc has no E_8 factor, γ is G(𝔸_F)-conjugate to an element of G(F) stably conjugate to γ_0 if and only if obs(γ) is trivial (Kottwitz 1986, Theorem 6.6; the E_8 restriction comes from the Hasse principle, which is now known for E_8 by Chernousov, so it can be removed). (c) For κ ∈ 𝔎(I_0/F), ⟨obs(γ), κ⟩ = ∏_v ⟨inv_v(γ_0, γ_v), κ_v⟩, the product formula used to stabilize the elliptic terms; the number of G(F)-classes in G(F) ∩ (stable class of γ_0) adelically conjugate to γ is |ker^1(F, I_0)|-weighted as in Kottwitz 1986 §9.
hypotheses: F a number field
G connected reductive with G_der simply connected; for (b) G_sc without E_8 factors (removable by Chernousov's Hasse principle for E_8)
proofSteps: Construct obs_1(γ) first using G_sc(𝔸)-conjugacy and the Hasse principle for G_sc (Kottwitz 1986 §6.1–6.3, Lemma 6.3), then pass to obs(γ) using the global duality ker^1(F, I_0) ≅ ker^1(F, Z(Î_0))^D of ET.0/kottwitz-duality (b) and Tate–Nakayama for the global-mod-local cohomology (ET.0/tate-nakayama-tori (b)).
The criterion (b) is Kottwitz 1986 Theorem 6.6; the Hasse principle input is ET.0/abelianization-theorems (c), which includes E_8 (Labesse Théorème 1.6.9).

The product formula (c): Kottwitz 1986 §6.7 gives obs(γ′) = obs(γ)·inv(γ, γ′) for adelic elements of one geometric class; apply it with γ_0, whose obstruction is trivial, and use the local duality of ET.0/kottwitz-duality (a). Kottwitz's conjecture (6.10.1), which identifies the adelic transfer factor with ⟨obs(γ), κ⟩, is the theorem of Langlands–Shelstad recorded in ET.1/transfer-factor-properties (f).
acceptance: For G = GL_n every adelic element stably conjugate everywhere to γ_0 ∈ GL_n(F) is G(𝔸)-conjugate to γ_0 (obs is trivial because 𝔎(I_0/F) = 1 for centralizers that are products of restrictions of scalars of GL's).

For G = SL_2 and γ_0 regular elliptic with splitting field E: the local invariants lie in ℤ/2 at each place nonsplit in E, and obs(γ) is their sum; an adelic element whose invariants are nontrivial at exactly one place is not conjugate to a rational element.

sources.match: With G_der simply connected and γ_0 in a quasi-split inner form, the obstructions obs_1(γ) and obs(γ) ∈ 𝔎(I_0/F)^D; γ is G(𝔸)-conjugate to a rational element iff obs(γ) is trivial (assuming no E_8 factors); obs(γ′) = obs(γ)·inv(γ, γ′) (§6.7); the conjectural identity (6.10.1) of the adelic transfer factor with ⟨obs(γ), κ⟩.
Shin's Kottwitz triples and the Kottwitz invariant α(γ_0; γ, δ) ∈ 𝔎(I_0/ℚ)^D, which consume this obstruction theory.
The Hasse principle for simply connected groups including type E_8 (Chernousov).

nodes.title: Unramified Galois cohomology of reductive models
nodes.statement: Let G be a connected reductive group over ℚ_p with a reductive model G_{ℤ_p} (smooth affine with connected reductive special fibre), and L = ℚ_p^ur. (a) (Lang) H^1(Gal(L/ℚ_p), G_{ℤ_p}(ℤ_p^ur)) = 1, i.e. every G_{ℤ_p}-torsor over ℤ_p is trivial; the same holds for every smooth affine ℤ_p-group with connected fibres, and over ℤ_ℓ. (b) (Integral z-extensions) A reductive group G_{ℤ_(p)} over ℤ_(p) admits a z-extension G_{1,ℤ_(p)} → G_{ℤ_(p)}: a surjection of reductive ℤ_(p)-groups whose kernel is a central induced torus and with G_1^der simply connected. (c) (Kernel of the Kottwitz homomorphism on unramified points) Let ρ : G̃ → G be the simply connected cover of the derived group and κ̃_G : G(L) → π_1(G) the Kottwitz homomorphism (ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.1/kottwitz-homomorphism, with I acting trivially since G is unramified). Then ρ(G̃(L))·G_{ℤ_p}(ℤ_p^ur) = ker κ̃_G, a normal subgroup; its intersection with G(ℚ_p) is ρ(G̃(ℚ_p))·G_{ℤ_p}(ℤ_p) = ker(κ̃_G|_{G(ℚ_p)}); and a class in G(L)/ρ(G̃(L))G_{ℤ_p}(ℤ_p^ur) whose κ̃_G-image is Frobenius invariant contains an element of G(ℚ_p).
hypotheses: G_{ℤ_p} a reductive model (connected special fibre)
for (b): G_{ℤ_(p)} reductive over ℤ_(p)
proofSteps: (a) Lang's theorem for the connected special fibre (ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.3/lang-theorem) gives a section mod p; smoothness and Hensel's lemma lift it (Kisin footnote 20 and proofs of Proposition 3.6.7, Lemma 3.8.2, extraction item lang-lemma-integral).

(b) Kottwitz's construction of z-extensions over fields (ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.1/z-extension-existence) carried out with an induced torus split over an unramified extension so that it extends to ℤ_(p) (Kisin, proof of Proposition 3.6.10, citing Kottwitz 'Shimura varieties and λ-adic representations' §1; extraction item z-extension-integral).

(c) The Cartan decomposition for the hyperspecial subgroup G_{ℤ_p}(ℤ_p^ur) of G(L) (ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.3/hyperspecial-vertices and RG2.4) shows that G(L) = ⊔ over dominant cocharacters of double cosets, and κ̃_G is the image of the cocharacter in π_1(G); its kernel is generated by ρ(G̃(L)) and the hyperspecial subgroup. Intersecting with G(ℚ_p) uses (a) and Kneser's vanishing (ET.0/abelianization-theorems (a)); the last assertion uses Lang's theorem for the Frobenius-twisted action (Kisin, proof of Lemma 3.6.2(2), extraction item kappa-kernel-unramified-points).
acceptance: For G = GL_n: κ̃_G = val ∘ det, its kernel is SL_n(L)·GL_n(ℤ_p^ur) and the rational points of the kernel are SL_n(ℚ_p)·GL_n(ℤ_p) = {g : val det g = 0}.
For G = G_m: H^1(Gal(L/ℚ_p), ℤ_p^{ur,×}) = 1 (the unit group is cohomologically trivial for unramified extensions).

sources.locator: footnote 20 (p. 54); Proposition (3.6.7) and its proof (p. 56); Proposition (3.6.10) and its proof (p. 58); Lemma (3.6.2) (p. 53) and the Cartan-decomposition step of its proof (p. 54); (3.6.8) (p. 57) and (3.6.9) (p. 58)
sources.match: Lang's lemma for smooth connected integral groups; integral z-extensions; the kernel of κ̃_G on unramified and rational points (extraction items lang-lemma-integral, z-extension-integral, kappa-kernel-unramified-points).

nodes.title: Endoscopic data, twisted endoscopic data and their isomorphisms
nodes.statement: Let F be a local or global field of characteristic 0, W_F its Weil group, G connected reductive over F, θ an F-automorphism of G (quasi-semisimple, i.e. preserving a Borel pair over F̄), ω a character of G(F) (local) or of G(𝔸_F)/G(F) (global) with class a_ω ∈ H^1(W_F, Z(Ĝ)) (Langlands' correspondence for characters, recalled by Waldspurger 2008 §1.3), Ĝ the dual group with a Γ-stable pinning (B̂, T̂, {X_α}) and ^LG = Ĝ ⋊ W_F (ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.5/l-group), θ̂ the dual automorphism of Ĝ preserving the pinning and ^Lθ = θ̂ × id. An endoscopic datum for (G, θ, ω) is a quadruple (H, ℋ, s, ξ) with: (1) H a quasi-split connected reductive group over F; (2) ℋ a split extension of W_F by Ĥ whose induced outer action of W_F on Ĥ is the one given by H; (3) s ∈ Ĝ such that Int(s)∘θ̂ is semisimple; (4) ξ : ℋ → ^LG a continuous injective homomorphism over W_F such that (a) there is a 1-cocycle a : W_F → Z(Ĝ) of class a_ω with s ^Lθ ξ(h) = a(h) ξ(h) s ^Lθ for all h ∈ ℋ, and (b) ξ restricts to an isomorphism of Ĥ onto the identity component Z_Ĝ(s ^Lθ)^0 of the centralizer of s θ̂. Ordinary endoscopic data are the case θ = 1, ω = 1, written (H, ℋ, s, ξ) with s ∈ Ĝ semisimple (Langlands–Shelstad §1.2; for G_der simply connected one may take ℋ = ^LH). An isomorphism (H, ℋ, s, ξ) → (H′, ℋ′, s′, ξ′) is g ∈ Ĝ with g ξ(ℋ) g⁻¹ = ξ′(ℋ′) and g s ^Lθ g⁻¹ ∈ Z(Ĝ) s′ ^Lθ; Out(H, ℋ, s, ξ) is the group of automorphisms modulo ξ(Ĥ). In the ordinary global or local case the datum is elliptic if ξ(Z(Ĥ)^Γ)^0 ⊆ Z(Ĝ); E(G) and E_ell(G) denote sets of representatives of isomorphism classes (resp. elliptic ones); for F local E_ell(G) is finite. Endoscopic triples (H, s, η) (Kottwitz's convention, used by Shin) are the data with ℋ = ^LH and η = ξ|_Ĥ when G_der is simply connected. For a Levi subgroup M ⊆ G with ^LM ⊆ ^LG (ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.5/l-group-levi-embedding), an endoscopic datum (M_H, ℳ, s, ξ_M) for M induces one for G with H ⊇ M_H as a Levi, by taking the centralizer of s in Ĝ.
hypotheses: F local or global of characteristic 0
G connected reductive, θ quasi-semisimple, ω a character
proofSteps: The definition is Waldspurger 2008 §1.3 (twisted, after Kottwitz–Shelstad Chapter 2) specialising to Langlands–Shelstad §1.2 for θ = 1, ω = 1.

Finiteness of E_ell(G) for local F: an elliptic s is determined up to Z(Ĝ) and Ĝ-conjugacy by finitely many choices because Z_Ĝ(s)^0 has semisimple rank at most that of Ĝ and the elliptic condition bounds s modulo Z(Ĝ) to a finite set of torsion classes (Kottwitz 1986 §7, Proposition 7.1–7.5 for the local finiteness results).
Induction from Levi subgroups: Z_Ĝ(s)^0 ⊇ Z_M̂(s)^0 and the Levi embedding of L-groups transports ξ_M (Kottwitz 1986 §7; Waldspurger 2008 §1.3 for the twisted case).
acceptance: E_ell(GL_n) consists of GL_n alone.
E_ell(SL_2) over a p-adic field with p odd consists of SL_2 and the three norm-one tori.
For quasi-split U(n), the data U(n_1) × U(n_2) with s = diag(1, −1) are elliptic.

Standard endoscopic data (H, s, ξ) with ξ an L-homomorphism ^LH → ^LG, and the observation that (H, s⁻¹, ξ) is again endoscopic data (p. 13).
Endoscopic triples (H, s, η) as in Kottwitz's earlier paper, and the local finiteness results.

nodes.title: z-pairs for endoscopic data
nodes.statement: Let (H, ℋ, s, ξ) be an endoscopic datum for (G, θ, ω) over a field F of characteristic 0. A z-pair is a triple (H_1, ξ_1, ξ̂_1) with: (1) H_1 a quasi-split connected reductive group over F with simply connected derived group; (2) ξ_1 : H_1 → H a surjective homomorphism whose kernel Z_1 is a central induced torus (so H_1 → H is a z-extension in the sense of ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.1/z-extension); (3) ξ̂_1 : ℋ → ^LH_1 an injective homomorphism over W_F whose restriction to Ĥ is the dual of ξ_1. Because Z_1 is induced, H_1(F) → H(F) is surjective. The composite W_F → ℋ → ^LH_1 → ^LZ_1 → Ẑ_1 (for any section W_F → ℋ) is a 1-cocycle whose class is independent of the section; it defines a character λ_1 of Z_1(F) (of Z_1(𝔸_F)/Z_1(F) globally). Transfer to H is replaced by transfer to functions on H_1(F) that transform under Z_1(F) by λ_1^{-1}. z-pairs exist for every endoscopic datum (Kottwitz–Shelstad §2.2).
hypotheses: (H, ℋ, s, ξ) an endoscopic datum over F of characteristic 0
proofSteps: Existence: take a z-extension H_1 → H (ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.1/z-extension-existence); since H_1 has simply connected derived group, ℋ embeds into ^LH_1 extending the dual inclusion Ĥ → Ĥ_1 (Langlands' lemma on L-embeddings for groups with simply connected derived group, as used by Kottwitz–Shelstad §2.2; recalled in Waldspurger 2008 §1.4).

Independence of the cocycle class from the section: two sections differ by a cocycle valued in Ĥ, which maps trivially to Ẑ_1 after composing with ^LH_1 → ^LZ_1 because ξ̂_1 is dual to ξ_1 on Ĥ (Waldspurger 2008 §1.4).
Surjectivity H_1(F) → H(F): H^1(F, Z_1) = 0 for an induced torus (Shapiro and Hilbert 90).
acceptance: When H_der is simply connected and ℋ = ^LH, the trivial z-pair exists and λ_1 = 1.
For U(n_1) × U(n_2) and for the tori of SL_2, the trivial z-pair applies.
A central extension with non-induced torus kernel need not give H_1(F) → H(F) surjective.

nodes.title: Images and norms: matching of strongly regular classes
nodes.statement: Let (H, ℋ, s, ξ) be an endoscopic datum for (G, θ, ω) over F of characteristic 0, with G* the quasi-split inner form of G (in the ordinary case) or the quasi-split form of the twisted space. Fix Γ-stable Borel pairs (B_H, T_H) of H and (B*, T*) of G*; ξ gives an isomorphism T_H ≅ (T*)_{θ*} (coinvariants) and, through the Weyl groups Ω_H ⊆ Ω^{θ*}, a Γ-equivariant map T_H/Ω_H → (T*)_{θ*}/Ω^{θ*} from semisimple conjugacy classes of H to semisimple θ-conjugacy classes of G (Waldspurger 2008 §1.3 (5)); in the ordinary case it is the map of Chevalley quotients induced by an admissible embedding T_H → T ⊆ G*. A semisimple γ_H ∈ H(F) is (strongly) G-regular if its image consists of (strongly) regular elements; then it is strongly regular in H. An element δ ∈ G(F) (strongly regular, or θ-strongly regular) is an image (ordinary case) or a norm (twisted case) of γ_H if its class corresponds to that of γ_H; D denotes the set of such pairs (γ_H, δ). In the ordinary case with G = G* quasi-split, every strongly G-regular γ_H ∈ H(F) has an image in G(F) (rationality, ET.0/rational-classes-in-stable-class (d), after a z-extension); for G not quasi-split, γ_H need not have an image in G(F) (e.g. split γ_H for G = D^×). For cyclic base change (G = R_{E/F} G_0, θ a generator of Gal(E/F), H the quasi-split inner form of G_0), every semisimple δ ∈ G(F) has a norm in H(F) (Kottwitz), and the norm induces an injection from stable θ-classes of G(F) to stable classes of H(F); the set of norms is described locally and globally by Labesse's image-of-norm theorems. Matching is defined analogously on the Lie algebras (𝔥, 𝔤) through the map of Chevalley quotients 𝔠_H → 𝔠.
hypotheses: F of characteristic 0
(H, ℋ, s, ξ) an endoscopic datum (ordinary or twisted)
proofSteps: Construct the map T_H/Ω_H → (T*)_{θ*}/Ω^{θ*} from the dual isomorphism given by ξ on maximal tori (Waldspurger 2008 §1.3; Langlands–Shelstad §1.3 for the ordinary case, where admissible embeddings T_H → T are those induced by ξ up to Ĝ-conjugacy).
Strong G-regularity implies strong regularity in H (Waldspurger 2008 §1.3, citing Kottwitz–Shelstad Lemma 3.3.C).

Existence of images in quasi-split G: Kottwitz's rationality theorem for quasi-split groups with simply connected derived group and reduction through z-extensions (ET.0/rational-classes-in-stable-class (d)).

Base change norms: Labesse Définition 2.4.1 and Théorème 2.4.2 (every semisimple δ has a norm), Lemme 2.4.3 (injectivity on stable classes, after Kottwitz), and the descriptions of the image of the norm locally (Propositions 2.5.2–2.5.3) and globally (Théorème 2.6.3).
acceptance: For the principal datum of quasi-split G the image of γ_H is its own stable class.
For R_{E/F}G_m with the Galois automorphism, norms are N_{E/F}(x) and the set of norms is N E^×.
A split regular element of GL_2(F) has no image in D^×.

nodes.title: Elliptic endoscopic data of unitary similitude groups
nodes.statement: Let F = F^+F_0 be a CM field with F^+ totally real and F_0 imaginary quadratic, and for a vector n⃗ = (n_1, …, n_s) of positive integers let G_{n⃗} be the quasi-split group over ℚ of [Shin 2011 §3.1]: G_{n⃗}(R) = {(λ, g) ∈ R^× × GL_{n⃗}(F ⊗_ℚ R) : g Φ_{n⃗} ᵗg^c = λ Φ_{n⃗}} with Φ_{n⃗} = diag(Φ_{n_1}, …, Φ_{n_s}) the block-diagonal matrix built from Φ_m = ((−1)^{i+1}δ_{i, m+1−j}). Its dual group is Ĝ_{n⃗} = ℂ^× × ∏_{σ ∈ Φ^+} GL_{n⃗}(ℂ) (Φ^+ the embeddings F → ℂ above a fixed τ_0 : F_0 → ℂ), with W_ℚ acting through W_ℚ/W_{F_0} by (λ, (g_σ)) ↦ (λ ∏_σ det g_σ, (Φ_{n⃗} ᵗg^{-1}_{c w⁻¹σ} Φ^{-1}_{n⃗})_σ) for w ∉ W_{F_0}. For G = G_N (N = n in Shin's notation, N = 2n for Caraiani–Scholze) a set of representatives of E_ell(G_N) is {(G_N, 1, id)} ∪ {(G_{n_1,n_2}, s_{n_1,n_2}, η_{n_1,n_2}) : n_1 + n_2 = N, n_1 ≥ n_2 ≥ 1}, where s_{n_1,n_2} = (1, (I_{n_1}, −I_{n_2})) and η_{n_1,n_2} is induced by GL_{n_1} × GL_{n_2} ⊂ GL_N, where, following Caraiani–Scholze, the pair (n_1, n_2) may be omitted when n_1, n_2 and [F^+ : ℚ] are all odd (Kottwitz 1984, condition 7.4.3). Fixing a character ϖ : 𝔸_{F_0}^×/F_0^× → ℂ^× whose restriction to 𝔸^×/ℚ^× is the quadratic character of F_0 (viewed as a character of W_{F_0} by class field theory), the L-morphism η̃_{n_1,n_2} : ^LG_{n_1,n_2} → ^LG_N is w ↦ (ϖ(w)^{−N(n_1,n_2)}, (diag(ϖ(w)^{ε(N−n_1)} I_{n_1}, ϖ(w)^{ε(N−n_2)} I_{n_2}))_σ) ⋊ w for w ∈ W_{F_0} and w* ↦ (a_{n_1,n_2}, (Φ_{n_1,n_2}Φ_N^{-1})_σ) ⋊ w* for a fixed w* ∈ W_ℚ \ W_{F_0}, where ε(m) ∈ {0, 1} is m mod 2, N(n_1,n_2) = [F^+ : ℚ](n_1 ε(N − n_1) + n_2 ε(N − n_2))/2 and a_{n_1,n_2}² = (−1)^{N(n_1,n_2)} (Shin writes (−1)^{−N(n_1,n_2)} det(Φ_{n_1,n_2}Φ_N), which is the same number since det Φ_m = 1). Each such datum is elliptic, the listed data are pairwise non-isomorphic, and Out(G_{n_1,n_2}, s, η) is trivial unless n_1 = n_2, when it has order 2.
hypotheses: F = F^+F_0 CM with F^+ ≠ ℚ allowed (Caraiani–Scholze assume [F^+ : ℚ] > 1 for the trace formula, not for this list)
the character ϖ fixed as above
proofSteps: Compute Ĝ_N and its Galois action from the definition of G_N (ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.5/dual-of-weil-restriction for the restriction of scalars, RG2.5/galois-action-on-dual-group).

An elliptic s ∈ Ĝ_N modulo the centre has, in each GL_N(ℂ)-factor compatible with the Galois action, eigenvalues ±1 up to the centre; the Galois-fixed connected centralizers are of the form GL_{n_1} × GL_{n_2} (Rogawski's classification for unitary groups, adapted to similitudes in Shin §3.2).

The L-morphism condition for η̃ is checked directly from the semidirect product rule (Caraiani–Scholze non-compact §5.2, p. 68, after Rogawski 1992 §1.2); Kottwitz's condition 7.4.3 removes data that do not extend to L-embeddings or are not relevant when all three integers are odd.
The index condition n_2 ≥ 1 (Shin) avoids repeating the principal datum; Caraiani–Scholze print n_2 ≥ 0 (recorded in sourceIssues).
acceptance: N = 2, [F^+ : ℚ] even: E_ell(G_2) = {G_2, G_{1,1}}, and G_{1,1} has Out of order 2 (the swap of the two factors).
N = 3 and [F^+ : ℚ] odd: the pair (n_1, n_2) = (2, 1) is kept and there are two elliptic data.
N = 2 with [F^+ : ℚ] odd: n_1 = n_2 = 1 and [F^+ : ℚ] are all odd, so the datum G_{1,1} may be omitted under condition 7.4.3; for [F^+ : ℚ] even it is present.

sources.locator: §§3.1–3.2, (3.1)–(3.4) and the displays for η̃_{n_1,n_2} and N(n_1,n_2), Remark 3.2 (pp. 12–14)
sources.match: The groups G_{n⃗}, their dual groups, the set E_ell(G_n) = {(G_n, s_n, η_n)} ∪ {(G_{n_1,n_2}, s_{n_1,n_2}, η_{n_1,n_2}) : n_1 + n_2 = n, n_1 ≥ n_2 > 0} and the explicit L-morphisms through ϖ.
The same list for G_{2n} with the exclusion when n_1, n_2 and [F^+ : ℚ] are all odd (Kottwitz 1984, 7.4.3), and the explicit extension η̃_{n_1,n_2} of η_{n_1,n_2} via ϖ and the element a_{n_1,n_2}.
For a unitary group G attached to an unramified quadratic F′/F and a nontrivial partition n = n_1 + n_2, H = U(n_1) × U(n_2) is the corresponding endoscopic group, with κ : Λ → {±1}.

nodes.title: Centralizers, stable classes and matching for unitary Lie algebras
nodes.statement: Let E/F be a quadratic extension of nonarchimedean local fields of characteristic 0 with Galois conjugation c and norm character η_{E/F}, V a nondegenerate Hermitian space of dimension n over E, U(V) its unitary group and Herm(V) the F-space of Hermitian endomorphisms (the Lie algebra of U(V) up to the scalar ε with ε^c = −ε). (a) (Centralizers) For regular semisimple δ ∈ Herm(V) write F[δ] = F[X]/(char_δ) = ∏_{i=1}^m F_i (F_i/F fields), E_i = E ⊗_F F_i, and S_1 = {i : F_i ⊉ E}, S_2 its complement. The centralizer T_δ of δ in U(V) is the torus of norm-one elements of E[δ] = E ⊗_F F[δ], so T_δ(F) ≅ ∏_{i ∈ S_1} E_i^1 × ∏_{i ∈ S_2} F_i^× with E_i^1 the norm-one elements of E_i/F_i; H^1(F, T_δ) ≅ ∏_{S_1} ℤ/2; and E(T_δ, U(V); F) = ker(H^1(F, T_δ) → H^1_ab(F, U(V))) = ker(∏_{S_1} ℤ/2 → ℤ/2), the map being the sum. (b) (Matching) Let V_a, V_b be Hermitian spaces of dimensions a, b with a + b = n and W_{a,b} = V_a ⊕ V_b. Regular semisimple δ ∈ Herm(V) and δ′ ∈ Herm(V′) are Jacquet–Langlands transfers of each other if they are GL_n(E)-conjugate after identifying V ≅ E^n ≅ V′; then δ′ = Ad(g)δ and inv(δ, δ′) := [σ ↦ g^{-1}σ(g)] ∈ H^1(F, T_δ) extends the invariant on D(T_δ, U(V); F). Regular semisimple δ ∈ Herm(V) and (δ_a, δ_b) ∈ Herm(V_a) ⊕ Herm(V_b) match if δ and φ_{a,b}(δ_a, δ_b) are Jacquet–Langlands transfers, where φ_{a,b} : Herm(V_a) ⊕ Herm(V_b) → Herm(W_{a,b}) is the block-diagonal embedding. (c) (The endoscopic character) If y ∈ Herm(V) matches (y_a, y_b), then H^1(F, T_y) = ∏_{S_1(a)} ℤ/2 × ∏_{S_1(b)} ℤ/2 = H^1(F, T_{y_a} × T_{y_b}), and the character κ attached to the elliptic endoscopic datum (U(V_a) × U(V_b), s, ξ) is the restriction to E(T_y, U(V); F) of the character κ̃ that is trivial on the factors indexed by S_1(a) and nontrivial on those indexed by S_1(b).
hypotheses: E/F quadratic, F nonarchimedean of characteristic 0 (residue characteristic odd where the source uses it)
δ regular semisimple
proofSteps: (a) Decompose V along the characteristic polynomial; on each factor with F_i ⊉ E the centralizer is the norm-one torus of E_i/F_i, otherwise a split torus; Tate–Nakayama (ET.0/tate-nakayama-tori) gives H^1 = ℤ/2 for each norm-one factor and 0 for the others, and H^1_ab(F, U(V)) = ℤ/2 (the discriminant) with the map the sum (Leslie Lemma 1.8, citing Rogawski 1990 §3.4).

(b) Definition 2.6 of Leslie, an instance of ET.0/norm-correspondence for the Lie algebra with the endoscopic datum of ET.0/unitary-elliptic-endoscopic-data (local version) and transport across the inner forms U(V), U(V′) (ET.0/inner-twist).
(c) Leslie Lemma 2.7 (stated there without proof as standard): compute κ ∈ π_0(T̂^Γ) from s = diag(1_a, −1_b) through the identification of (a) (Rogawski 1990 Chapter 3).
acceptance: n = 1: Herm(V) = F, T_δ = U(1) = E^1, H^1 = ℤ/2, and E(T_δ, U(V); F) = ker(ℤ/2 → ℤ/2) = 0, so each stable class is a single class.
n = 2, δ with F[δ] = F × F and E ⊄ F: S_1 = {1, 2}, H^1(F, T_δ) = (ℤ/2)², E = ℤ/2 (two rational classes) and for (a, b) = (1, 1) κ is the nontrivial character.

nodes.title: Worked examples for stable conjugacy and endoscopic data
nodes.statement: The following are verified from the definitions of ET.0. (1) Split torus T = G_m^r: E(T) = {(T, 1, id)}, D(T, T; F) = 0, stable = rational conjugacy. (2) GL_n over F: H^1(F, T) = 0 for every maximal torus (a product of R_{F_i/F} G_m), so D = 0 and stable = rational conjugacy; E_ell(GL_n) = {GL_n}; H^1_ab(F, GL_n) = 0 and A(GL_n) = π_0(ℂ^×)^D = 0. (3) A nonsplit unitary group U(1,1) or U(2) attached to quadratic E/F: elliptic maximal tori T ≅ U(1)×U(1) have D(T) of order 2 (ET.0/unitary-hermitian-matching (a)), E_ell(U(2)) = {U(2), U(1)×U(1)} and the character κ of the second datum is the nontrivial character of D(T). (4) A proper Levi with different rational classes in one stable class: in Sp_4 over p-adic F the Levi M = GL_1 × SL_2 contains regular elliptic elements of its SL_2 factor whose M-stable class consists of two M(F)-classes (ET.0/rational-classes-in-stable-class acceptance), while the corresponding G-stable class may contain further classes. (5) SL_2: H^1(F, SL_2) = 1, H^1(F, PGL_2) = ℤ/2, E_ell(SL_2) consists of SL_2 and the norm-one tori of the three quadratic extensions (for p odd).
hypotheses: F a p-adic field (p odd for (5))
proofSteps: Each item is a direct computation with ET.0/tate-nakayama-tori, ET.0/kottwitz-duality, ET.0/rational-classes-in-stable-class and ET.0/endoscopic-datum.
acceptance: Each of the five examples is checked as stated.

nodes.title: Invariant orbital integrals and their normalizations
nodes.statement: Let F be a local field of characteristic 0 and G connected reductive over F, with a fixed Haar measure dg on G(F). The orbital integral of a semisimple γ ∈ G(F) is owned by AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.6 (target AS.6.8a of its package, which moved it below this roadmap in the upstream order) and is imported here: for f ∈ C_c^∞(G(F)) (locally constant compactly supported if F is p-adic, smooth compactly supported if F is archimedean), O_γ(f) = ∫_{G_γ^0(F)\G(F)} f(g⁻¹γg) dg/dt, with dt a Haar measure on the identity component G_γ^0(F) of the centralizer and the quotient measure (AdelicAlgebraicGroups:AA.2/quotient-measure); it converges for every semisimple γ, and J_G(γ, f) = |D^G(γ)|^{1/2} O_γ(f) with D^G(γ) = det(1 − Ad(γ))|_{𝔤/𝔤_γ}. This node fixes the conventions under which ET uses it and plans its extensions: (i) following Waldspurger, O^G_γ(f) = [G_γ(F) : G_γ^0(F)]⁻¹ O_γ(f), which depends only on the G(F)-class of γ; (ii) measures on centralizers of stably conjugate (or matching) elements are transported by the inner twist between their identity components (ET.0/semisimple-conjugacy); (iii) for regular semisimple γ, J_G(γ, f) is a bounded locally constant (p-adic) or smooth (real) function of γ on G_reg(F) for fixed f (Harish-Chandra), and the Weyl integration formula expresses ∫_{G(F)} f through the integrals of |D^G(t)| O_t(f) over maximal tori; (iv) the Lie-algebra version: for f ∈ C_c^∞(𝔤(F)) and X ∈ 𝔤(F) semisimple, O_X(f) = ∫_{G_X^0(F)\G(F)} f(Ad(g)⁻¹X) dg/dt and D(X) = det(ad X)|_{𝔤/𝔤_X}; for F p-adic, the orbital integrals of nilpotent orbits are defined by the invariant measure on the orbit (Deligne–Ranga Rao) and are needed for germ expansions; (v) semisimple descent: near a semisimple γ, O^G is expressed through O^{G_γ} of a descended function on a neighbourhood of 0 in 𝔤_γ(F).
hypotheses: F local of characteristic 0
G connected reductive with fixed Haar measures on G(F) and on the centralizers
proofSteps: The group orbital integral, its quotient measure and its convergence are imported from AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.6 (requested; AS.6.8a of its package, after Arthur's introduction §18). Quotient measure: AdelicAlgebraicGroups:AA.2/quotient-measure applies since reductive groups are unimodular; Weil's integration formula AA.2/quotient-integral-integrable gives the integral as an iterated integral (Kottwitz, Clay notes §2).

Convergence for semisimple γ (the argument behind AS.6.8a, used here for the Lie-algebra version): the orbit O_γ is closed, and G_γ^0(F)\G(F) → O_γ(F) is proper with finite fibres over its image (Kottwitz, Clay notes §3).

Boundedness and local constancy of normalized orbital integrals near regular elements: Harish-Chandra; the p-adic statements are in Kottwitz's Clay notes §§3, 15–16 (Harish-Chandra's compactness lemma and semisimple descent).

Nilpotent orbital integrals: the invariant measure on a nilpotent orbit extends to a Radon measure on 𝔤(F) (Deligne–Ranga Rao), recalled in Kottwitz's Clay notes §17; the original papers were not read (sourceVersions).
acceptance: O_X(f) = f(X) for central X ∈ 𝔤(F) and for tori (the group statement is AS.6.8a's test).
For GL_2 over a p-adic field and γ = diag(a, b) with a, b ∈ 𝒪^× and |a − b| = 1, the orbital integral of 1_{GL_2(𝒪)} is 1 with the standard measures.
Orbital integrals are invariant under conjugation of γ and of f.

nodes.title: κ-orbital integrals and stable orbital integrals
nodes.statement: Let F be local of characteristic 0, G connected reductive, γ ∈ G(F) strongly regular semisimple with centralizer the maximal torus T, and for each γ′ in the stable class of γ let inv(γ, γ′) ∈ D(T, G; F) be its invariant (ET.0/rational-classes-in-stable-class); measures on the centralizers T_{γ′} are transported from T. For a character κ of E(T, G; F) (equivalently an element of Kottwitz's 𝔎(T/F), ET.0/rational-classes-in-stable-class (b)) and f ∈ C_c^∞(G(F)), the κ-orbital integral is O^κ_γ(f) = Σ_{γ′} κ(inv(γ, γ′)) e(G_{γ′}) O_{γ′}(f), the sum running over representatives of the G(F)-classes in the stable class of γ (a finite set) and e the Kottwitz sign (trivial for tori; it enters for singular γ with non-quasi-split centralizers). The stable orbital integral is SO_γ(f) = O^1_γ(f). For γ semisimple but not strongly regular one sums over the rational classes in the stable class weighted by e(G_{γ′}) and the measure conventions of Kottwitz 1986 §5. Changing γ within its stable class multiplies O^κ_γ by κ(inv(γ, γ′))⁻¹, so O^κ is not a function of the stable class alone unless κ = 1; SO_γ is. A distribution on G(F) is stable if it is a limit of linear combinations of the SO_γ. The same definitions apply on the Lie algebra 𝔤(F).
hypotheses: F local of characteristic 0
γ strongly regular (singular case with Kottwitz's conventions)
proofSteps: Finiteness of the sum: D(T, G; F) is finite (ET.0/rational-classes-in-stable-class (b)).
Dependence on γ within its stable class: inv(γ″, γ′) = inv(γ, γ′) − inv(γ, γ″) in the abelian group E(T, G; F) (Leslie (2.5); Hales §6.1).
Singular case: Kottwitz 1986 §5.1–5.2 with the signs e(I).
acceptance: For GL_n, SO_γ = O_γ.
For SL_2 and an elliptic torus, O^κ_γ = O_γ − O_{γ′} for the nontrivial κ.
O^κ changes by κ(inv(γ, γ″))⁻¹ when γ is replaced by a stably conjugate γ″.

nodes.title: a-data and χ-data for the roots of a maximal torus
nodes.statement: Let F be a field of characteristic 0, T a maximal torus of a connected reductive G over F (or of G* quasi-split), R = R(G, T) its roots with the action of Γ_F, and for α ∈ R let F_α ⊇ F_{±α} be the fixed fields of the stabilizers of α and of {±α} in Γ_F; α is symmetric if F_α ≠ F_{±α} (then [F_α : F_{±α}] = 2) and asymmetric otherwise. (a) a-data is a family {a_α ∈ F_α^× : α ∈ R} with a_{σα} = σ(a_α) for σ ∈ Γ_F and a_{−α} = −a_α. (b) χ-data is a family of characters {χ_α : F_α^× → ℂ^×} with χ_{σα} = χ_α ∘ σ⁻¹, χ_{−α} = χ_α⁻¹, and, for α symmetric, χ_α restricted to F_{±α}^× equal to the quadratic character of F_α/F_{±α} (local case; for F global, characters of the idele class groups with the same properties). a-data is used to define the splitting invariant λ(T_sc) of Δ_I and the term Δ_III2 uses χ-data to build an L-embedding ^LT → ^LG; the absolute transfer factor (ET.1/local-transfer-factor) does not depend on these choices (Langlands–Shelstad Theorem 3.7.A), but each of Δ_I, Δ_II, Δ_III2 separately does. In the twisted setting, a-data and χ-data are taken for the restricted root system of (T, θ) (Kottwitz–Shelstad 2012 §2.2, (2.2.2)).
hypotheses: F of characteristic 0 (local or global)
T a maximal torus of G over F
proofSteps: Existence: choose a_α on representatives of Γ-orbits of roots and extend by the equivariance rules; for symmetric α choose a_α with σ(a_α) = −a_α for the nontrivial σ ∈ Gal(F_α/F_{±α}). For χ-data, extend characters of the idele class or multiplicative groups of F_{±α} by class field theory (Langlands–Shelstad §2.2 and §2.5).
The defining properties are exactly those used to make λ(T_sc) and the L-embedding ^LT → ^LG well defined (Langlands–Shelstad §2.3, §2.6).
acceptance: For a split torus of SL_2, a-data is a single a ∈ F^× with a_{−α} = −a.
For a symmetric root, χ_α restricted to F_{±α}^× is the quadratic character of F_α/F_{±α}.
The transfer factor does not depend on the choice of a-data and χ-data (ET.1/local-transfer-factor).

nodes.title: The Langlands–Shelstad transfer factor
nodes.statement: Let F be local of characteristic 0, G connected reductive with quasi-split inner form G* and inner twist ψ : G → G*, (H, ℋ, s, ξ) an endoscopic datum with a z-pair (H_1, ξ_1) (ET.0/z-pair). For a strongly G-regular γ_1 ∈ H_1(F) with image γ_H ∈ H(F) and a strongly regular δ ∈ G(F) matching it (ET.0/norm-correspondence), choose an admissible embedding T_H → T* of the centralizer of γ_H into G*, a-data and χ-data for T* (ET.1/a-data-chi-data). Define: Δ_I(γ_1, δ) = ⟨λ(T_sc), s_T⟩ (the splitting invariant λ(T_sc) ∈ H^1(F, T_sc) built from a-data paired by Tate–Nakayama with the image s_T of s); Δ_II(γ_1, δ) = ∏_α χ_α((α(γ) − 1)/a_α) over Γ-orbit representatives of roots of T outside H; Δ_III1(γ_1, δ; γ̄_1, δ̄) = ⟨inv(γ, δ; γ̄, δ̄), κ⟩, the pairing of the relative invariant in H^1(F, U) (U = T × T̄/Z(G)) with the endoscopic character; Δ_III2(γ_1, δ) = ⟨a, γ⟩ for a ∈ H^1(W_F, T̂) measuring the difference of the L-embeddings ^LT → ^LG given by χ-data and by ξ through ℋ (with the z-pair); Δ_IV(γ_1, δ) = |D_G(δ)|^{1/2}|D_H(γ_H)|^{-1/2}. The relative transfer factor Δ(γ_1, δ; γ̄_1, δ̄) = Δ_I Δ_II Δ_III1 Δ_III2 Δ_IV (ratios) is independent of all choices (Langlands–Shelstad Theorem 3.7.A). An absolute transfer factor is a function Δ(γ_1, δ) on matching pairs with Δ(γ_1, δ)Δ(γ̄_1, δ̄)⁻¹ = Δ(γ_1, δ; γ̄_1, δ̄); it is determined up to a nonzero constant. Normalizations: (i) for G quasi-split, the Langlands–Shelstad absolute factor Δ_0 = Δ_I Δ_II Δ_III2 Δ_IV (Δ_III1 trivial with base point δ̄ = δ for G = G*); (ii) Kottwitz–Shelstad 2012 (§5.1) record four variants for (H, s, ξ): the Langlands–Shelstad factor Δ, adapted to the classical local Langlands correspondence (Langlands' normalization of local class field theory, uniformizers ↔ Frobenius); its renormalization Δ_D = Δ_I Δ_II Δ_III1 Δ_III2,D Δ_IV with Δ_III2,D = ⟨γ, a(χ⁻¹)⟩⁻¹, adapted to Deligne's normalization (uniformizers ↔ inverse Frobenius); and Δ′, Δ′_D, the factors Δ, Δ_D of the datum (H, s⁻¹, ξ) regarded as factors for (H, s, ξ). The corrected twisted factors Δ_D = Δ_I^new Δ_II⁻¹ Δ_III Δ_IV and Δ′ = (Δ_I^new Δ_III)⁻¹ Δ_II Δ_IV of ET.1/twisted-transfer-factor reduce to these Δ_D and Δ′ in standard endoscopy (§§5.3–5.4); (iii) the Whittaker normalization Δ_λ fixes the constant by a Whittaker datum λ of G* through the root number ε_L(V, ψ) of the virtual representation V = X^*(T*) ⊗ ℂ − X^*(T_H) ⊗ ℂ: Δ_{λ,D} = ε_L(V, ψ) Δ_I^new Δ_II Δ_III^new Δ_IV = ε_L(V, ψ) Δ_I^new Δ_II⁻¹ Δ_III Δ_IV and Δ′_λ = ε_L(V, ψ)(Δ_I^new Δ_III)⁻¹ Δ_II Δ_IV (Kottwitz–Shelstad (5.5.1)–(5.5.2), for quasi-split G with an F-splitting preserved by θ). Every consumer records which of Δ, Δ′, Δ_D, Δ′_D and which normalization (base point or Whittaker) it uses, and which normalization of local class field theory (CFT Layer 7) is in force; the product formula (ET.1/transfer-factor-properties) does not identify two conventions without this record.
hypotheses: F local of characteristic 0
(H, ℋ, s, ξ) an endoscopic datum of G with a z-pair
δ strongly regular in G(F), γ_1 strongly G-regular in H_1(F), matching
proofSteps: Δ_I: Langlands–Shelstad §3.2 (p. 241), λ(T_sc) from the a-data splitting (§2.3) and Tate–Nakayama pairing (ET.0/tate-nakayama-tori).

Δ_II: §3.3 (p. 243); Δ_III1: §3.4 (p. 245), a relative term pairing an invariant with κ; Δ_III2: §3.5 (p. 246), built from χ-data through the L-embedding of §2.6; Δ_IV: §3.6 (p. 248), the quotient of Weyl discriminants.
Independence of the product of choices: Theorem 3.7.A (p. 248), proved by computing how each term changes with the admissible embedding, a-data and χ-data (Lemmas of §§3.2–3.5).

Sign corrections: Kottwitz–Shelstad 2012 show the 1999 twisted factor is not independent of χ-data unless Δ_II or Δ_III enters with exponent −1 (introduction, PDF p. 2), define Δ_D and Δ′ ((1.0.3), (1.0.4); §§5.3–5.4) and their Whittaker-normalized versions ((5.5.1)–(5.5.2), §5.5); for standard endoscopy they list the four variants Δ, Δ_D, Δ′, Δ′_D (§5.1, (5.1.1)–(5.1.2)).
Conventions on local class field theory and Frobenius: KS 2012 §4.1 (Deligne's vs Langlands' reciprocity), with the upstream ClassFieldTheory Layer 7 normalizations recorded as the ones in force.
acceptance: For H = G = G* and s = 1 the relative factor is 1.
The relative factor satisfies the cocycle identity for three matching pairs.
For SL_2 and the elliptic torus datum, |Δ_IV(u, δ)| = |(u − ū)²|_F^{1/2} and the factor changes by the nontrivial character between the two rational classes.
