nodes.title: Transport, descent, central extensions and the global product formula
nodes.statement: In the setting of ET.1/local-transfer-factor: (a) (Invariance) Δ(γ_1, δ) is invariant under H_1(F)-conjugation of γ_1 and G(F)-conjugation of δ, and transforms under Z_1(F) by λ_1: Δ(zγ_1, δ) = λ_1(z)⁻¹ Δ(γ_1, δ). (b) (Change of z-pair and of datum) An isomorphism of endoscopic data and a change of z-pair transport the factor, with the transported factor a multiple of the original by a constant determined by the change of λ_1. (c) (Central extensions) For a z-extension G̃ → G with induced kernel, the transfer factor of G is obtained by restriction from that of G̃ for the corresponding datum (Langlands–Shelstad §4.4). (d) (Extension to G-regular elements) The factor extends to all G-regular, not only strongly G-regular, pairs (§4.3). (e) (Descent) Near a semisimple element ε_1 of H_1(F) whose image matches a semisimple η ∈ G(F), the factor on nearby pairs is, up to a constant, the Lie-algebra transfer factor of the descended endoscopic datum for G_η at the corresponding elements of 𝔥_ε and 𝔤_η (Langlands–Shelstad 'Descent for transfer factors', used by Waldspurger 2008 §§2.3, 3.9, 5.10–5.11). (f) (Global product formula) Let F be a number field, (H, s, ξ) a global endoscopic datum with z-pair, and (γ_1, δ) a pair of rational elements that match at every place (γ_1 ∈ H_1(F) strongly G-regular, δ ∈ G(F)). Then the canonical adelic transfer factor Δ_𝔸 = ∏_v Δ_v (defined using global a-data and χ-data and well defined because almost all local factors equal 1) satisfies Δ_𝔸(γ_1, δ) = 1 (Langlands–Shelstad Theorem 6.4.A; Corollary 6.4.B); consequently local absolute factors Δ_v can be normalized so that ∏_v Δ_v(γ_1, δ_v) = ⟨obs-invariant, κ⟩ for adelic δ = (δ_v), the pairing of ET.0/global-kottwitz-obstruction. The formula is stated for one fixed convention of ET.1/local-transfer-factor at every place; mixing Δ′ and Δ_D, or two normalizations of class field theory, invalidates it.
hypotheses: F local (a)–(e) or a number field (f), characteristic 0
the conventions of ET.1/local-transfer-factor fixed uniformly
proofSteps: (a) Langlands–Shelstad §4.1 'Invariance' and Waldspurger 2008 §2.2 (Kottwitz–Shelstad Lemma 5.1.C for the Z_1-behaviour).
(b)–(d) Langlands–Shelstad §§4.2–4.4 (the local hypothesis, extension to G-regular elements, passage to central extensions).

(e) Langlands–Shelstad 'Descent for transfer factors' (1990, not read); the statements used are those recalled by Waldspurger 2008 §2.3 and §3.9 and by Kottwitz's Clay notes §16 (semisimple descent for orbital integrals).

(f) Langlands–Shelstad §6.4, Theorem 6.4.A and Corollary 6.4.B (p. 269): the global a-data and χ-data give a product of local terms each of which is trivial globally by the product formula for characters and the global Tate–Nakayama duality (ET.0/tate-nakayama-tori (b)); the comparison with the obstruction pairing uses ET.0/global-kottwitz-obstruction.
acceptance: For ordinary endoscopy of GL_n only H = GL_n occurs and the product formula is trivial; for SL_2 over a number field and H = R^1_{E/F} G_m with γ ∈ E^1 rational and regular, the product over all places of the local factors built from global a-data and χ-data equals 1.

nodes.title: Twisted transfer factors and the Kottwitz–Shelstad corrections
nodes.statement: Let F be local of characteristic 0, (G, θ, ω) a twisted triple with θ quasi-semisimple, (H, ℋ, s, ξ) a twisted endoscopic datum (ET.0/endoscopic-datum) with z-pair (H_1, ξ_1, ξ̂_1), and 𝒟_1 the set of matching pairs (γ_1, δ) of strongly G-regular γ_1 ∈ H_{1,z}(F) and strongly θ-regular δ ∈ G(F) (ET.0/norm-correspondence). The twisted transfer factor is built from twisted a-data and χ-data for the restricted roots of (T, θ), the twisted splitting invariant (Kottwitz–Shelstad 2012 §2.2, Lemma 2.2.1, Proposition 2.2.3) and the analogues of Δ_II, Δ_III, Δ_IV: (1) the corrected factors Δ_D = Δ_I^new Δ_II⁻¹ Δ_III Δ_IV (compatible with Deligne's normalization of local class field theory) and Δ′ = (Δ_I^new Δ_III)⁻¹ Δ_II Δ_IV (compatible with Langlands' classical normalization), where the 1999 product Δ_I Δ_II Δ_III Δ_IV is not independent of χ-data; (2) the new term Δ_I^new = ⟨λ_{a}(T, θ), s_{T,θ}⟩ uses the twisted splitting invariant; it agrees with Δ_I unless the restricted root system is non-reduced (some power θ^i preserves an irreducible component of type A_{2n} and acts on it by a nontrivial diagram automorphism), for instance θ = transpose-inverse (up to inner automorphisms) on GL(2n + 1), and never differs for cyclic base change; (3) the Whittaker-normalized twisted factors Δ_{λ,D} and Δ′_λ. The relative factor Δ(γ_1, δ; γ̄_1, δ̄) is independent of all auxiliary choices and transforms under Z_1(F) by λ_1; an absolute factor is fixed by a base point or a Whittaker datum. For cyclic base change (G = R_{E/F} G_0, θ a generator of Gal(E/F), ω = 1) with H the quasi-split inner form of G_0 and s = 1, the transfer factor of the norm correspondence is 1 on pairs (γ, δ) with γ a norm of δ (Labesse's normalization of association, §3.2).
hypotheses: F local of characteristic 0
(G, θ, ω) twisted triple and (H, ℋ, s, ξ) a twisted endoscopic datum with z-pair
proofSteps: Use the twisted splitting invariant of Kottwitz–Shelstad 2012 §2.2 and its comparison with the untwisted one (§3.5, Proposition 3.5.2) to define Δ_I^new (§3.4).
Check independence of χ-data for Δ_D and Δ′ by the computation of Kottwitz–Shelstad 2012 §§5.3–5.4: the χ-data dependence of Δ_II and Δ_III cancels only with one of them inverted.
Whittaker normalization: §5.5, formulas (5.5.1)–(5.5.2).

Base change: Labesse §3.2 defines association with factor 1 on norms; Kottwitz–Shelstad 2012 §5.6 note Δ_I^new = Δ_I for cyclic base change, so Labesse's normalization is the specialization of either corrected factor up to sign conventions recorded in the consumer.
acceptance: For base change of G_m the factor is 1 on norms and 0 elsewhere.
For θ = 1 the twisted factors reduce to the ordinary Δ′ and Δ_D.
For GL_{2n+1} with transpose-inverse, Δ_I^new differs from Δ_I.

nodes.title: Transfer factors for Lie algebras
nodes.statement: Let F be local of characteristic 0 (or a local field of characteristic p not dividing |W| in the equal-characteristic setting of Ngô), G quasi-split connected reductive and (H, s, ξ) an endoscopic datum (no z-pair is needed on the Lie algebra). Matching of regular semisimple elements of 𝔥(F) and 𝔤(F) is the Lie-algebra version of ET.0/norm-correspondence (stable classes on both sides, ET.0/semisimple-conjugacy). The Lie-algebra transfer factor Δ(X_H, X) on matching regular semisimple pairs is defined as in Langlands–Shelstad with Δ_II, Δ_III2 replaced by their infinitesimal versions; on the stable class matching a given X_H it has the form Δ(X_H, X) = κ(inv(X_0, X))·Δ_IV(X_H, X)·c(X_H) for a base point X_0 = X_0(X_H) in that stable class, with Δ_IV(X_H, X) = |D_G(X)|^{1/2}|D_H(X_H)|^{-1/2}, inv the invariant of ET.0/rational-classes-in-stable-class and c(X_H) a nonzero number that depends on X_H and on the choice of base point. The relative factor is independent of choices; for quasi-split G the base point can be chosen uniformly in the stable class (the Kostant-section normalization of Kottwitz, used to state Ngô's theorem, is recorded with ET.3/lie-algebra-fundamental-lemma). The relative discriminant r_{G,H}(X_H) = val(D_G(X))/2 − val(D_H(X_H))/2 measures |Δ_IV|. Near the identity the group transfer factor of ET.1/local-transfer-factor descends to this Lie-algebra factor up to a constant (ET.1/transfer-factor-properties (e)). For unitary groups the factor takes the explicit form of ET.1/unitary-transfer-factor.
hypotheses: F local; G quasi-split for the Kostant normalization; in equal characteristic, p ∤ |W|
proofSteps: Langlands–Shelstad's construction carries over to Lie algebras with the exponential replaced by the identity (Waldspurger 2008 §1.6; Kottwitz 'Transfer factors for Lie algebras', Represent. Theory 3 (1999), which was not read: its AMS copy refused automated access).

Base points: for quasi-split G every regular semisimple stable class over F contains a rational element whose centralizer data are uniform in the class (Kottwitz; the Kostant-section version is stated in ET.3/lie-algebra-fundamental-lemma, after Ngô §1.11, p. 23).
The relative discriminant and r_{G,H}: Ngô §1.10, Lemmes 1.10.1–1.10.2 and (1.10.3), p. 22; the restatement with Δ_G, Δ_H: §1.11.3, p. 24.
Unramified normalization and its agreement with the group factor after descent: Waldspurger 2008 §§4.6–4.7, 5.10–5.11.
acceptance: For the principal datum the Lie-algebra factor is 1 on stably conjugate pairs.
For an elliptic datum whose H is a torus, r_{G,H}(a_H) = val(D_G(a))/2.
The factor is invariant under G(F)-conjugation and changes by κ(inv)⁻¹ under stable conjugacy.

nodes.title: Matching test functions and transfer classes
nodes.statement: Let F be local of characteristic 0, (G, θ, ω) with endoscopic datum (H, ℋ, s, ξ), z-pair (H_1, λ_1) and an absolute transfer factor Δ (ET.1/local-transfer-factor, ET.1/twisted-transfer-factor). For f ∈ C_c^∞(G(F)) define O^{G,ω}_{γ_1}(f) = Σ_δ Δ(γ_1, δ) O^ω_δ(f), the sum over representatives of G(F)-classes (θ-classes) of δ matching γ_1. A function f^{H_1} ∈ C_1^∞(H_1(F)) (locally constant, compactly supported modulo Z_1(F), with f(zx) = λ_1(z)⁻¹ f(x)) is a transfer of f, written f ↔ f^{H_1}, if SO_{γ_1}(f^{H_1}) = O^{G,ω}_{γ_1}(f) for every strongly G-regular γ_1 ∈ H_{1,z}(F), and SO_{γ_1}(f^{H_1}) = 0 when no δ matches γ_1. A transfer, if it exists, is unique only modulo the subspace of functions all of whose strongly regular stable orbital integrals vanish; the canonical object is the class of f^{H_1} in the space SI(H_1) of stable orbital integrals (the quotient of C_1^∞(H_1(F)) by that kernel), and the transfer map f ↦ [f^{H_1}] is linear. The same definition applies to Lie algebras (no z-pair) and, at archimedean places, to K-finite or Schwartz functions. For cyclic base change, f ∈ C_c^∞(G_0(E)) and f^H ∈ C_c^∞(H(F)) are associated if SO_γ(f^H) = SO_δ^θ(f) whenever γ is a norm of δ and SO_γ(f^H) = 0 when γ is not a norm (Labesse §3.2).
hypotheses: F local of characteristic 0
an endoscopic datum with z-pair and an absolute transfer factor
proofSteps: Well definedness of O^{G,ω}_{γ_1}: finitely many classes match γ_1 (ET.0/rational-classes-in-stable-class (b)), and the sum does not depend on the representatives because Δ(γ_1, δ)O^ω_δ(f) is a class function of δ (Waldspurger 2008 §1.5).
Ambiguity: two transfers differ by a function in the kernel of all SO_{γ_1}; stable orbital integrals of strongly regular elements determine the class in SI (by definition of SI).
Base change association: Labesse §3.2; Clozel (Proposition 7.2 there) shows that it suffices to test regular elements.
acceptance: For the principal datum of quasi-split G, f is a transfer of itself.
Two transfers of f have the same stable orbital integrals.
In the unramified situation the unit function of H(𝒪) is a transfer of that of G(𝒪) (ET.3/group-fundamental-lemma).

nodes.title: Shalika germs on p-adic Lie algebras
nodes.statement: Let F be a p-adic field and G connected reductive over F with Lie algebra 𝔤. (a) The set of nilpotent G(F)-orbits in 𝔤(F) is finite, and each nilpotent orbit 𝒪 carries an invariant Radon measure μ_𝒪 extending to 𝔤(F) (nilpotent orbital integrals). (b) (Germ expansion) There are functions Γ_𝒪 on 𝔤_rs(F) (Shalika germs), one for each nilpotent orbit, such that for every f ∈ C_c^∞(𝔤(F)) there is a neighbourhood U_f of 0 with O_X(f) = Σ_𝒪 Γ_𝒪(X) μ_𝒪(f) for all X ∈ U_f ∩ 𝔤_rs(F); the germs are uniquely determined as germs at 0. (c) (Homogeneity) For t ∈ F^×, Γ_𝒪(t²X) = |t|^{−dim 𝒪} Γ_𝒪(X) (after normalizing measures compatibly); equivalently the normalized germs Γ̄_𝒪 = |D|^{1/2} Γ_𝒪 satisfy Γ̄_𝒪(t²X) = |t|^{dim G^{X_𝒪} − rank G} Γ̄_𝒪(X) for X_𝒪 ∈ 𝒪 (Kottwitz (17.11.2)). In particular the germ Γ_0 of the zero orbit is homogeneous of degree 0, and the normalized regular germ Γ̄_reg is homogeneous of degree 0 and constant on each Cartan subalgebra (Shalika), so the regular germ Γ_reg is a constant multiple of |D|^{−1/2} there. (d) (Descent) Near a semisimple element, orbital integrals have an expansion in terms of the germs of the centralizer (semisimple descent).
hypotheses: F p-adic of characteristic 0 (the germ expansion also holds in large positive characteristic as used by Waldspurger 2006)
proofSteps: (a) Finiteness of nilpotent orbits and the Deligne–Ranga Rao measures (Kottwitz, Clay notes §17).

(b) Shalika's germ expansion: Kottwitz, Clay notes §6 (for GL_2 and in general) and §17 'Basic results on Shalika germs on 𝔤', via Harish-Chandra's compactness lemma (§15) and the density of regular orbital integrals.
(c) Homogeneity from the scaling X ↦ t²X and the dimension of 𝒪 (Kottwitz, Clay notes §17); deeper results in §27.
(d) Semisimple descent (Kottwitz, Clay notes §16).
acceptance: For 𝔤 = 𝔤𝔩_2, the nilpotent orbits are {0} and the regular one; on an elliptic Cartan subalgebra the germ Γ_0 of {0} is constant and the regular germ is a constant multiple of |D(X)|^{−1/2} (Kottwitz's GL_2 computation, §5.9: for elliptic γ ∈ GL_2(𝒪) the coefficient of the identity orbit is −2/(q − 1), independent of γ, while that of the regular unipotent orbit grows like q^{d_γ}).
For 𝔤 = 𝔱 a torus there is one nilpotent orbit {0} and Γ_0 = 1.

sources.locator: §5.9 (pp. 417–418); §6 'Shalika germs' (p. 418); §15 'Harish-Chandra's compactness lemma' (p. 457); §16 'Semisimple descent' (p. 458); §17 'Basic results on Shalika germs on 𝔤' (p. 459); §27 'Deeper results on Shalika germs' (p. 512); (17.11.2) (p. 465)
sources.match: The germ expansion of orbital integrals near 0 in terms of nilpotent orbital integrals, its uniqueness and homogeneity, and semisimple descent.
Orbital integrals of functions attached to Moy–Prasad lattices depend on F only through its residue field; their germ behaviour is the input of the change of characteristic.

nodes.title: Fourier transforms of orbital integrals and their compatibility with transfer
nodes.statement: Let F be a p-adic field, G connected reductive, ψ a nontrivial additive character and ⟨·,·⟩ a nondegenerate G-invariant symmetric bilinear form on 𝔤 (existing when p is large relative to G), with self-dual Haar measure. For f ∈ C_c^∞(𝔤(F)) let f̂(Y) = ∫ f(X)ψ(⟨X, Y⟩) dX. (a) (Harish-Chandra) For X ∈ 𝔤_rs(F) the distribution f ↦ O_X(f̂) is represented by a locally integrable function Ô_X on 𝔤(F), locally constant on 𝔤_rs(F), and |D(Y)|^{1/2} Ô_X(Y) is locally bounded. (b) (Waldspurger) For an endoscopic datum (H, s, ξ) of quasi-split G and the Lie-algebra transfer factors (ET.1/lie-algebra-transfer-factor), if f^H is a transfer of f then γ_ψ(𝔤) γ_ψ(𝔥)⁻¹ \widehat{f^H} is a transfer of f̂, where γ_ψ are the Weil constants of the quadratic forms; equivalently, the transfer commutes with the Fourier transform up to this explicit constant. (c) Consequently, if the transfer exists for all functions supported near 0 whose Fourier transforms are supported on topologically nilpotent elements, it exists for all of C_c^∞(𝔤(F)) (the reduction in Waldspurger's proof that the fundamental lemma implies transfer).
hypotheses: F p-adic of characteristic 0
p large enough for the invariant form and exponential to behave (Waldspurger's standing hypothesis)
proofSteps: (a) Harish-Chandra's local integrability theorem on the Lie algebra (Kottwitz, Clay notes §26 'Niceness of Ô_X for X ∈ 𝔤_rs', p. 509).

(b) Waldspurger, 'Le lemme fondamental implique le transfert', Compositio Math. 105 (1997), main theorem on Fourier transform and transfer; the paper itself was not freely available and was not read; the statement is the one recalled by Labesse (§3.3, citing its Corollaire 1.7 for inner forms) and by Ngô (introduction, p. 2) and Shin (§3.4, p. 15). Recorded as a gap on source access.
(c) Combine (b) with homogeneity of germs (ET.1/shalika-germs) and the local gluing lemma for transfer (Waldspurger 2008 §2.2).
acceptance: For 𝔤 = 𝔱 a torus, Ô_X(Y) = ψ(⟨X, Y⟩) and transfer is the identity.
For 𝔤𝔩_n (no proper elliptic endoscopy) (b) is the trivial statement that the Fourier transform preserves orbital integral identities up to γ_ψ(𝔤)γ_ψ(𝔤)⁻¹ = 1.

sources.match: Harish-Chandra's theorem that the Fourier transform of a regular semisimple orbital integral is a locally integrable function, locally constant on the regular set, with a bound after multiplying by |D|^{1/2}.
Waldspurger's difficult result that transfer between a connected reductive G_0(F) and its quasi-split inner form is possible (Corollaire 1.7 of his 1997 paper).
The transfer and the fundamental lemma for unit elements are known in all cases, due to Waldspurger, Laumon–Ngô and Ngô, with Hales' reduction to unit elements.

nodes.title: The transfer factor for unitary Lie algebras
nodes.statement: Let E/F be an unramified quadratic extension of p-adic fields (p odd), V, V_a, V_b Hermitian spaces with a + b = n and the elliptic endoscopic datum (U(V_a) × U(V_b), s, ξ) of U(V) (ET.0/unitary-elliptic-endoscopic-data, local version). For matching regular semisimple δ ∈ Herm(V) and (δ_a, δ_b) (ET.0/unitary-hermitian-matching) let D(δ) = ∏_{x_a, x_b}(x_a − x_b), the product over the eigenvalues x_a of δ_a and x_b of δ_b (the quotient of Weyl discriminants of Langlands–Shelstad's Δ_IV). For a nice matching pair (δ = φ_{a,b}(δ_a, δ_b), V ≅ V_a ⊕ V_b) the transfer factor is Δ((δ_a, δ_b), δ) = η_{E/F}(D(δ))|D(δ)|_F, and in general Δ((δ_a, δ_b), δ) = κ(inv(δ, δ′)) η_{E/F}(D(δ))|D(δ)|_F with δ′ = φ_{a,b}(δ_a, δ_b) and κ the endoscopic character (ET.0/unitary-hermitian-matching (c)). Δ vanishes on non-matching pairs and Δ((δ_a, δ_b), δ) Orb^κ(f, δ) depends only on the stable class of δ. This is the specialization of ET.1/lie-algebra-transfer-factor to unitary Lie algebras, in the normalization used by Laumon–Ngô and Leslie.
hypotheses: E/F unramified quadratic, p odd
the endoscopic datum U(V_a) × U(V_b) of U(V)
proofSteps: Specialize the Lie-algebra factor: Δ_IV gives |D(δ)| and the remaining terms combine to the quadratic character η_{E/F}(D(δ)) for the base point given by nice matching pairs (Leslie Remark 2.8 and its Appendix A of a companion paper, cited there).
Behaviour under stable conjugacy: ET.1/lie-algebra-transfer-factor and ET.0/unitary-hermitian-matching (c).
acceptance: n = 2, a = b = 1: δ_a = x, δ_b = y with x ≠ y in F, D = x − y, Δ = η_{E/F}(x − y)|x − y|_F on the nice pair.
a = n, b = 0 (the principal datum): D = 1 and Δ = 1.

sources.match: The transfer factor for Herm(W_1): η_{E/F}(D(δ))|D(δ)|_F for nice matching pairs and κ(inv(δ, δ′)) times it in general; D(δ) is the quotient of Weyl discriminants of Δ_IV (extraction item PAPER-LESLIE-25/15).
The unitary Lie-algebra fundamental lemma O^κ_γ = (−1)^r q^r SO^H_γ uses this normalization.

nodes.title: Harish-Chandra's character theory for real reductive groups
nodes.statement: Let G be a connected reductive group over ℝ (more generally a real reductive group in the sense of AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups:AF.1/real-reductive-group), K a maximal compact subgroup and π a finite-length admissible representation of G(ℝ) (an admissible (𝔤, K)-module with its Casselman–Wallach globalization). (a) For f ∈ C_c^∞(G(ℝ)), π(f) is trace class, and Θ_π(f) = tr π(f) is a conjugation-invariant distribution, an eigendistribution of the centre Z(𝔤) of U(𝔤_ℂ) acting through the infinitesimal character of π when π has one. (b) (Harish-Chandra's regularity theorem) Θ_π is a locally integrable function on G(ℝ), real-analytic on the set G_reg(ℝ) of strongly regular elements: Θ_π(f) = ∫_{G_reg(ℝ)} f(x)Θ_π(x) dx. (c) |D(x)|^{1/2}Θ_π(x) is locally bounded, and on each Cartan subgroup Θ_π is a finite combination of exponentials divided by the Weyl denominator; for discrete series π with Harish-Chandra parameter λ, on the compact Cartan T: Θ_π = (−1)^{q(G)} Σ_{w ∈ W_K} ε(w) e^{wλ}/Δ, and Harish-Chandra's algorithm determines Θ_π on the other Cartan subgroups. (d) Characters determine finite-length representations up to semisimplification, and the characters of the tempered irreducible representations are linearly independent.
hypotheses: G connected reductive over ℝ (all real reductive groups, not only the unitary groups of ET.4–ET.7)
π of finite length, admissible
proofSteps: (a) Trace class property and invariance from admissibility (AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups:AF.1/harish-chandra-admissibility) and the Casselman–Wallach globalization (AF.1/casselman-wallach-globalization).

(b)–(c) Harish-Chandra's regularity theorem for invariant eigendistributions (Harish-Chandra, 'Invariant eigendistributions on a semisimple Lie group', Trans. AMS 119 (1965), not read: the AMS copy refused automated access); the statement is the one recalled by Arthur (Clay introduction §24, pp. 158–159) and required by Kaletha (extraction item P18). The discrete series character formula on the compact Cartan is part of Harish-Chandra's classification (AF.1/discrete-series).
(d) Linear independence of characters: standard consequence of (b) and the Langlands classification (AF.1/langlands-classification).
acceptance: For G = U(1) = SO(2): Θ_{χ_k}(e^{iθ}) = e^{ikθ}.

For G = SL_2(ℝ) and the discrete series D_k^±: on the compact Cartan, Θ_{D_k^+} + Θ_{D_k^−} = −(e^{i(k−1)θ} − e^{−i(k−1)θ})/(e^{iθ} − e^{−iθ}), the negative of the character of the (k−1)-dimensional representation.

sources.match: The character of a real irreducible representation is the distribution f ↦ tr π(f); Harish-Chandra proved it is a locally integrable function analytic on the strongly regular set, with a Weyl-type formula for discrete series on the compact torus and an algorithm for other tori.
Trace distributions of finite-length admissible representations of real reductive groups, their invariance and representability by the regular semisimple character function.

nodes.title: Transfer at the real place
nodes.statement: Let G be connected reductive over ℝ with an endoscopic datum (H, ℋ, s, ξ), z-pair and Langlands–Shelstad transfer factor (ET.1/local-transfer-factor). (a) (Shelstad) For every f ∈ C_c^∞(G(ℝ)) (indeed every Schwartz or K-finite f) there is f^{H_1} ∈ C_1^∞(H_1(ℝ)) whose strongly regular stable orbital integrals are the endoscopic orbital integrals of f: transfer exists at the real place. (b) Spectral form: for tempered L-packets the transfer is dual to the endoscopic character identities expressing the stable character of an H-packet, transported by ξ, as a combination Σ_π Δ(φ_H, π)Θ_π of characters of the corresponding G-packet. (c) For cyclic base change of unitary groups at ℝ (or ℂ/ℝ), K-finite transfer exists and is compatible with the twisted Paley–Wiener theorem (Labesse §3.5, Propositions 3.5.2–3.5.4).
hypotheses: F = ℝ
an endoscopic datum with z-pair (and, for (c), cyclic base change)
proofSteps: (a)–(b) Shelstad's theory of real endoscopy (Shelstad, 'L-indistinguishability for real groups', Math. Ann. 259 (1982), and subsequent papers; not read for this plan). Arthur's Clay introduction §27 (p. 192 ff.) states that the transfer conjecture at archimedean places was established by Shelstad and motivated the general transfer factors; recorded as a source-access gap.

(c) Labesse §3.5: Propositions 3.5.2–3.5.4 establish K-finite base-change transfer at archimedean places using the twisted trace Paley–Wiener theorem of Clozel–Delorme, and Proposition 3.5.6 for complex groups.
acceptance: For the principal datum the transfer is the identity on stable orbital integrals.
For G = SL_2(ℝ) and H = U(1): the κ-character Θ_{D_k^+} − Θ_{D_k^−} is, up to the sign fixed by the transfer factor normalization, the transfer of a character of U(1) (Shelstad's character identity).

sources.match: For archimedean places the Langlands–Shelstad transfer conjecture was established by Shelstad, whose results for real groups motivated the general transfer factors.
K-finite transfer for base change at archimedean places through the twisted Paley–Wiener theorem.

nodes.title: Pseudo-coefficients and Euler–Poincaré functions at the real place
nodes.statement: Let G be connected reductive over ℝ with A_G the split component of the centre, ξ an irreducible finite-dimensional algebraic representation of G_ℂ with central character χ on A_G(ℝ)^0, and q(G) = ½ dim(G(ℝ)/K_∞A_G(ℝ)^0). Assume G(ℝ) has discrete series modulo A_G(ℝ)^0 (equivalently a maximal ℝ-torus anisotropic modulo A_G). (a) (Clozel–Delorme; imported from AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.6, targets AS.6.16a–AS.6.17 of its package, which moved them below this roadmap in the upstream order) For each discrete series π (modulo the centre) there is a pseudo-coefficient φ_π ∈ C_c^∞(G(ℝ), χ⁻¹), K-finite, with tr π′(φ_π) = 1 if π′ ≅ π and 0 for every other irreducible tempered π′ with the same central character, and tr π′(φ_π) given by the Euler–Poincaré pairing for non-tempered π′; AS.6 also supplies a test function with tr π′ = Σ_i (−1)^i dim H^i(𝔤, K_∞; π′ ⊗ ξ) for every finite-length π′. (b) For the L-packet Π(ξ^∨) of discrete series with the infinitesimal character of ξ^∨, the Euler–Poincaré function φ_ξ = |Π(ξ^∨)|⁻¹ Σ_{π ∈ Π(ξ^∨)} φ_π satisfies tr π′(φ_ξ) = (−1)^{q(G)} |Π(ξ^∨)|⁻¹ Σ_i (−1)^i dim H^i(𝔤, K_∞; π′ ⊗ ξ) for every irreducible admissible π′ with the given central character. Put f_ξ = (−1)^{q(G)} |Π(ξ^∨)| φ_ξ (Kottwitz's Euler–Poincaré function, tr π′(f_ξ) = Σ_i (−1)^i dim H^i(𝔤, K_∞; π′ ⊗ ξ)). The orbital integrals of f_ξ vanish at regular semisimple elements that are not elliptic, and at an elliptic semisimple γ, O_γ(f_ξ) = (−1)^{q(G_γ)} vol(Ḡ_γ(ℝ)/A_G(ℝ)^0)⁻¹ tr ξ(γ), with Ḡ_γ the inner form of G_γ that is compact modulo A_G, its Haar measure transported from that of G_γ(ℝ), and q(G_γ) defined like q(G); for regular elliptic γ the sign is 1, and SO_γ(f_ξ) is the sum of these values over the rational classes in the stable class of γ, with the signs of ET.1/kappa-and-stable-orbital-integrals. (c) The construction applies to every inner form of a quasi-split group of arbitrary signature at ∞ (needed for the unitary groups of Caraiani–Scholze), and to a twisted space (Labesse's Lefschetz functions for base change).
hypotheses: G connected reductive over ℝ with discrete series modulo the centre
ξ irreducible algebraic
proofSteps: (a) is imported from AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.6 (requested; AS.6.16a–AS.6.17 of its package, after Clozel–Delorme 1990 §5.2). Clozel–Delorme's invariant Paley–Wiener theorem (Invent. Math. 77 (1984); Ann. Sci. ÉNS 1990) gives functions with prescribed tempered traces; not read, recalled by Shin (p. 18–19: credits Clozel–Delorme for existence) and Arthur (§24).

(b) The Euler–Poincaré property follows from Wigner's lemma (AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups:AF.4/wigner-lemma) and Vogan–Zuckerman (AF.4/vogan-zuckerman), with q(G) as in AF.4/l0-q0-invariants. Orbital integrals at elliptic elements: for regular elliptic γ with centralizer T, O_γ(φ_π) = vol(T(ℝ)/A_G(ℝ)^0)⁻¹ Θ_π(γ⁻¹) (Weyl integration formula and the orthogonality of discrete series characters), and Σ_{π ∈ Π(ξ^∨)} Θ_π(γ⁻¹) = (−1)^{q(G)} tr ξ(γ) on the compact Cartan, so O_γ(f_ξ) = vol(T(ℝ)/A_G(ℝ)^0)⁻¹ tr ξ(γ); at a singular elliptic γ the sign (−1)^{q(G_γ)} of Arthur's global term (24.4) appears, which for central γ is (−1)^{q(G)}, the sign of f_ξ(1) = (−1)^{q(G)} Σ_π d(π) with d(π) the formal degrees; the discrete series characters vanish on non-elliptic tori after summing over the packet (Arthur §24 (24.2)–(24.4); Shin (3.12), (3.14)).
(c) The construction does not use quasi-splitness; the arbitrary-signature case is required by Caraiani–Scholze (compact paper, §5.2, p. 735; extraction item PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17/149).
acceptance: For SL_2(ℝ) and ξ trivial, tr 1(φ_ξ) = −1 and tr D_2^±(φ_ξ) = 1/2.
For compact G(ℝ), f_ξ = vol(G(ℝ))⁻¹ tr ξ and O_γ(f_ξ) = vol(G_γ(ℝ))⁻¹ tr ξ(γ).
Orbital integrals of f_ξ vanish at regular non-elliptic elements.

sources.match: Pseudo-coefficients φ_π of discrete series, the averaged function φ_{φ_H} over an L-packet (an Euler–Poincaré function), q(G), and the credit to Clozel–Delorme for existence and to Labesse for the twisted analogue.
Discrete series characters on elliptic tori, the function Φ′_M(μ, γ) built from them and the global term χ(M_γ) with q(M_γ).

sources.locator: arXiv v1: §5.2, p. 74; §5.3, pp. 75–76 (published Annals pp. 735, 737–738, not read)
sources.match: The archimedean test functions as precise linear combinations of Euler–Poincaré functions and pseudo-coefficients, Labesse's Lefschetz functions for base change, and the remark that the inner form at infinity is more general than the Harris–Taylor signature of Shin's paper (extraction item PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17/149).

uses.how: transfer of φ_ξ to endoscopic groups

AS.6 owns pseudo-coefficients and the Euler–Poincaré trace identity (AS.6.16a–AS.6.17 of its package, moved below this roadmap in the upstream order); this node imports them and adds the packet averages, their orbital integrals and the inner-form and twisted versions that endoscopic transfer uses
the infinity component of the test functions in the simple twisted trace formula

tests.name: eulerPoincare_trace_trivial
tests.statement: For G = SL_2(ℝ) and ξ trivial: q(G) = 1, Π(ξ^∨) = {D_2^+, D_2^−}, the trivial representation has (𝔤, K)-cohomology ℂ in degrees 0 and 2, so tr 1(φ_ξ) = (−1)·2/2 = −1, while tr D_2^±(φ_ξ) = (−1)·(−1)/2 = 1/2.

tests.statement: tr π(φ_π) = 1 and tr π′(φ_π) = 0 for tempered π′ ≇ π with the same central character (the property of AS.6.16a, checked on the imported functions).

tests.statement: If G(ℝ) is compact (A_G trivial), q(G) = 0, Π(ξ^∨) = {ξ^∨} and f_ξ = vol(G(ℝ))⁻¹ tr ξ, so O_γ(f_ξ) = vol(G_γ(ℝ))⁻¹ tr ξ(γ) by Schur orthogonality.

tests.name: eulerPoincare_sl2_elliptic

tests.statement: O_γ(φ_ξ) = 0 for γ regular semisimple non-elliptic (e.g. hyperbolic elements of SL_2(ℝ)), so φ_ξ is not a positive multiple of a function concentrated near the identity.

nodes.title: Transfer of Euler–Poincaré functions to endoscopic groups
nodes.statement: Let G be a connected reductive group over ℝ with discrete series modulo the centre, (H, s, η) an elliptic endoscopic datum (so H(ℝ) also has discrete series), ξ irreducible algebraic and φ_ξ the Euler–Poincaré function (ET.1/pseudocoefficients). Then a transfer of φ_ξ to H is an explicit linear combination Σ_{φ_H} c(φ_H) φ_{φ_H} of the averaged pseudo-coefficients φ_{φ_H} of the discrete L-packets of H(ℝ), over the discrete parameters φ_H with η∘φ_H equivalent to the parameter of Π(ξ^∨); each coefficient c(φ_H) is a sign times a pairing ⟨a, s⟩ determined by Shelstad's character identities and the normalization of the transfer factor (Kottwitz's construction). For G a unitary similitude group of Harris–Taylor or arbitrary signature at ∞ the coefficients are those of Shin's Lemma 3.7 with (3.13)–(3.15), and the resulting functions are Caraiani–Scholze's φ^{n⃗}_∞.
hypotheses: G over ℝ with discrete series; (H, s, η) elliptic
the transfer factor normalization of ET.1/local-transfer-factor
proofSteps: Kottwitz's construction (Kottwitz, 'Shimura varieties and λ-adic representations', 1990, §7; not read) via Shelstad's character identities for discrete series (ET.1/real-transfer (b)); the explicit form used here is Shin's Lemma 3.7 and its proof (pp. 18–19) and Caraiani–Scholze §5.2.
Twisted analogue for base change: Labesse's Lefschetz functions (Shin p. 19; Caraiani–Scholze compact §5.3).
acceptance: For the principal datum the transfer of φ_ξ is e(G)·φ_ξ^{G*}, the Euler–Poincaré function of the quasi-split inner form (Kottwitz sign).
For U(1,1) and H = U(1)×U(1), the transfer is a signed sum over the two discrete parameters of H lifting the parameter of ξ.

sources.match: The transfer φ^H_π of pseudo-coefficients, the trace identity and the Δ-transfer statement for unitary similitude groups.
Kottwitz's function h_{H∞} as a sum of pseudo-coefficients for the endoscopic groups in the Igusa stable trace formula.
The functions φ^{n⃗}_∞ and f^{n⃗}_∞ for inner forms of arbitrary signature; they are base-change matching.

nodes.title: The Chevalley quotient and the characteristic map
nodes.statement: Let k be a field and G a connected reductive group over k, split over k̄ with maximal torus T, Lie algebras 𝔤 ⊇ 𝔱 and Weyl group W, and assume char(k) does not divide |W|. (a) (Chevalley restriction) Restriction of functions gives an isomorphism k[𝔤]^G ≅ k[𝔱]^W, and k[𝔱]^W is a polynomial algebra on homogeneous generators a_1, …, a_r of degrees e_1, …, e_r (the exponents plus one); put 𝔠 = Spec k[𝔱]^W ≅ 𝔸^r, with the G_m-action of weights e_i, and χ : 𝔤 → 𝔠 the characteristic map. (b) χ is smooth exactly on the open subset 𝔤^reg of regular elements, and 𝔤^reg → 𝔠 is surjective; the discriminant divisor 𝔇 ⊂ 𝔠 is the image of the root hyperplanes and 𝔠^rs = 𝔠 \ 𝔇 parametrizes regular semisimple stable classes: for any field extension K/k, χ induces a bijection between stable conjugacy classes of regular semisimple elements of 𝔤(K) and 𝔠^rs(K) (for G quasi-split). (c) (Outer twists) If G is the quasi-split form over a scheme X attached to an Out(G_0)-torsor ρ_G (for a split pinned G_0), the quotient 𝔠 and χ descend to X as 𝔠 = ρ_G ∧^{Out} 𝔠_0, and the G_m-action twisted by a line bundle D gives the vector bundle (or cone) 𝔠_D = 𝔠 ∧^{G_m} D^× over X. For G = GL_n, 𝔠 = 𝔸^n with χ the non-leading coefficients of the (monic, degree n) characteristic polynomial, and 𝔇 is the zero locus of the discriminant of the characteristic polynomial.
hypotheses: k a field with char(k) ∤ |W| (Ngô's standing hypothesis)
G connected reductive over k, quasi-split over X for (c)
proofSteps: (a) Chevalley's restriction theorem and the polynomiality of invariants of the reflection group W when char(k) ∤ |W| (Ngô Théorème 1.1.1, p. 9).

(b) Kostant's smoothness criterion for χ on 𝔤^reg (Ngô Lemme 1.1.2, p. 10); the stable-class parametrization uses ET.0/semisimple-conjugacy and the Kostant section (ET.2b/kostant-section) for existence of rational points in each fibre.
(c) Descent along the Out-torsor (Ngô Définition 1.3.1 and §§1.3.2–1.3.3, p. 11).
acceptance: For GL_n, 𝔠 = 𝔸^n and χ is the characteristic polynomial.
For SL_2, 𝔠 = 𝔸^1 with χ of weight 2 and discriminant {0}.
χ is smooth on 𝔤^reg and not at 0.

sources.match: Chevalley's isomorphism k[V]^G = k[D]^W with homogeneous generators, the characteristic polynomial map χ : V → 𝔠 smooth on the regular locus, and quasi-split forms over X attached to Out(G)-torsors.

uses.how: the Hitchin base is the space of sections of 𝔠_D
stable classes in 𝔤(F) are points of 𝔠^rs(F)
the endoscopic map 𝔠_H → 𝔠

nodes.title: The Kostant section
nodes.statement: In the setting of ET.2b/chevalley-quotient (char(k) ∤ |W|, G split with a pinning, regular nilpotent e = Σ_{α simple} X_α and an 𝔰𝔩_2-triple (e, h, f)), the affine subspace e + 𝔤^f maps isomorphically to 𝔠 under χ, giving a section ε : 𝔠 → 𝔤^reg of χ with image in the regular locus (Kostant). It is equivariant for the G_m-action on 𝔠 with weights e_i and the action of G_m on 𝔤 combining homotheties with the adjoint action of the cocharacter 2ρ^∨ (equivalently of ρ^∨ after passing to the double cover of G_m); this is why, over a curve, ε globalizes only after choosing a square root D′ of D (D′^{⊗2} ≅ D), giving the Kostant–Hitchin section ε_D : 𝔠_D → 𝔤_D^reg. Every regular element X of 𝔤(K) is G(K̄)-conjugate to ε(χ(X)). For K a field, G quasi-split and a ∈ 𝔠^rs(K), sending γ = Ad(g)ε(a) ∈ χ^{-1}(a)(K) to the class of σ ↦ g⁻¹σ(g) is a bijection from the G(K)-conjugacy classes in χ^{-1}(a)(K) onto ker[H^1(K, J_a) → H^1(K, G)], and the isomorphism classes of pairs (E, φ) (E a G-torsor over K, φ ∈ ad(E) with χ(φ) = a) are in bijection with H^1(K, J_a) (Ngô §§1.5.1–1.5.2; ET.2b/regular-centralizer). For G = GL_n, ε(a) is the companion matrix of the polynomial with coefficients a.
hypotheses: char(k) ∤ |W| (Ngô's standing assumption)
G split with a pinning (descends to quasi-split G with the Out-torsor)
proofSteps: Kostant's theorem: χ restricted to e + 𝔤^f is an isomorphism onto 𝔠 (Ngô Lemme 1.2.1, p. 10; section (1.2.2), p. 11).
Equivariance and the square root: Ngô §4.2.4 (p. 63) and Lemme 2.2.5 (p. 34).
Classes in a stable class: Ngô §§1.5.1–1.5.2 (pp. 14–15), using that [𝔤^reg/G] → 𝔠 is a gerbe banded by J and neutralized by ε (ET.2b/regular-centralizer (b)).
acceptance: For GL_n, ε(a) is the companion matrix, with characteristic polynomial a.
ε(0) is a regular nilpotent element.
Over a curve, ε globalizes after choosing a square root of D.

nodes.title: The regular centralizer group scheme
nodes.statement: In the setting of ET.2b/chevalley-quotient (char(k) ∤ |W|), let I → 𝔤 be the group scheme of centralizers. (a) There is a unique smooth commutative group scheme J → 𝔠 with a G-equivariant isomorphism χ^*J|_{𝔤^reg} ≅ I|_{𝔤^reg}, and it extends to a homomorphism χ^*J → I over all of 𝔤 (Ngô Lemme 2.1.1). (b) The morphism [𝔤^reg/G] → 𝔠 is a gerbe banded by J, neutralized by the Kostant section (Proposition 2.2.1). (c) If the centre of G is connected the fibres of J are connected. (d) (Galois description, after Donagi–Gaitsgory) With π : 𝔱 → 𝔠 the finite flat W-cover, there is a canonical homomorphism J → J^1 := (π_*(T × 𝔱))^W, an isomorphism over 𝔠^rs and identifying J with an open subgroup scheme J′ of J^1 whose fibres have the same identity component (Propositions 2.4.2, 2.4.7, Corollaire 2.4.8). (e) For an endoscopic datum with map ν : 𝔠_H → 𝔠 there is a homomorphism μ : ν^*J → J_H (Proposition 2.5.1). (f) For a ∈ 𝔠(X) the pullback J_a is a smooth commutative group scheme over X; over the open where a is regular semisimple, J_a = π_a ∧^W T for the cameral W-torsor π_a (Lemme 1.4.3, (1.4.2)), and over all of X, J_a is an open subgroup of (π_{a,*}(T × X̃_a))^W with the same identity component, by (d).
hypotheses: char(k) ∤ |W|
proofSteps: (a) Descend I|_{𝔤^reg}, which is commutative and smooth over 𝔤^reg, along the smooth surjection χ|_{𝔤^reg} using the transitivity of the G-action on fibres (Ngô Lemme 2.1.1, p. 32).
(b) Ngô Proposition 2.2.1 (p. 33); (c) Proposition 2.3.1 (p. 34) and Corollaire 2.3.2 (p. 35).
(d) Ngô §2.4: Lemme 2.4.1 (smoothness of J^1, using |W| invertible), Proposition 2.4.2 (p. 36), Proposition 2.4.7 (p. 39), Corollaire 2.4.8 (p. 40).
(e) Ngô Proposition 2.5.1 (p. 40); (f) Lemme 1.4.3 and (1.4.2), p. 14.
acceptance: For GL_n, J_a is the unit group of k[t]/(P_a(t)).
Over 𝔠^rs, J is a torus.
J is not the full centralizer at non-regular elements (at X = 0 the centralizer is G).

sources.locator: §2.1, Lemme 2.1.1 (p. 32); §2.2, Proposition 2.2.1 (p. 33); §2.3, Proposition 2.3.1 and Corollaire 2.3.2 (pp. 34–35); §2.4, Lemme 2.4.1, Propositions 2.4.2 and 2.4.7, Corollaire 2.4.8 (pp. 35–40); §2.5, Proposition 2.5.1 (p. 40); §1.4, Lemme 1.4.3 and (1.4.2) (p. 14)

nodes.title: The Hitchin moduli stack, base and fibration
nodes.statement: Let k = 𝔽_q, X a smooth projective geometrically connected curve over k of genus g, G a quasi-split reductive group scheme over X attached to an Out-torsor ρ_G (ET.2b/chevalley-quotient (c)), with char(k) ∤ |W|, and D a line bundle on X (in Ngô's applications D = D′^{⊗2} with deg D > 2g; the carrier is defined for every D, including the canonical bundle ω_X and D = O_X, which Yu's counting needs). The Hitchin moduli stack M = M_{G,D} assigns to a k-scheme S the groupoid of pairs (E, φ) with E a G-torsor on X × S (an S-point of Bun_G, GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands:GS.0) and φ ∈ H^0(X × S, ad(E) ⊗ D). The Hitchin base A = A_{G,D} = H^0(X, 𝔠_D) is a finite-dimensional affine space over k, and f : M → A sends (E, φ) to χ(φ). Properties: (a) M is an algebraic stack locally of finite type over k: over Bun_G it is the stack of sections of the coherent sheaf ad(E) ⊗ D, and the restriction of f to the anisotropic locus is of finite type (ET.2b/anisotropic-locus); (b) if deg D > 2g − 2 and G is split, A = ⊕_i H^0(X, D^{⊗e_i}) has dimension Σ_i (e_i deg D + 1 − g) = (#Φ^+ + r) deg D + r(1 − g) by Riemann–Roch (Ngô Lemme 4.4.1, which also covers the quasi-split case), and the open A^♥ of a whose image meets 𝔠^rs generically is non-empty when deg D > 2g; (c) M is smooth at every point (E, φ) with χ(φ) ∈ A^♥ when deg D > 2g − 2, and at every point with χ(φ) ∈ A^ani when deg D = 2g − 2 (Ngô Théorème 4.12.1: the obstruction group H^1(X, ad(E, φ)) vanishes there); (d) the Kostant–Hitchin section A → M (after choosing D′ with D′^{⊗2} = D) lands in the regular locus M^reg.
hypotheses: k = 𝔽_q, X smooth projective geometrically connected of genus g
G quasi-split over X with char(k) ∤ |W|
D a line bundle; the listed properties need the stated degree bounds
proofSteps: Algebraicity: M → Bun_G is the stack of sections of the coherent sheaf ad(E) ⊗ D, representable by an abelian cone (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.4 linear stacks and the Artin criterion of A0-extension); Bun_G is algebraic and locally of finite type (GS.0/bun-g-of-the-global-curve).
Dimension and non-emptiness: Riemann–Roch on X for the line bundles of weights e_i (upstream AlgebraicCurves Layer 4; Ngô Lemme 4.4.1, p. 64; §4.5, p. 67; Proposition 4.6.1, p. 69).
Smoothness: deformation theory of Higgs pairs and the vanishing of the obstruction H^1 under the degree hypothesis, at points over A^♥ (Ngô Théorème 4.12.1, p. 84).
The Kostant–Hitchin section: ET.2b/kostant-section globalized with D′ (Ngô §4.2.4, p. 63).
acceptance: For GL_1, M = Pic_X × H^0(X, D).
For GL_2 and deg D = d > 2g − 2, dim A = 3d + 2 − 2g.
The fibre over 0 contains Bun_G (φ = 0), so M is not of finite type.

nodes.title: Boundedness of Higgs sheaves through a good pair of line bundles
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve over a field k, Ω_X its canonical bundle, and α = (r, d) a class (rank r ≥ 1, degree d). A Higgs sheaf of class α is a coherent sheaf V of rank r and degree d with θ ∈ Hom(V, V ⊗ Ω_X); a Higgs subsheaf is a subsheaf W with θ(W) ⊆ W ⊗ Ω_X; (V, θ) is semistable if μ(W) ≤ μ(V) for every proper Higgs subsheaf (μ the slope), and a Higgs subsheaf with μ(W) > μ(V) is destabilizing. A coherent sheaf V is strongly generated by a line bundle L if Ext^1(L, V) = 0 and the evaluation L ⊗ Hom(L, V) → V is surjective. Then there is a pair of line bundles (L_1, L_2) ∈ Pic^{−n}(X) × Pic^{−m}(X) (n, m depending on α and the genus) such that: (a) every semistable Higgs bundle of class α is strongly generated by L_1 and by L_2; (b) every indecomposable vector bundle of class α is strongly generated by L_1 and by L_2; (c) for every coherent sheaf V of class α and every epimorphism φ : L_1 ⊗ V′ → V (V′ a vector space), ker(φ) is strongly generated by L_2; (d) every unstable Higgs sheaf of class α has a destabilizing Higgs subsheaf strongly generated by L_1 and L_2. Consequently the stacks of semistable Higgs bundles and of indecomposable bundles of class α, and the Hitchin moduli stack with the canonical twist restricted to semistable objects, admit presentations as quotients of open subschemes of Quot schemes (Álvarez-Cónsul–King construction) and are of finite type.
hypotheses: X smooth projective geometrically connected over a field k
Higgs fields twisted by the canonical bundle Ω_X
class α of positive rank
proofSteps: Bound the slopes of subsheaves of semistable Higgs bundles and of indecomposable bundles of class α (Harder–Narasimhan filtrations and the bound on Hom from destabilizing pieces); choose L_1, L_2 of sufficiently negative degree so that Ext^1(L_i, V) = H^1(X, L_i^{-1} ⊗ V) = 0 by Serre duality and V ⊗ L_i^{-1} is globally generated (Schiffmann, proof of Lemma 6.1).

Finite type: strongly generated sheaves of class α are quotients of L_1^{⊕N} with N = χ(L_1^{-1} ⊗ V), parametrized by an open subscheme of a Quot scheme (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.2/quot-projectivity).
acceptance: For r = 1, every Higgs bundle of class (1, d) is semistable, and a line bundle M of degree d is strongly generated by every line bundle L with deg L ≤ d − 2g: then deg(L^{-1}M) ≥ 2g, so Ext^1(L, M) = H^1(X, L^{-1}M) = 0 and L^{-1}M is globally generated.

On X = ℙ^1 (Ω = O(−2)) every indecomposable vector bundle is a line bundle, so (b) is vacuous for r = 2; for V = O(a) ⊕ O(−a) with a ≥ 1 there is no nonzero component O(a) → O(−a) ⊗ Ω = O(−a − 2), so O(a) is a destabilizing Higgs subsheaf, and the only semistable Higgs bundle of class (2, 0) is (O ⊕ O, 0).

sources.locator: arXiv v2 (4 October 2014, no printed page numbers): §6.2 and the definition of strong generation in §6.3 (PDF p. 22); Lemma 6.1 (PDF p. 23)

nodes.title: Cameral covers and spectral curves
nodes.statement: In the setting of ET.2b/hitchin-moduli-stack, for a ∈ A(k̄) viewed as a map a : X̄ → 𝔠_D, the cameral cover is the finite flat W-equivariant cover π_a : X̃_a = X̄ ×_{𝔠_D} 𝔱_D → X̄. Let A^♥ ⊆ A be the open subset of a with a(X̄) ⊄ 𝔇_D (generically regular semisimple). For a ∈ A^♥, X̃_a is reduced and is a W-torsor over the open U_a = a^{-1}(𝔠_D^rs); Ngô Proposition 4.5.4 gives its connectedness under the hypotheses stated there. The regular centralizer J_a = a^*J is described by the cameral cover: J_a ⊆ (π_{a,*}(T × X̃_a))^W with equality of identity components (ET.2b/regular-centralizer (d)). For G = GL_n the cameral cover is the Galois closure of the spectral curve Y_a ⊂ V(D) (the total space of D), Y_a = {t : t^n + a_1 t^{n−1} + … + a_n = 0}, a finite cover of X̄ of degree n; J_a = R_{Y_a/X̄} G_m and M_a is the stack of torsion-free rank-one sheaves on Y_a (Beauville–Narasimhan–Ramanan) when Y_a is integral.
hypotheses: the setting of ET.2b/hitchin-moduli-stack
a ∈ A^♥ for the torsor and reducedness statements
proofSteps: Base change of the finite flat W-cover 𝔱 → 𝔠 (Ngô §1.4 and §4.5).
Reducedness and the generic W-torsor structure: Ngô Lemme 4.5.1 (p. 67); connectedness: Proposition 4.5.4 (p. 68).

The spectral description for GL_n: J_a is the Weil restriction of G_m from the spectral curve, and M_a is identified with rank-one torsion-free sheaves via pushforward (Ngô §4 recalls this as the motivating example).
acceptance: For GL_1 the cameral cover is X̄ itself.
For GL_2 and a = (0, a_2) with simple zeros, the spectral curve has genus 2g − 1 + deg D.
Over the regular semisimple locus the cameral cover is a W-torsor.

nodes.title: The Picard stack acting on Hitchin fibres
nodes.statement: In the setting of ET.2b/hitchin-moduli-stack, for a ∈ A(S) let P_a be the Picard groupoid of J_a-torsors on X × S; as a varies these form a Picard stack P → A. Via the homomorphism χ^*J → I (ET.2b/regular-centralizer (a)), J_a acts on every (E, φ) ∈ M_a by automorphisms, so P acts on M over A by twisting (E, φ) by a J_a-torsor. (a) The regular open M^reg (φ regular everywhere) is a P-torsor over A, trivialized by the Kostant–Hitchin section (Ngô Proposition 4.3.3). (b) P is smooth over A^♥ (Proposition 4.4.2). (c) For a ∈ A^♥(k̄), the group of connected components π_0(P_a) is a finitely generated abelian group described through the cameral cover: with P′_a the stack of J′_a-torsors, P′_a → P_a is surjective with finite kernel, and the Cartier duals of π_0(P′_a) and π_0(P_a) are the diagonalizable groups Ĉ^{W̃_a} and Ĉ(I_a, W_a) attached to the monodromy of the cameral cover (Ngô Lemme 4.10.1, Proposition 4.10.2). (d) The irreducible components of the fibre M_a (a ∈ A^ani) are indexed by π_0(P_a) (Corollaire 4.14.3).
hypotheses: the setting of ET.2b/hitchin-moduli-stack; (b)–(d) for a ∈ A^♥ (resp. A^ani)
proofSteps: Define P_a and the action using χ^*J → I (Ngô §4.3.1, p. 63); the torsor statement (a) uses that J ≅ I on the regular locus (Proposition 4.3.3, p. 64).
Smoothness (b): the deformation theory of J_a-torsors is governed by H^1(X, Lie J_a), which has constant dimension over A^♥ (Proposition 4.4.2, p. 65).
(c) Ngô §4.10, Lemme 4.10.1 and Proposition 4.10.2 (p. 78): compute π_0 through the Néron model and the cameral monodromy.
(d) Corollaire 4.14.3 (p. 88), from the product formula and the local statement on components of affine Springer fibres.
acceptance: For GL_1, P_a = Pic_X and π_0(P_a) = ℤ.
For GL_n with integral spectral curve, P_a = Pic_{Y_a}.
For SL_2 and a in the image of the endoscopic base of a connected étale double cover X′ → X, π_0(P_a) carries the nontrivial character attached to X′.

nodes.title: The anisotropic locus: properness and Deligne–Mumford structure
nodes.statement: In the setting of ET.2b/hitchin-moduli-stack with deg D > 2g and D = D′^{⊗2}: (a) the anisotropic locus A^ani ⊆ A^♥, the set of a ∈ A^♥ for which π_0(P_a) is finite (equivalently the cameral cover has no monodromy-invariant cocharacters modulo the centre), is open (Ngô Lemme 6.1.1, §6.1); (b) P^ani = P|_{A^ani} is a separated smooth Deligne–Mumford stack of finite type over A^ani; M^ani = f^{-1}(A^ani) is a separated smooth Deligne–Mumford stack and f^ani : M^ani → A^ani is proper (Proposition 6.1.5); (c) for a ∈ A^ani(k̄) the fibre M_a is a proper Deligne–Mumford stack and the quotient of the product of local affine Springer fibres by the local symmetry groups is proper (Proposition 4.13.1); (d) if the centre of G is not finite one restricts to a fixed degree component (or quotients by a lattice of the centre) to obtain finite type.

char(k) ∤ |W|
G semisimple, or a fixed central degree component

(b) Ngô Proposition 6.1.5 (p. 113): finiteness of π_0 and of stabilizers gives the DM property; properness by the valuative criterion using the product formula and the properness of the local quotients (Kazhdan–Lusztig).
(c) Ngô Proposition 4.13.1 (pp. 86–87); smoothness of M at anisotropic points with deg D = 2g − 2 is Théorème 4.12.1 (ET.2b/hitchin-moduli-stack (c)).

For G = SL_2 and a with irreducible spectral curve, a ∈ A^ani and M_a is a compactified Prym, proper.

nodes.title: Affine Springer fibres and their local symmetry groups
nodes.statement: Let k be a finite field (or k̄), F_v = k((ε_v)) with ring 𝒪_v, G a reductive group over 𝒪_v (quasi-split, split over an unramified extension; char(k) ∤ |W|), Gr_v = G(F_v)/G(𝒪_v) the affine Grassmannian, an ind-scheme over k (the fibre at v of the Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian of GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands:GS.1), and a ∈ 𝔠(𝒪_v) ∩ 𝔠^rs(F_v) with γ_a = ε(a) the Kostant section value. The affine Springer fibre M_v(a) is the functor of pairs (E, φ) on Spec 𝒪_v × S with χ(φ) = a, together with an isomorphism with (E_0, γ_a) over F_v; it is represented by the closed sub-ind-scheme {g ∈ Gr_v : Ad(g)^{-1}γ_a ∈ 𝔤(𝒪_v)} (Ngô Proposition 3.2.1). (a) (Kazhdan–Lusztig) M_v(a)^red is locally of finite type, and the local symmetry group P_v(J_a) (the group ind-scheme of J_a-torsors on Spec 𝒪_v trivialized over F_v) acts on it; a free abelian group Λ of finite rank in P_v(J_a) acts freely with projective quotient M_v(a)^red/Λ (Proposition 3.4.1). (b) (Dimension; Bezrukavnikov) The regular open M_v^reg(a) is a P_v(J_a)-torsor, dense in M_v(a), and dim M_v(a) = dim P_v(J_a) = δ_v(a) = (d_v(a) − c_v(a))/2 with d_v(a) = val(Δ(a)) the valuation of the discriminant and c_v(a) the drop of split rank (Propositions 3.7.1, 3.7.5). (c) The irreducible components of M_v(a) are in bijection with π_0(P_v(J_a)) (Corollaire 3.10.2). These are algebraic loop objects over k((ε)), not Witt-vector or diamond Grassmannians.
hypotheses: F_v = k((ε_v)) of equal characteristic
char(k) ∤ |W|
a regular semisimple over F_v and integral
proofSteps: Representability as a closed sub-ind-scheme of Gr_v and local finiteness (Kazhdan–Lusztig), recalled in Ngô Proposition 3.2.1 (p. 43); the affine Grassmannian itself is requested from GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands:GS.1.
Symmetries and the projective quotient: Ngô §3.3 (p. 45) and Proposition 3.4.1 (p. 47).
Dimension: Ngô Proposition 3.7.1 (p. 50), Corollaire 3.7.2 (p. 51), Proposition 3.7.5 (p. 52), via the Néron model of J_a (§3.8, Lemme 3.8.1, Corollaire 3.8.3).
Components: Ngô §§3.9–3.10, Corollaire 3.9.6 and Corollaire 3.10.2 (pp. 57–58).
acceptance: If a is regular semisimple modulo ε, δ_v = 0 and M_v(a) is the discrete set X_*(T).
For GL_2 and characteristic polynomial t² − ε^n, δ_v = ⌊n/2⌋.
For γ = diag(ε, −ε), M_v(a) has infinitely many components and its quotient by Λ is projective.

sources.locator: §3.2, Proposition 3.2.1 (p. 43); §3.3 (p. 45); Proposition 3.4.1 (p. 47); §3.7, Propositions 3.7.1, 3.7.5 and Corollaire 3.7.2 (pp. 50–52); §3.8 (pp. 52–54); Corollaires 3.9.6 and 3.10.2 (pp. 57–58)

nodes.title: The product formula for Hitchin fibres
nodes.statement: In the setting of ET.2b/hitchin-moduli-stack and ET.2b/affine-springer-fibre, let a ∈ A^♥(k̄) and U ⊆ X̄ the open subset where a is regular semisimple, with finite complement. Gluing local data along the Kostant section gives a morphism ζ : (∏_{v ∈ X̄ \ U} M_v(a)) ∧^{∏_v P_v(J_a)} P_a → M_a which is a universal homeomorphism (Ngô Proposition 4.13.1). For counting points over k (a ∈ A^ani(k)), with P′ built from the open subgroup J′, there is an equivalence of groupoids [M_a/P′_a] ≅ ∏_{v ∈ X \ U} [M_v(a)/P_v(J′_a)] (Proposition 8.4.2), and stabilizer volumes are recorded by the Néron model of J_a. Consequently dim M_a = dim P_a, and δ_a := dim P_a − dim P_a^{ab} = Σ_v δ_v(a) (the affine part of P_a has dimension the sum of local δ-invariants).
hypotheses: a ∈ A^♥ (homeomorphism) or a ∈ A^ani(k) (point-count form)
proofSteps: Ngô Proposition 4.13.1 (pp. 86–87), citing his earlier 'Fibration de Hitchin et endoscopie' Théorème 4.6 for the equivalence on k̄-points; Proposition 8.4.2 (p. 175) for the point-count form.
The δ formula: the affine part of P_a is the product of the local affine parts (ET.2b/affine-springer-fibre (b)).
acceptance: If a is regular semisimple everywhere (U = X̄), M_a = P_a-torsor and δ_a = 0.
For G = GL_2 and a spectral curve with a single node over v, M_a is a compactified Jacobian, homeomorphic to M_v(a) ∧^{P_v} P_a with δ_a = δ_v(a) = 1.

sources.match: The product formula ζ, a homeomorphism, and its groupoid form for counting points over k in the anisotropic locus.

nodes.title: The δ-stratification and the codimension estimate
nodes.statement: In the setting of ET.2b/hitchin-moduli-stack, for a ∈ A^♥ let δ_a = Σ_v δ_v(a) (ET.2b/product-formula). (a) A^♥ ⊗ k̄ has a unique stratification by locally closed strata A_ψ indexed by the cameral monodromy and local data ψ, on which δ_a is constant; δ is upper semicontinuous: ψ ≥ ψ′ implies δ(ψ) ≤ δ(ψ′) (Ngô Proposition 5.2.4, Lemme 5.3.1). (b) (Local codimension) At a point of a δ-stratum with δ > 0, the local codimension of the stratum in the space of local data is at least δ + 1 (Proposition 5.4.1). (c) (δ-regularity) If deg D is large relative to δ, the stratum A_δ = {a : δ_a = δ} ∩ A^ani has codimension ≥ δ in A^ani (Proposition 5.4.2); hence, for each δ_0, if deg D is large enough, the open A^{≤δ_0} on which the inequality codim A_δ ≥ δ holds for all δ ≤ δ_0 can be used in the support theorem. In characteristic p the estimate is only proved under this degree hypothesis (Ngô notes the issue in §5.4 and §8.6); it is the source of the restriction to an open U ⊂ A^ani in the global argument, with globalization choosing deg D large relative to the δ of the prescribed local data.
hypotheses: deg D large relative to δ (stated for each δ)
char(k) ∤ |W|
proofSteps: (a) Ngô Proposition 5.2.4 (p. 97), §5.3 and Lemme 5.3.1 (p. 98).
(b) Proposition 5.4.1 (p. 101): deformation of local data at points with δ_v > 0.

(c) Proposition 5.4.2 (p. 101), with Proposition 5.1.3 (p. 94) for the degree hypothesis: the evaluation of global sections of 𝔠_D at finitely many points is surjective onto the jets when deg D is large, so local codimensions add up.
acceptance: δ = 0 stratum: a regular semisimple everywhere; codimension 0.
For G = GL_2 the locus of spectral curves with one node has codimension 1 = δ in A when deg D ≥ 2g + 2 (one condition on the discriminant).

sources.match: The stratification of A^♥ by ψ with δ constant on strata, the local codimension bound δ + 1 and the global estimate codim A_δ ≥ δ when deg D is very large relative to δ.

nodes.title: Weak abelian fibrations
nodes.statement: Let k be a finite field (or its algebraic closure) and S a scheme of finite type over k. A weak abelian fibration of relative dimension d is a pair (f : M → S, g : P → S) with: (1) f proper with geometrically reduced fibres of pure dimension d, M smooth over k (Ngô uses M and S smooth, or M a smooth Deligne–Mumford stack); (2) P a smooth commutative group scheme over S with connected fibres of dimension d acting on M over S; (3) the stabilizers of points of M in P are affine (§7.1.2); (4) the Tate module T_{ℚ_ℓ}(P^ab) of the abelian part of the Chevalley decomposition 1 → P^aff_s → P_s → P^ab_s → 1 is polarizable (§7.1.4); (5) (δ-regularity) writing δ_s = dim P^aff_s and S_δ the δ-strata, codim S_δ ≥ δ for all δ (§7.1.3) — P is then called δ-regular. The fibration is used with Q̄_ℓ-coefficients and the perverse cohomology sheaves of f_*Q̄_ℓ, with π_0(P) acting on them through a finite quotient.
hypotheses: k finite (or algebraically closed)
S of finite type
proofSteps: Ngô §7.1 (pp. 122–124): hypotheses 7.1.1–7.1.4 listed as the axioms used in the support theorem; Ngô does not use the name 'weak abelian fibration' in this paper (the term is from his subsequent expositions), and the data here are exactly those hypotheses.
acceptance: An abelian scheme acting on itself is a weak abelian fibration with δ = 0.
The anisotropic Hitchin fibration over its δ-regular open is a weak abelian fibration.
A trivial action of an abelian scheme violates the affine-stabilizer axiom.

sources.match: The hypotheses of the support theorem: f proper flat with geometrically reduced fibres, M and S smooth, P acting with affine stabilizers, δ-regularity of P and polarizability of its Tate module.
