nodes.title: Purity, decomposition and the κ-isotypic parts of the Hitchin cohomology
nodes.statement: In the setting of ET.2b/anisotropic-locus, let f^ani : M^ani → A^ani and K = f^ani_* Q̄_ℓ. (a) K is pure (M^ani smooth, f^ani proper) and, by the decomposition theorem, K ⊗ k̄ is isomorphic to the direct sum of its shifted perverse cohomology sheaves ^pH^n(K), each geometrically semisimple. (b) Over the étale cover Ã^ani of A^ani trivializing the cameral monodromy, the action of π_0(P) on ^pH^n(f̃^ani_* Q̄_ℓ) factors through a finite quotient and gives a decomposition ^pH^n = ⊕_{κ} ^pH^n_κ over the characters κ of that quotient (κ ∈ κ^ani), with ^pH^n_κ supported in Ã_κ ∩ Ã^ani, where Ã_κ is the locus of a whose cameral monodromy fixes κ (Ngô (6.2.5), Proposition 6.2.6). (c) The κ = 1 part is the stable part ^pH^n_st. The decomposition theorem is applied to f^ani with source a smooth separated Deligne–Mumford stack (Ngô Remarque 7.5.1); the atlas's decomposition theorem (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.7) is stated for schemes, and its extension to proper maps from such stacks is requested.
hypotheses: the setting of ET.2b/anisotropic-locus
ℓ ≠ char(k), coefficients Q̄_ℓ
proofSteps: (a) Deligne's theorem that proper direct images of pure complexes are pure (DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.8/proper-direct-image-preserves-purity-6-2-6) and the decomposition theorem of BBD 5.4.5 (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.7/decomposition-theorem), applied as in Ngô §6.2 (p. 113) with Remarque 7.5.1 (p. 149) for Deligne–Mumford stacks.

(b) The homotopy argument: P acts on K, its identity component acts trivially on cohomology sheaves, so π_0(P) acts; over Ã^ani it is a quotient of a constant finitely generated group with finite image (Ngô §6.2, (6.2.5) and Proposition 6.2.6, p. 114; Corollaire 5.7.5, p. 110).
acceptance: For G = GL_n, π_0(P_a) = ℤ for all a and its action on each fixed-degree component is trivial, so only κ = 1 occurs.

For G = SL_2, κ ranges over characters of ℤ/2, and the nontrivial κ-part attached to a connected étale double cover X′ → X is supported on the image of the endoscopic base A_H, where the spectral curves are nodal with normalization X′.

sources.match: Purity and the decomposition theorem for f^ani, the action of π_0(P) and the κ-decomposition of the perverse cohomology with supports in Ã_κ; the extension of the purity/decomposition argument to Deligne–Mumford stacks.

nodes.title: Ngô's support theorem
nodes.statement: Let (f : M → S, P) be a weak abelian fibration of relative dimension d over S of finite type over a finite field (ET.2b/weak-abelian-fibration), with M and S smooth and P δ-regular. (a) (Support inequality) For every geometrically simple perverse constituent K of some ^pH^n(f_*Q̄_ℓ) with support Z, and δ_Z the minimal δ on Z, the amplitude of the cohomology of K at a generic point satisfies amp ≥ 2(d − δ_Z) (Ngô Proposition 7.2.3, after the cohomological amplitude argument of 7.2.2); combined with δ-regularity and relative hard Lefschetz this forces codim Z ≤ δ_Z. (b) (Support theorem) Z is the closure of one of the strata S_σ of the stratification by the monodromy of the Tate module (Théorème 7.1.5), and, with the action of π_0(P), the κ-part has its supports among the strata where κ is fixed (Théorème 7.1.13). (c) (Hitchin case) For the anisotropic Hitchin fibration restricted to the δ-regular open, every support of ^pH^n(f̃^ani_* Q̄_ℓ)_κ is the image Ã_H of the endoscopic Hitchin base of the endoscopic group H attached to κ (Théorème 7.6.6); in particular for κ = 1 the support of the stable part is all of Ã^ani.
hypotheses: (f, P) a weak abelian fibration with M, S smooth and P δ-regular
for (c): the δ-regular open of A^ani (deg D large)
proofSteps: (a) Ngô §7.2 (pp. 130–131): freeness of the cohomology of the fibres over the cohomology of the Tate module of P^ab gives the amplitude bound.

(b) Ngô §7.3 (p. 131 ff.) deduces Théorème 7.1.5 (pp. 124–125) and its κ-version Théorème 7.1.13 (pp. 127–128) from (a), δ-regularity and relative hard Lefschetz (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.7/relative-hard-lefschetz-theorem for the projective case, as in BBD).
(c) Ngô §7.6 (pp. 149–153), Lemme 7.6.5 and Théorème 7.6.6, identifying the strata where κ is fixed with the images of endoscopic Hitchin bases.
acceptance: For an abelian scheme (δ = 0 everywhere), the only support is S itself.

For the compactified Jacobian family of a versal family of integral plane curves, the support theorem recovers that the perverse cohomology has full support (Ngô's argument, cf. Migliorini–Shende for the comparison).

sources.locator: §7.1, Théorème 7.1.5 and Corollaire 7.1.6 (pp. 124–125), Théorème 7.1.13 (pp. 127–128); §7.2, 7.2.2 and Proposition 7.2.3 (pp. 130–131); §7.6, Lemme 7.6.5 and Théorème 7.6.6 (p. 153)
sources.match: The support theorem for weak abelian fibrations, its κ-version, the support inequality amp(α) ≥ 2(d − δ_α), and its application identifying the supports of the κ-parts of the anisotropic Hitchin cohomology with Ã_H.

nodes.title: Geometric stabilization: comparison of κ-parts with stable parts of endoscopic groups
nodes.statement: In the setting of ET.2b/support-theorem, let κ be a character as in ET.2b/kappa-decomposition, (H, κ) the corresponding endoscopic datum over X (determined by κ and the cameral monodromy, Ngô §1.8 and §6.3), ν : Ã_H → Ã the endoscopic map of Hitchin bases (finite and unramified on the anisotropic part over the transverse locus), and r_{G,H}(D) = (#Φ − #Φ_H) deg(D)/2. Then over Ã_H^ani (restricted to the δ-regular open) there is an isomorphism between the semisimplifications of the graded perverse sheaves ν^*(⊕_n ^pH^n(f̃^ani_* Q̄_ℓ)_κ)[2r_{G,H}(D)](r_{G,H}(D)) and ⊕_n ^pH^n(f̃^ani_{H,*} Q̄_ℓ)_st (Ngô Théorème 6.4.3). The proof first establishes the comparison over the transverse (good) locus by point counting — the local identities of ET.2b/hitchin-point-count at the points of Ã_H where the δ of G equals the δ of H plus the explicit contribution — and then extends it to all of Ã_H^ani by the support theorem (both sides have supports exactly Ã_H, so an isomorphism over a dense open of each support extends).
hypotheses: the setting of ET.2b/support-theorem
deg D large (δ-regular open), D = D′^{⊗2}
proofSteps: Transverse locus: Ngô §8.5, Lemme 8.5.1 (p. 178) gives the open set of transversal a_H, and Lemme 8.5.7 (p. 179) the local count identity with q^{deg v · r_{GH,v}(a_H)}; the Chebotarev-type principle that semisimple mixed perverse sheaves on a scheme over 𝔽_q are determined up to semisimplification by their Frobenius traces at closed points (requested from EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.7) gives equality of the semisimplified perverse sheaves on that open.
Extension: ET.2b/support-theorem (c) — every support of either side is Ã_H — so the isomorphism of semisimplifications over a dense open of Ã_H extends (Ngô §§6.4, 7.6–7.7).
Shift r_{G,H}(D): the difference of dimensions of the Hitchin fibres of G and H over Ã_H (Ngô §6.4.2, p. 120).
acceptance: For κ = 1 and H = G the statement is a tautology with r_{G,G} = 0.

For G = SL_2 and H the norm-one torus of a connected étale double cover X′ → X: #Φ − #Φ_H = 2, so r_{G,H}(D) = deg D, and the comparison identifies the nontrivial κ-part over Ã_H with the stable cohomology of the Hitchin fibration of the torus H (whose fibres are torsors under the Picard stack of H-torsors), shifted by 2 deg D and Tate-twisted by deg D.

sources.match: The geometric stabilization: isomorphism between the semisimplifications of the shifted κ-part for G and the stable part for H over Ã_H^ani, its proof over the transverse locus by counting and its extension by the support theorem.

nodes.title: Counting points of Hitchin fibres
nodes.statement: In the setting of ET.2b/anisotropic-locus, for a ∈ A^ani(k) with U ⊆ X the regular semisimple locus of a: (a) (Grothendieck–Lefschetz) the number of k-points of [M_a/P′_a], counted with the weights 1/#Aut and twisted by a character κ of π_0(P_a) (κ-weighted count), equals the alternating trace of Frobenius on the κ-part of the cohomology of M_a (Ngô Proposition 8.1.13); (b) (Local factors) by the product formula in its point-count form (ET.2b/product-formula), the global κ-weighted count of [M_a/P′_a] is the product over v ∈ X \ U of the κ-weighted counts of the local quotients [M_v(a)/P_v(J′_a)] (Propositions 8.4.2–8.4.3); (c) (Endoscopic local identity on the transverse locus) at a point a_H of the transverse open of the endoscopic base (Lemme 8.5.1), the κ-weighted local count for G at v equals q^{deg(v) r_{G,H,v}(a_H)} times the stable local count for H (Lemme 8.5.7), proved by direct comparison of the local affine Springer fibres where the G-discriminant exceeds the H-discriminant only by the resultant. The translation of local κ-weighted counts into κ-orbital integrals is ET.3/orbital-integrals-as-point-counts.
hypotheses: a ∈ A^ani(k)
Grothendieck–Lefschetz for Deligne–Mumford stacks of finite type over k
proofSteps: (a) The Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula for Deligne–Mumford stacks of finite type over 𝔽_q (requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2; the scheme case underlies it), as used by Ngô §8.1 (Proposition 8.1.6 for finiteness, Proposition 8.1.13 for the formula, pp. 157–160).
acceptance: If a is regular semisimple and unramified everywhere, the κ-count is the number of k-points of a torsor under P_a weighted by κ, and the product of local counts is 1.
For G = GL_1 the count of degree-d points is #Pic^d_X(k) = #Pic^0_X(k).

sources.match: The cohomological point count, the product of local κ-weighted counts over the singular points, and the endoscopic local identity on the transverse locus.

nodes.title: Worked examples for the Hitchin fibration
nodes.statement: (1) Torus: for G = T, A = H^0(X, 𝔱 ⊗ D), M = Bun_T × A, P = Bun_T × A, δ = 0, every a is regular semisimple, affine Springer fibres are discrete and the support theorem is trivial. (2) Rank-one degenerating spectral curve: for G = GL_2, a family of spectral curves acquiring one node at v ∈ X has δ_v = 1, M_a is the compactified Jacobian of the nodal curve, P_a is the generalized Jacobian (an extension of the Jacobian of the normalization by G_m), and the product formula expresses M_a through the affine Springer fibre at v (a chain of ℙ^1's modulo ℤ). (3) Nontrivial component character: for G = SL_2 and a = ν(a_H) with H the norm-one torus of a connected étale double cover X′ → X, the spectral curve is nodal with normalization X′ and π_0(P_a) carries the nontrivial character κ attached to X′. (4) Endoscopic Hitchin fibre: for G = SL_2 and H the norm-one torus of a connected étale double cover X′ → X, the endoscopic Hitchin base A_H maps to A by ν, and over its image the nontrivial κ-part of the cohomology is identified (ET.2b/endoscopic-comparison) with the stable cohomology of the H-fibration shifted by 2 deg D.
hypotheses: X smooth projective over 𝔽_q, char ≠ 2 for (3)–(4)
proofSteps: Each example is computed from ET.2b/hitchin-moduli-stack, ET.2b/picard-stack-action, ET.2b/affine-springer-fibre, ET.2b/product-formula and ET.2b/endoscopic-comparison.
acceptance: Each of the four examples is checked as stated.

sources.locator: §§4–7 as cited in the nodes used
sources.match: The constructions from which the examples are computed.

nodes.title: The Lie-algebra fundamental lemma in equal characteristic (Ngô)
nodes.statement: Let k be a finite field with q elements, 𝒪 = k[[ε]], F = k((ε)), G a reductive group scheme over 𝒪 (quasi-split, split over an unramified extension) whose Weyl group order is not divisible by char(k), and (H, κ) an unramified endoscopic datum of G with H the corresponding reductive group scheme over 𝒪. For a ∈ 𝔠_H(𝒪) ∩ 𝔠_H^{G-rs}(F) (G-regular semisimple) with image ν(a) ∈ 𝔠(𝒪), and Haar measures giving the centralizer tori compatible volumes, Δ_G(ν(a)) O^κ_{ν(a)}(1_{𝔤(𝒪)}) = Δ_H(a) SO_a(1_{𝔥(𝒪)}), where 1_{𝔤(𝒪)}, 1_{𝔥(𝒪)} are the characteristic functions of the integral points of the Lie algebras, O^κ is the κ-orbital integral and SO the stable orbital integral (ET.1/kappa-and-stable-orbital-integrals), Δ_G(a) = q^{−val(D_G(a))/2} and Δ_H(a) = q^{−val(D_H(a))/2}; equivalently O^κ_{ν(a)}(1_{𝔤(𝒪)}) = q^{r_{G,H}(a)} SO_a(1_{𝔥(𝒪)}) with r_{G,H}(a) the valuation of the relative discriminant divided by 2. This is the Langlands–Shelstad fundamental lemma for Lie algebras with the transfer factor of ET.1/lie-algebra-transfer-factor normalized by taking as base point of each stable class the value of the Kostant section (ET.2b/kostant-section), which Kottwitz showed agrees with the Langlands–Shelstad normalization for quasi-split G (Ngô §1.11, p. 23). The characteristic hypothesis is char(k) ∤ |W| (Ngô, arXiv v3, Théorème 1); the roadmap's earlier description of this layer quoted the stronger condition p > 2h, which is not the hypothesis of the version read.
hypotheses: k finite, char(k) ∤ |W|
G, H unramified over 𝒪 = k[[ε]] with an unramified endoscopic datum
a G-regular semisimple
proofSteps: Globalize: choose a smooth projective curve X over k, a point v with completion F, a line bundle D = D′^{⊗2} of large degree, and a global a_H ∈ A_H^ani(k) whose germ at v is the given local element and which is regular semisimple and unramified at the other points where needed (Ngô §8.6.1–8.6.4, pp. 182–183; the choice uses deg D > rN + 2g).

Count points: the κ-weighted count of the G-Hitchin fibre and the stable count of the H-Hitchin fibre are products of local counts (ET.2b/hitchin-point-count), and each local count is a volume times a κ-orbital (resp. stable) integral of the unit function (ET.3/orbital-integrals-as-point-counts).

Compare cohomologies: the geometric stabilization (ET.2b/endoscopic-comparison) identifies the κ-part of the G-cohomology over Ã_H with the stable part of the H-cohomology, shifted and twisted by r_{G,H}(D); taking traces of Frobenius gives a global identity of products of local terms.

Isolate the local factor at v: at the other singular points the local identity holds by induction or by the transverse-locus identity (ET.2b/hitchin-point-count (c)), so the local identity at v follows (Ngô §8.6, proof of Théorème 1.11.1, p. 182 ff.).
acceptance: For H = G (κ = 1) both sides are equal by definition (r = 0).

For G = SL_2 and H the norm-one torus of an unramified quadratic extension: O^κ_{ν(a)}(1_{𝔰𝔩_2(𝒪)}) = q^{val(D_G(a))/2} times the volume of the integral points of the torus, a statement checkable by counting lattices (the case Langlands verified by hand).
For unitary groups the statement specializes to Laumon–Ngô's theorem (ET.3/unitary-fundamental-lemma).

sources.match: The fundamental lemma for Lie algebras of unramified groups over k((ε)) with char(k) not dividing |W|, in the forms with q^{r_{GH}} and with Δ_G, Δ_H; the globalization of local data and the deduction from the geometric stabilization.
The statement of the fundamental lemma for unit elements and its reduction to an identity in the Lie algebra.

nodes.title: Local κ-weighted point counts are κ-orbital integrals
nodes.statement: Let k = 𝔽_q, v a closed point of a curve over k with completion F_v = k(v)((ε_v)), G as in ET.2b/affine-springer-fibre and a ∈ 𝔠(𝒪_v) ∩ 𝔠^rs(F_v), with J_a, J′_a ⊆ J_a the open subgroup of ET.2b/regular-centralizer and κ a character of π_0(P_v(J′_a)) induced from a global κ. Then the number of k(v)-points of the quotient groupoid [M_v(a)/P_v(J′_a)], each point weighted by κ of its invariant and divided by the order of its automorphism group, equals vol(J′_a(𝒪_v), dt_v)·O^κ_a(1_{𝔤(𝒪_v)}, dt_v), where O^κ is the κ-orbital integral of ET.1/kappa-and-stable-orbital-integrals of the characteristic function of 𝔤(𝒪_v) over the stable class a with the measure dt_v on the centralizer torus; for κ = 1 the count is the stable orbital integral (Ngô Lemme 8.2.4, Propositions 8.2.5 and 8.2.7). Consequently the global κ-count of ET.2b/hitchin-point-count is a product of local κ-orbital integrals of unit functions times explicit volumes.
hypotheses: k finite, char(k) ∤ |W|
a integral and regular semisimple over F_v
proofSteps: Points of M_v(a) over k(v) are lattices g ∈ G(F_v)/G(𝒪_v) with Ad(g)⁻¹γ_a ∈ 𝔤(𝒪_v) (ET.2b/affine-springer-fibre); modulo P_v(J′_a)(k(v)) = J′_a(F_v)/J′_a(𝒪_v) they are the G(F_v)-conjugacy classes of elements of 𝔤(𝒪_v) in the stable class of γ_a with given invariant, weighted by the inverse volumes of their centralizers (Ngô §8.2, Lemme 8.2.4).

The κ-twist: the invariant of a rational class in the stable class is identified with the class in H^1(F_v, J_a) and κ is evaluated on it (ET.0/rational-classes-in-stable-class), giving the κ-weighted sum (Propositions 8.2.5, 8.2.7).
acceptance: If a is regular semisimple modulo ε_v (δ_v = 0), M_v(a)/P_v(J′_a) is a point with automorphism group of volume matching vol(J′_a(𝒪_v)), and O^κ_a(1) = 1.
For G = GL_n (κ = 1 only) the count is the classical lattice count expressing O_a(1_{𝔤𝔩_n(𝒪)}) as a number of 𝒪[γ_a]-stable lattices up to the centralizer.

sources.match: The κ-weighted number of k-points of [M_v(a)/P_v(J′_a)] is vol(J′_a(𝒪_v))·O^κ_a(1_{𝔤_v}), and its variant for P_v(J_a).

nodes.title: The fundamental lemma for unitary Lie algebras (Laumon–Ngô)
nodes.statement: Let F be a finite extension of 𝔽_p((t)) with residue field k, F′/F an unramified quadratic extension with residue characteristic ≠ 2, G = U(n) the unitary group of a hermitian form over F′/F with a hyperspecial model, and n = n_1 + n_2 a nontrivial partition with H = U(n_1) × U(n_2) the corresponding endoscopic group and κ the associated character. If char(k) > n, then for G-regular semisimple γ in the Lie algebra of H(F) with image in 𝔤(F), O^κ_γ = (−1)^r q^r SO^H_γ for the characteristic functions of the integral Lie algebras, with r = r_{I_1,I_2} the valuation of the resultant of the two characteristic polynomials (Laumon–Ngô Théorème 1.5.1); combined with Waldspurger's reductions this gives the fundamental lemma for unitary groups over p-adic fields when p is large, used by Shin and by Liu–Tian–Xiao–Zhang–Zhu.
hypotheses: F of equal characteristic p with char(k) > n
F′/F unramified quadratic, residue characteristic ≠ 2
proofSteps: Laumon–Ngô prove it by a G_m-equivariant localization on the Hitchin fibration for unitary groups (a special case subsumed by ET.3/lie-algebra-fundamental-lemma, whose hypothesis char(k) ∤ |W| = n! is the same as char(k) > n for U(n)).
Transfer to characteristic 0: ET.3/change-of-characteristic and ET.3/group-fundamental-lemma.
acceptance: n = 2, n_1 = n_2 = 1: H = U(1) × U(1) is a torus, SO^H_γ is a volume, and the identity is the unitary analogue of the SL_2 computation.
n_2 = 0 is excluded (nontrivial partition); for it the statement is the tautology O_γ = SO_γ for G.

sources.locator: Abstract and §0.1 (PDF pp. 1–2); §1.1 (PDF pp. 4–5); §1.5, Théorème 1.5.1 (PDF p. 10)
sources.match: The Langlands fundamental lemma for unitary groups over finite extensions of 𝔽_p((t)) with p > rank, for the unramified quadratic F′/F and H = U(n_1) × U(n_2); the identity O^κ_γ = (−1)^r q^r SO^H_γ.

Uses the fundamental lemma for unramified unitary groups: the characteristic function of a hyperspecial subgroup transfers to that of the endoscopic group (extraction item PAPER-LIU-ETAL-22/endoscopic-fundamental-lemma).

nodes.title: Waldspurger's non-standard fundamental lemma (Ngô)
nodes.statement: Let k be a finite field, 𝒪 = k[[ε]], F = k((ε)), and G_1, G_2 two semisimple simply connected quasi-split groups over 𝒪 with isogenous root data, i.e. a non-standard endoscopic triple (G_1, G_2, j_*) in Waldspurger's sense: an isomorphism j_* : X_{1,*} ⊗ ℚ → X_{2,*} ⊗ ℚ of rational cocharacter spaces, Galois-equivariant, sending each coroot of G_1 to a positive rational multiple of a coroot of G_2 and dually (the basic case G_1 = Sp(2n), G_2 = SO(2n + 1) or Spin(2n+1)), with the Weyl group order prime to char(k). Then for regular semisimple a_1 ∈ 𝔠_1(𝒪) and a_2 = j(a_1) ∈ 𝔠_2(𝒪) corresponding under the induced isomorphism of Chevalley quotients 𝔠_1 ≅ 𝔠_2 (over 𝒪 after the identification of 𝔱_1 and 𝔱_2 given by j_*), SO_{a_1}(1_{𝔤_1(𝒪)}) = SO_{a_2}(1_{𝔤_2(𝒪)}) (Ngô Théorème 2; Théorème 1.12.7 in equal characteristic). Its consumer in this roadmap is the twisted fundamental lemma (ET.3/twisted-fundamental-lemma-and-transfer), where non-standard triples arise from the descent of twisted endoscopy to centralizers; it is not needed for ordinary endoscopy or for cyclic base change.
hypotheses: equal characteristic, char(k) ∤ |W|
a non-standard endoscopic triple (G_1, G_2, j_*)
proofSteps: Ngô §8.8 (Théorème 8.8.2, p. 186): the anisotropic Hitchin fibrations of G_1 and G_2 have isomorphic bases and their stable perverse cohomologies have isomorphic semisimplifications (same support argument as ET.2b/endoscopic-comparison with κ = 1), and the point count gives the equality of stable orbital integrals (§8.8.7, p. 187).
Waldspurger's definition and reduction of the non-standard triples: Waldspurger 2008 §1.7 (pp. 13–15) and §3.6–3.7.
acceptance: For G_1 = G_2 and j_* the identity the statement is a tautology.
G_1 = Sp(2), G_2 = Spin(3) ≅ SL_2: the coroots are scaled by 2 and 1/2 and the identity is between stable orbital integrals of 𝔰𝔭_2 = 𝔰𝔩_2 and 𝔰𝔬_3 ≅ 𝔰𝔩_2 at matching elements.

sources.match: The non-standard fundamental lemma for groups with isogenous root data, proved in equal characteristic by the same geometric method.
Non-standard endoscopic triples, the constraints on those arising by descent from twisted endoscopy, and the statement of the non-standard fundamental lemma.

nodes.title: Change of characteristic for orbital integrals and the fundamental lemma
nodes.statement: Fix a finite field 𝔽_q of characteristic p and let CL_q be the set of nonarchimedean local fields with residue field 𝔽_q (of characteristic 0 or p). Fix the root datum of a connected reductive group with an action of the tame Galois group Θ ⋉ I (independent of F ∈ CL_q) and an endoscopic triple, both tamely ramified. Assume p is large relative to the rank of G (Waldspurger's standing hypothesis; this bound is separate from and in general stronger than p ∤ |W|). Then: (a) orbital integrals of the functions attached to Moy–Prasad lattices (the space S of the source) depend on F only through 𝔽_q: there are linear forms J^D(z, δ, ·) on S, indexed by F-independent replacements z of stable classes and cohomological data δ, with J_{G^D}(X, rea_F(φ)) = J^D(z, δ, φ) for every F ∈ CL_q (Théorème 7.2); (b) if rea_{H,F}(φ_H) is a transfer of rea_F(φ) for one F ∈ CL_q, then rea_{H,F′}(φ_H) is a transfer of rea_{F′}(φ) for every F′ ∈ CL_q (Corollaire 9.2); (c) in the unramified case, the Lie-algebra fundamental lemma holds over F if and only if it holds over F′ (Corollaire 9.3). Combined with ET.3/lie-algebra-fundamental-lemma, the Lie-algebra fundamental lemma holds for unramified data over every p-adic field of characteristic 0 whose residue characteristic p is large relative to G.
hypotheses: p large relative to the rank of G (Waldspurger's hypothesis)
G and the endoscopic datum tamely ramified (unramified for (c))
proofSteps: Translate stable classes, Moy–Prasad lattices and the tame Galois group into F-independent data (Waldspurger 2006, Introduction and §§1–6), using DeBacker's parametrization of nilpotent orbits and homogeneity of germs (ET.1/shalika-germs).
(a) Théorème 7.2 (p. 62); (b) Corollaire 9.2 (p. 70); (c) Corollaire 9.3 (p. 71), applying (b) to the unit functions of the hyperspecial lattices.
Close local fields (Deligne, Kazhdan) are the classical form of the same principle; the source's route is the F-independent description above.
acceptance: For G = T a torus the forms J^D are evaluations and the statements are trivial.
For G = SL_2 and its elliptic torus data, the κ-orbital integrals of the unit function computed over 𝔽_q((t)) and over the unramified extension of ℚ_p of residue field 𝔽_q agree for p large.

sources.match: Under the hypothesis that the residue characteristic is large relative to the rank, orbital integrals of Moy–Prasad lattice functions are independent of the local field with given residue field; transfer and the Lie-algebra fundamental lemma transfer between fields of characteristic 0 and p with the same residue field.
Ngô proves the equal-characteristic case and notes that the mixed-characteristic case follows from Waldspurger's change of characteristic.

nodes.title: The fundamental lemma for groups and for spherical Hecke algebras
nodes.statement: Let F be a p-adic field of characteristic 0, G a connected reductive group over F, unramified with hyperspecial subgroup K = G(𝒪), (H, ℋ, s, ξ) an unramified endoscopic datum with z-pair, hyperspecial K_H ⊆ H(F), and Δ_0 the unramified normalization of the transfer factor (ET.1/local-transfer-factor, normalized as in Hales and Waldspurger). If p is large relative to G (Waldspurger's hypotheses of 2008 §4.4), then: (a) (unit elements) the characteristic function 1_{K_H}, suitably normalized for the z-pair and Haar measures giving K and K_H volume 1, is a transfer of 1_K: SO_{γ_H}(1_{K_H}) = Σ_δ Δ_0(γ_H, δ) O_δ(1_K) for every strongly G-regular γ_H; (b) (spherical Hecke algebra) for every f in the spherical Hecke algebra ℋ(G(F), K), the function b(f) ∈ ℋ(H(F), K_H) obtained from the L-embedding ξ through the Satake isomorphisms is a transfer of f. (a) follows from the Lie-algebra fundamental lemmas for the descended data of all semisimple centralizers (ET.3/change-of-characteristic and ET.3/lie-algebra-fundamental-lemma) by semisimple descent (Waldspurger 2008 Théorème 4.11 specialised to θ = 1, where the non-standard triples are trivial); (b) follows from (a) by Hales' reduction to unit elements.
hypotheses: F p-adic of characteristic 0, residue characteristic p large relative to G
G, H unramified with hyperspecial subgroups; unramified endoscopic datum
proofSteps: (a) Waldspurger 2008 §§4.4–4.11 and §5 with θ = 1 and ω = 1: descent of stable and κ-orbital integrals of the unit function to centralizers of topologically semisimple elements (§§5.2–5.8), equality of unramified transfer factors after descent (§§5.10–5.11), and the Lie-algebra fundamental lemma for each descended datum.
(b) Hales, 'On the fundamental lemma for standard endoscopy: reduction to unit elements', Canad. J. Math. 47 (1995) (not read; recalled by Hales 2003 Remark 9.3 and by Shin §3.4, p. 15).
Satake isomorphism and the map b: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.4/satake-isomorphism (with its unitary normalizations) and ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.5 (dual groups).
acceptance: For H = G (s = 1), b is the identity and (a)–(b) are tautologies.
For G = GL_n there is no proper elliptic datum and the statement reduces to (a) for H = G.

The proof uses Waldspurger's bound on the residue characteristic (2008 §4.4, (H1), and the change of characteristic); the hypothesis p ∤ |W| of the equal-characteristic theorem does not by itself give the statement over p-adic fields.

sources.match: Under the unramified hypotheses of §4.4, the Lie-algebra fundamental lemma for the descended data (and the non-standard one, trivial when θ = 1) implies the fundamental lemma for unit elements of the group.
The statement for unit elements of hyperspecial Hecke algebras and the known passage from the unit element to the whole spherical Hecke algebra.
The transfer and the fundamental lemma for unit elements are known in all cases (Waldspurger, Laumon–Ngô, Ngô), with Hales' reduction to unit elements.

uses.how: finite-place test functions in the stable trace formula are spherical functions and their transfers
hyperspecial transfer at unramified places

nodes.title: Existence of smooth transfer (Waldspurger)
nodes.statement: Let F be a local field of characteristic 0, G connected reductive over F, (H, ℋ, s, ξ) an endoscopic datum with z-pair (H_1, λ_1) and Δ an absolute transfer factor. Then every f ∈ C_c^∞(G(F)) has a transfer f^{H_1} ∈ C_1^∞(H_1(F)) (ET.1/matching-functions). At archimedean F this is Shelstad's theorem (ET.1/real-transfer). For F p-adic, Waldspurger proved that the Lie-algebra fundamental lemma for unramified data over all p-adic fields of sufficiently large residue characteristic implies Lie-algebra transfer for every p-adic F of characteristic 0 (through a global argument with an auxiliary place, the compatibility of transfer with Fourier transform and the germ expansion, which remove any restriction on the residue characteristic of F itself), and the group transfer follows by semisimple descent and the local gluing lemma; with ET.3/group-fundamental-lemma (unconditional by Ngô and Waldspurger) transfer is unconditional. In particular transfer exists between a connected reductive group and its quasi-split inner form (Waldspurger 1997, Corollaire 1.7).
hypotheses: F local of characteristic 0 (any residue characteristic)
an endoscopic datum with z-pair
proofSteps: Lie algebra: Waldspurger 1997 (not read; its main theorem and Corollary 1.7 are recalled by Labesse §3.3 and Shin §3.4): the Fourier-transform compatibility (ET.1/fourier-transform-orbital-integrals), homogeneity of germs (ET.1/shalika-germs), and a global argument choosing a number field and an auxiliary place where the fundamental lemma holds for large residue characteristic (ET.3/change-of-characteristic).

Group: descend near each semisimple element to the Lie algebra of its centralizer (ET.1/transfer-factor-properties (e)) and glue local transfers by Waldspurger 2008 §2.2 (lemma after Langlands–Shelstad 2.2.A).
Archimedean: ET.1/real-transfer.
acceptance: For the principal datum of quasi-split G the identity function transfer is valid.
For SL_2 and the elliptic torus data, transfer exists for every f, matching κ-orbital integrals with orbital integrals on the torus times transfer factors.

sources.match: Waldspurger's difficult result that transfer between a connected reductive group and its quasi-split inner form is possible (his Corollary 1.7).
The transfer conjecture of Langlands–Shelstad is known, via Waldspurger and Ngô, for all endoscopic data.
The local gluing lemma for transfer (after Langlands–Shelstad Lemma 2.2.A) and descent to Lie algebras.

Statement of the Langlands–Shelstad transfer conjecture and its reduction to the fundamental lemma by Waldspurger; written in 2005, it records the nonarchimedean conjecture as open and reduces its unramified case to the fundamental lemma (p. 203).

nodes.title: Transfer between inner forms of GL_n and quaternionic matching
nodes.statement: Let F be a local field of characteristic 0, D a central division algebra of degree d over F, n = md and G = GL_m(D), an inner form of G* = GL_n(F) with Kottwitz sign e(G) = (−1)^{n−m}. Regular semisimple γ ∈ G(F) and γ* ∈ G*(F) correspond if they have the same characteristic polynomial (then their centralizers are isomorphic tori); measures on the centralizers are transported. (a) (Deligne–Kazhdan–Vignéras) For every f ∈ C_c^∞(G(F)) there is f* ∈ C_c^∞(G*(F)) with O_{γ*}(f*) = e(G) O_γ(f) when γ* corresponds to γ, and O_{γ*}(f*) = 0 when γ* corresponds to no element of G(F); (b) there is a canonical injection π ↦ π* from tempered irreducible representations of G(F) to those of G*(F) with tr π*(f*) = e(G) tr π(f) (the local Jacquet–Langlands correspondence on characters). For GL_2 and the quaternion algebra D: e(D^×) = −1, the regular semisimple elements of D^× correspond to elliptic elements of GL_2(F), and the matching f ↦ f* uses the common elliptic torus measure; for an unramified place where D splits, the unit element of GL_2(𝒪) corresponds to itself. This is the case s = 1 of ET.3/local-transfer-existence for inner forms, with the transfer factor equal to e(G) on corresponding pairs.
hypotheses: F local of characteristic 0
G = GL_m(D) an inner form of GL_n
proofSteps: (a)–(b) Deligne–Kazhdan–Vignéras (not read), as stated by Arthur's Clay introduction Theorem 25.1 (p. 168), proved by a simple trace formula argument.

Transfer factor: for the principal datum of GL_n (s = 1) and an inner form, Δ = e(G) on corresponding pairs (stable = rational conjugacy in GL_m(D) by Hilbert 90 for the centralizer tori), compatible with ET.1/local-transfer-factor and ET.0/kottwitz-sign.
acceptance: GL_2 and D^×: e = −1, and for f the characteristic function of 𝒪_D^× a matching f* satisfies O_{γ*}(f*) = −O_γ(f) at every elliptic γ* corresponding to γ ∈ D^× and O_{γ*}(f*) = 0 at split regular γ*.
m = n (D = F): G = G*, e = 1 and f* = f.

sources.match: For an inner form G of GL(n) and any test function f_v, the function f*_v defined by matching orbital integrals with the sign e(G_v) is the orbital-integral image of a function on G*(F_v); a canonical injection of tempered representations with f*_v(π*_v) = e(G_v) f_{v,G}(π_v) (Deligne–Kazhdan–Vignéras).

uses.how: quaternionic matching with the rank-two sign and common torus measures
the local Jacquet–Langlands correspondence on characters

nodes.title: Stable base change: fundamental lemma, transfer and identity terms
nodes.statement: Let E/F be a cyclic extension of local fields of characteristic 0 of degree ℓ with generator θ of Gal(E/F), G_0 a connected reductive group over F, G = R_{E/F}G_0 with the automorphism θ, and H the quasi-split inner form of G_0 (cyclic stable base change, the twisted datum with s = 1 and ω = 1). (a) (Unit elements; Kottwitz) If E/F is unramified, G_0 is unramified and K_E = G_0(𝒪_E), K = G_0(𝒪_F) are hyperspecial with volume 1, then 1_{K_E} and 1_K have matching (twisted stable / stable) orbital integrals: SO_γ(1_K) = SO^θ_δ(1_{K_E}) when γ is a norm of δ, and SO_γ(1_K) = 0 when γ is not a norm. (b) (Spherical Hecke algebra; Clozel, Labesse) More generally, for every f_E ∈ ℋ(G_0(E), K_E) and its base-change image b_{E/F}(f_E) ∈ ℋ(G_0(F), K), the functions f_E and b_{E/F}(f_E) are associated (Labesse Proposition 3.7.3, with the vanishing at non-norms of Proposition 3.7.2). (c) (Transfer) For F nonarchimedean, every f_E ∈ C_c^∞(G_0(E)) has an associated f ∈ C_c^∞(H(F)) (Labesse Théorème 3.3.1, from Waldspurger's inner-form transfer and descent); for F archimedean, K-finite transfer exists (Labesse §3.5). (d) (Identity terms) If f_E and f are associated then ∫_{G_0(E)} f_E = ∫_{H(F)} f for compatible measures (Labesse Lemme 3.2.2). (e) Only the standard Lie-algebra fundamental lemma enters: in Waldspurger's twisted reduction the non-standard triples arising for base change are tautological (Waldspurger 2008, §§1.9 and 4.12 and the corollary for G_0 = U(n) or SL(n), using Laumon–Ngô). This is the finite-place twisted input of the simple twisted unitary trace formula.
hypotheses: E/F cyclic, characteristic 0
for (a)–(b): E/F unramified, G_0 unramified with hyperspecial subgroups
proofSteps: (a) Kottwitz, 'Base change for unit elements of Hecke algebras' (1986): the norm correspondence γ ↔ δ induces a bijection between classes contributing to the two unit-function orbital integrals, with equal integrals (Theorem of §1, p. 243), for G_der simply connected and in general by an unramified z-extension (§4).

(b) Labesse Propositions 3.7.2–3.7.3 (pp. 91–92), citing Clozel and Labesse 1990 for the compatibility of stable orbital integrals with the norm on the whole Hecke algebra, and correcting the vanishing argument at non-norms (Remarque after 3.7.2).
(c) Labesse Théorème 3.3.1 (p. 78) and §3.5; (d) Lemme 3.2.2 (p. 76) via the Weyl integration formula.
(e) Waldspurger 2008 Introduction (base-change corollaries), §1.9 (p. 16) and §4.12 (p. 53).
acceptance: G_0 = GL_1: the norm map E^× → F^× and the statement that 1_{𝒪_E^×} and 1_{𝒪_F^×} match for E/F unramified (the norm maps 𝒪_E^× onto 𝒪_F^×).
G_0 = GL_n, unit elements: Kottwitz's earlier Lemma 8.8 already gives the matching (cited in his 1986 introduction).

sources.match: For unramified E/F the unit elements of the Hecke algebras of G(E) and G(F) have matching stable twisted and stable orbital integrals.

Equality of total integrals for associated functions; existence of base-change transfer at nonarchimedean places and K-finite transfer at archimedean places; the base-change fundamental lemma for the spherical Hecke algebra with the vanishing at non-norms.

In the base-change case the non-standard triples are tautological, so twisted transfer and the twisted fundamental lemma follow from the standard Lie-algebra statements; for G_0 = SL(n) or U(n) they hold by Laumon–Ngô.

nodes.title: The twisted fundamental lemma and twisted transfer
nodes.statement: Let F be a p-adic field of characteristic 0, (G, θ, ω) a twisted triple with θ quasi-semisimple and (H, ℋ, s, ξ) a twisted endoscopic datum with z-pair (ET.0/endoscopic-datum, ET.0/z-pair), with the corrected twisted transfer factors of ET.1/twisted-transfer-factor. (a) (Waldspurger, Théorème 1.8) If, for all data obtained by descent to semisimple centralizers, Lie-algebra transfer holds for the ordinary data and non-standard transfer holds for the non-standard triples, then twisted transfer exists: every f ∈ C_c^∞(G(F)) has a twisted transfer to H_1. (b) (Waldspurger, Théorème 4.11) Under the unramified hypotheses (§4.4, residue characteristic large), if the Lie-algebra fundamental lemma holds for the descended ordinary data and the non-standard fundamental lemma holds for the non-standard triples, then the twisted fundamental lemma holds for unit elements. (c) The hypotheses of (a) and (b) are theorems: the ordinary Lie-algebra fundamental lemma and transfer (ET.3/lie-algebra-fundamental-lemma, ET.3/change-of-characteristic, ET.3/local-transfer-existence) and the non-standard fundamental lemma (ET.3/nonstandard-fundamental-lemma, with the change of characteristic for it); so twisted transfer and the twisted fundamental lemma for unit elements hold. (d) (Lemaire–Mœglin–Waldspurger) The twisted fundamental lemma for the whole spherical Hecke algebra reduces to the unit elements, hence holds. The twisted weighted fundamental lemma is not claimed here.
hypotheses: F p-adic of characteristic 0; for (b), (d): unramified data and residue characteristic large
the corrected twisted transfer factors
proofSteps: (a) Waldspurger 2008 §§2–3, Théorème 1.8 (proof §3.11, p. 41): descent of twisted orbital integrals near θ-semisimple elements to Lie algebras of twisted centralizers, decomposition of stable classes (§3.8) and equality of transfer factors (§3.9).
(b) Waldspurger 2008 §§4–5, Théorème 4.11 (proof §5.12, p. 71).
(c) Combine with Ngô (Théorèmes 1 and 2) and Waldspurger's change of characteristic.

(d) Lemaire–Mœglin–Waldspurger, 'Le lemme fondamental pour l'endoscopie tordue : réduction aux éléments unités', arXiv:1506.03383 (Ann. Sci. ÉNS 51 (2018)); not read; recorded through its abstract and the red-team finding RT-AREA-langlands-1/13.
acceptance: For θ = 1 (ordinary endoscopy) the non-standard triples are tautological and (b) is ET.3/group-fundamental-lemma (a).
For G = GL_{2n+1} with θ the transpose-inverse and H = Sp(2n), descent produces the non-standard triple (Sp(2m), SO(2m+1)), so the non-standard fundamental lemma is genuinely used.

sources.match: Théorème 1.8: Lie-algebra transfer and non-standard transfer imply twisted transfer; Théorème 4.11: the Lie-algebra fundamental lemma and the non-standard fundamental lemma imply the twisted fundamental lemma for unit elements.
The non-standard fundamental lemma, which together with the ordinary one gives Waldspurger's twisted fundamental lemma.

uses.how: the twisted fundamental lemma and twisted transfer as inputs of the stabilization behind Arthur's classification (the twisted weighted fundamental lemma is not supplied)
the twisted fundamental lemma is proved, so ET.5's description of it as unproved must be corrected

nodes.title: The fundamental lemma at almost all places of a global datum
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field, G a connected reductive group over F and (H, ℋ, s, ξ) a global endoscopic datum with z-pair, and S a finite set of places containing the archimedean places and the places where G, H or the datum ramify. Then there is a finite set S′ ⊇ S, depending only on G and H (the places of residue characteristic below Waldspurger's bound), such that for every v ∉ S′ the unit element 1_{K_{H,v}} is a transfer of 1_{K_v} with the unramified transfer factors and the spherical Hecke algebras match through b_v (ET.3/group-fundamental-lemma), and similarly for the twisted and base-change data (ET.3/twisted-fundamental-lemma-and-transfer, ET.3/base-change-fundamental-lemma-and-transfer). The global transfer factors are the products of these local ones (ET.1/transfer-factor-properties (f)). In global applications an auxiliary place where G is split may be chosen outside any finite set by Chebotarev's density theorem (upstream Chebotarev roadmap); no statement at the finitely many places of S′ \ S follows from the equal-characteristic theorem by renaming the field.
hypotheses: F a number field
a global unramified-outside-S endoscopic datum
proofSteps: Apply ET.3/group-fundamental-lemma at each v ∉ S′; the bound on residue characteristics is uniform in v because it depends only on the root data of G and H.
Chebotarev for the auxiliary split place: upstream Chebotarev Layer 10.
acceptance: For G = GL_n and H = G, S′ = S and the statement is trivial.
For unitary similitude groups G_{n⃗} over ℚ attached to a CM field, S′ is finite and contains the primes ramified in the CM field and the primes below Waldspurger's bound.

sources.match: In the global setting the transfer and the fundamental lemma for unit elements are used at all finite places outside a finite set.
The unramified hypotheses, including the bound on the residue characteristic, under which the fundamental lemma is stated.

requests.need: For a smooth projective curve X over 𝔽_q, a smooth affine group scheme G over X and a line bundle D: (i) for a G-torsor E on X × S, the stack over Bun_G of sections φ ∈ H^0(X × S, ad(E) ⊗ D) (an abelian cone of a coherent sheaf) is algebraic and locally of finite type; (ii) for a smooth commutative group scheme J over X × S, the Picard stack of J-torsors is algebraic and smooth when H^2 vanishes; (iii) the criterion that an algebraic stack of finite type with finite unramified inertia is Deligne–Mumford. These are the stack inputs of the Hitchin moduli stack, its Picard action and the anisotropic DM statement.

The Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula over 𝔽_q with Q̄_ℓ coefficients for separated schemes of finite type and its extension to separated Deligne–Mumford stacks of finite type (counting points weighted by 1/#Aut), with compact supports; used to count points of anisotropic Hitchin fibres.

The decomposition theorem (BBD 5.4.5) and relative hard Lefschetz for a proper morphism f : M → S from a smooth separated Deligne–Mumford stack of finite type over 𝔽_q to a scheme (in Ngô's application M^ani → A^ani, with M^ani a global quotient by a finite-stabilizer action), stated so that EDC.7/decomposition-theorem and EDC.7/relative-hard-lefschetz-theorem, now stated for schemes, apply; Ngô (Remarque 7.5.1) records that the argument carries over. Also the Chebotarev-type principle: two mixed perverse sheaves on a scheme X_0 of finite type over 𝔽_q whose Frobenius trace functions agree at all closed points of X_0 (and its finite extensions) have isomorphic semisimplifications.

Only the geometric prefix of GS.1, without Satake: the fibre of the Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian at a closed point v of X is the affine Grassmannian Gr_v = G(F_v)/G(𝒪_v) as an ind-projective ind-scheme over k(v), with its G(𝒪_v)-action and the closed sub-ind-schemes cut out by integrality conditions; ET.2b builds affine Springer fibres inside it (red-team finding RT-AREA-langlands-1/12).

The unweighted invariant orbital integral of a semisimple element of a connected reductive group over a local field of characteristic 0 (or a finite product of such): the quotient measure on G_γ^0\G, convergence, invariance, linearity in the measures and the full-centralizer factor [G_γ : G_γ^0] (target AS.6.8a of the AutomorphicSpectralTheory package); and, for real groups, the Clozel–Delorme pseudo-coefficients of discrete series and the Euler–Poincaré test functions with tr π(f_ξ) = Σ_i (−1)^i dim H^i(𝔤, K; π ⊗ ξ) for every finite-length π (targets AS.6.16a–AS.6.17). Add the stage edges GS.0 → ET.2b, GS.1 → ET.2b and FA.2 → ET.3, and narrow the ET.2b text to 'import Bun_G and the affine Grassmannian; construct the Higgs, Hitchin, Picard, affine Springer and support geometry'.

restructure.detail: Corrections to the roadmap text that this plan cannot make itself: (1) ET.3 states that Ngô's published Lie-algebra theorem needs p > 2h, while the version read assumes p ∤ |W|; (2) ET.5 (part 2) calls the general twisted fundamental lemma unproved, while Waldspurger (Théorèmes 1.8, 4.11) with Ngô's non-standard fundamental lemma proves it for unit elements and Lemaire–Mœglin–Waldspurger for the spherical Hecke algebra (red-team finding RT-AREA-langlands-1/13).
restructure.proposal: In ET.3 state the hypotheses as 'p ∤ |W| for the equal-characteristic Lie-algebra theorem (as in the version read; confirm against the published version), and p large relative to G for Waldspurger's change of characteristic and descent'. In ET.5 replace the sentence by 'the route does not need the twisted fundamental lemma; it is proved (ET.3/twisted-fundamental-lemma-and-transfer)'.

restructure.detail: RT-AREA-automorphic-1/24 made ET.1 the single owner of unweighted orbital integrals and AS.6 their consumer. The upstream order puts AutomorphicSpectralTheory in tier 13 and this roadmap in tier 14, so the AutomorphicSpectralTheory package planned the invariant orbital integral (AS.6.8a), the discrete functionals and pseudo-coefficients (AS.6.16a) and the real Euler–Poincaré test functions (AS.6.17) itself and asked this roadmap to import them (PKG-AutomorphicSpectralTheory handoff, "Upward citations"). The promoted AutomorphicSpectralTheory packet still requests them from ET.1.
restructure.proposal: Owners: the group orbital integral, its quotient measure and convergence, pseudo-coefficients and the Euler–Poincaré trace identity → AutomorphicSpectralTheory:AS.6 (formerly ET.1); Waldspurger's normalization, transport of centralizer measures, Lie-algebra and nilpotent orbital integrals, semisimple descent, packet averages of pseudo-coefficients with their orbital integrals, and the inner-form and twisted versions → ET.1. Retarget the AutomorphicSpectralTheory packet's requests 12 and 13 (to ET.1) as self-supplied when its package corrections are carried into the packet, and draw the edge AS.6 → ET.1.

redTeamFindings.handling: ET.1/orbital-integral was planned as the single owner of invariant (unweighted) orbital integrals, as the finding asked. Under the upstream tier order (research/blueprint/upstream/CaraianiNewton.md: AutomorphicSpectralTheory tier 13, this roadmap tier 14) the AutomorphicSpectralTheory package then moved the group orbital integral and the real pseudo-coefficients below this roadmap (its targets AS.6.8a and AS.6.16a–AS.6.17; PKG-AutomorphicSpectralTheory handoff). ET.1 now imports them from AS.6 (request recorded) and keeps the conventions, the Lie-algebra and nilpotent orbital integrals, semisimple descent, the packet averages and the inner-form and twisted versions. Each piece still has a single owner. The promoted AS packet still requests the unweighted integral and the Euler–Poincaré carriers from ET.1 (AS.6/weighted-orbital-integral, AS.6/general-euler-poincare); those requests lapse when the AS package's plan corrections are carried into the AS packet (restructure proposal).

ET.2b imports Bun_G from GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands:GS.0/bun-g-of-the-global-curve and the affine Grassmannian as the fibre of GS.1/beilinson-drinfeld-grassmannian (geometric prefix only, request recorded); ET.3's globalization imports function-field adeles from FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.2/projective-adeles. ET.2b constructs only the Higgs/Hitchin, cameral, Picard, affine-Springer, δ-stratification and support geometry. Owner pair recorded in restructure: Bun_G owned by GS.0 (formerly also described by ET.2b).

ET.3 plans the twisted fundamental lemma and twisted transfer as the consumer of the non-standard fundamental lemma (ET.3/twisted-fundamental-lemma-and-transfer, after Waldspurger 2008 Théorèmes 1.8 and 4.11 and Lemaire–Mœglin–Waldspurger for the spherical Hecke algebra); its consumer is ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions:ML.4. ET.4's cyclic base change uses ET.3/base-change-fundamental-lemma-and-transfer, which needs only the standard fundamental lemma (Waldspurger 2008 §§1.9, 4.12: the non-standard triples are tautological for base change). ET.5's sentence calling the twisted fundamental lemma unproved belongs to part 2 and is flagged in restructure for correction.

Kottwitz–Shelstad 2012 is a source of ET.1/local-transfer-factor and ET.1/twisted-transfer-factor: both corrected normalizations Δ′ (classical) and Δ_D (renormalized), the new twisted term Δ_I^new and the Whittaker-normalized factors are planned, each consumer records its convention, and the GL_{2n+1} transpose-inverse case is a unit test where the conventions differ.

z-extensions are imported from ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.1/z-extension and RG2.1/z-extension-existence (now owned there); ET.0 defines only z-pairs (ET.0/z-pair) and integral z-extensions for unramified groups (ET.0/unramified-local-cohomology (b)). Kaletha's z-embeddings are not needed by ET.0–ET.3 and are not planned here.

suggestedPolicy: The suggested Lean file research/blueprint/suggested/EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison--ET.0.lean has the compact shape of PACKAGE_REVIEW.md ('Shape of a roadmap'): real-bodied light definitions over carriers that exist at the pinned Mathlib (nonabelian H^1 of a group acting on a group, crossed modules, kappa-weighted sums over finite abelian groups, the Kottwitz sign, the GL_n Chevalley map and Kostant section, the GL_n regular centralizer, lattices and affine Springer fibres for GL_n) with statable milestones and examples. Reductive groups over local fields, their Galois cohomology, endoscopic data, transfer factors, orbital integrals, the Hitchin fibration and the fundamental lemma have no carriers at the pins and are targets of the document only; the API names of those nodes are recorded in the packet and the reader. Elaborated with lean-check (Mathlib 082e2d3): no errors; the only warnings mark statements left unproved.

review.notes: Independent review of the complete pass over ET.0–ET.3 (61 nodes; ET.2, ET.2a and its sub-layers closed by RS-19). All 24 sources were fetched at the URLs given (every SHA-256 matches the packet) and every node locator was read; the two Math. Ann. scans (Langlands–Shelstad 1987, Kottwitz 1986) were read through GDZ OCR and page images. All 7 Mathlib baseline declarations were confirmed at 082e2d3 (name, module, kind, statement). External node prerequisites (46 ids in 12 roadmaps) exist and say what the citing nodes use; requests reconcile with prerequisites in both directions; the packet induces no new stage cycle. 29 nodes were corrected in place, among them five false or misstated results: crossed-module cohomology item (5) (false as stated: the counterexample of the confirmed erratum PAPER-KISIN-17/E41 satisfies "ker ∂ central, coker ∂ abelian"; restated for braided crossed modules); Kottwitz's 𝔎(T/F) (only the classes with trivial image in H^1(F, Z(Ĝ)), §4.6); the Euler–Poincaré orbital integrals (sign (−1)^{q(G_γ)}, not (−1)^{q(G)}, and O_γ rather than SO_γ); the standard-endoscopy conventions of Kottwitz–Shelstad 2012 §5.1 (the twisted formulas had been transplanted); the smoothness of the Hitchin stack (only over A^♥, Ngô Théorème 4.12.1). Further corrections: H^1(𝔸_F/F, ·) is Kottwitz's and Labesse's quotient cohomology, not a cokernel; van Hoften's G(ℝ)_+; Kottwitz §6's standing hypothesis G_der simply connected; the classes in a regular stable class (ker[H^1(K, J_a) → H^1(K, G)]); J_a by the cameral cover only over 𝔠^rs; Shalika germs (Γ_0 constant, Γ_reg ∝ |D|^{−1/2} on elliptic Cartans of 𝔤𝔩_2); Shin's block-diagonal Φ_{n⃗}; the Lie-algebra transfer factor's base-point constant; twelve locators and the LTXZZ page offset. Duplication: Kneser's theorem is AdelicAlgebraicGroups:AA.4/kneser-local-torsor and is now imported; under the upstream tier order the AutomorphicSpectralTheory package (tier 13) moved the group orbital integral and the real pseudo-coefficients below this roadmap (AS.6.8a, AS.6.16a–AS.6.17), so ET.1 now imports them from AS.6 (request and restructure proposal added; RT-AREA-automorphic-1/24 handling updated). A circular dependency (ET.0/kottwitz-duality ↔ ET.0/abelianization-theorems) was removed. The handed red-team findings RT-AREA-automorphic-1/24, RT-AREA-langlands-1/12, /13, /14 and RT-AREA-geomlanglands/10 are handled in the packet and the document. Source issue E1 confirmed. Unit tests added for crossed modules without braiding, the Euler–Poincaré sign on SL_2(ℝ) and the convention for G(ℝ)_+. The suggested file elaborates with lean-check (Mathlib 082e2d3) with no errors, its only warnings marking unproved statements; one side-condition proof now has a real proof. The reader document was brought in line with every correction. Open for the package: GlobalShtukas (GS.0, GS.1) and FunctionFieldArithmetic (FA.2) are outside the 94 roadmaps of the upstream order and must be moved down or replaced when this roadmap is packaged; the promoted AutomorphicSpectralTheory packet still requests from ET.1 what its package now plans.
